title: Require application readback before tracked paired trial counts as passed
description: The tracked artifact validator currently accepts status=passed without requiring execution.decisionApplicationObservation=observed. Existing test 'accepts a passed artifact...' passes a recorder that returns [] (none_observed) and still expects passed. That weakens the quality gate: a future aggregate could count a checker pass without exact persisted decision application.
design: Tighten the public artifact quality seam: a passed tracked artifact must carry observed application readback, while invalid/blocked/unverified remain explicit. Update the focused test to prove none_observed cannot validate passed and preserve the replay/phase/hash invariants. Do not infer application from checker status or add operator/executor behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Add one focused falsifier at verifyTrackedTrialArtifact/runner seam; valid passed artifacts require observed application readback and stale/none/persistence_failed artifacts are excluded by aggregation. Run the paired-live focused suite and record non-proofs.

close_reason: Implemented application-proof gate. executeComparableTrial now returns unverified with explicit reason when the recorder observes zero applications; isPassedTrialArtifact additionally requires execution.decisionApplicationObservation=observed. Updated tracked runner test to use an observed application for the passed case and added a none_observed falsifier proving unverified status. Verification: 4 paired-live test files, 86 tests passed; @krn/cli typecheck passed; git diff --check passed. Non-proof: this does not prove application usefulness or causal attribution.

title: Atomically upgrade legacy helped memory through the reviewed authority gate
description:
## What To Build
Add one store-backed reconciliation seam that consumes an authority-bound reviewed-helped MemoryCandidate plus its legacy active MemoryRecord predecessor, validates the same source/review gate used by normal promotion, and atomically accepts the candidate, creates the replacement MemoryRecord, and supersedes the legacy record. Expose only the minimum operator CLI needed to preview and persist this exact reconciliation. Do not infer first-class authority IDs from legacy metadata and do not delete history.

## Consumer
The local KRN dogfood operator and subsequent DecisionPacket activation need exactly one active governed memory for a helped application after the authority-schema cutover. The currently observed pair is legacy candidate f5640319-b4ea-4f7d-a6a9-3ef4d9910baf / active record 0d73e037-058a-4ba5-bdb3-f65606e94d90 and authority-bound candidate 8f937cdd-0982-4fd4-869f-9b08a3874890.

## Acceptance Criteria
The public seam fails closed unless the candidate is proposed, first-class review/application bindings are present, reviewed source claims pass the existing MemoryReviewGate, and the predecessor is active in the same project. One DB transaction leaves the candidate accepted, exactly one replacement record active, the predecessor superseded with explicit reason/time, immutable version lineage preserved, and retry idempotent. CLI preview performs no writes and names non-proof. A real PostgreSQL test covers success, mismatch rejection, rollback on failure, retry, and next active selection. The observed local pair is reconciled only after the implementation gates pass.

## Falsifier
A failed transaction leaves two active records or a partially accepted candidate; a mismatched project/source/application can be reconciled; retry creates another record/version; or active selection still returns legacy truth.

## Proof / Non-Proof
Proof: focused repository/CLI tests against PostgreSQL, narrow package typechecks, migration/schema check if schema changes, selected KRN gates, independent fixed-point review, and exact before/after local store readback.
Non-proof: metadata similarity, direct SQL cleanup, a green typecheck, or candidate promotion without atomic predecessor supersession.

## Native Dependency Edges
Discovered from mise-en-palace-bkwd and enabled by completed mise-en-palace-bkwd.14. No open blocker.

## Rollback / Contraction
Keep the legacy record active and the new candidate proposed if any authority check fails. The implementation may be contracted to a repository-only seam if a CLI adds no direct operator value.

## Open Questions
None; existing MemoryReviewGate and applyReviewedMemoryRevision policy are the starting seams, but the implementation must remove any bypass rather than compose two non-atomic mutations.

## Required Skills
implement,typescript-engineering,krn-memory-core
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed authority-bound candidate atomically replaces and supersedes its same-project legacy record, fails closed on mismatches, is idempotent, is exposed through a bounded operator path, and is proven against the observed local conflict without deleting history.
notes: Implemented, independently reviewed, dogfooded on PostgreSQL, committed and pushed in 0d842a30

title: Make reviewed helped consolidation store-validated and fail closed
description: The .5 proof required an operator to assemble an exact accepted review, helped FeedbackDelta, usefulness application, SourceDecision, SourceClaim, and candidate evidence refs. Today the krn memory candidate add command accepts those identities as caller-supplied strings and MemoryReviewGate checks candidate shape/source lineage but does not prove that the cited ReviewAssessment is accepted, that it assesses the same EvidenceBundle, or that the cited FeedbackDelta contains one exact application-bound helped outcome for the proposed SourceDecision. A caller can therefore create a reviewable candidate from used or fabricated refs even though the governed manual path behaved correctly.
design: Consumer: positive learning consolidation between reviewed evidence and MemoryCandidate. Add one public store-backed proposal seam that takes the authoritative FeedbackDelta outcome plus accepted ReviewAssessment identity and derives the candidate; callers do not restate outcome authority in metadata. Validate one project/run chain: accepted ReviewAssessment -> same EvidenceBundle as the evidence-feedback chain -> FeedbackDelta with current admitted exact source usefulness outcome=helped -> canonical usefulness_application subject=source_decision and exact SourceDecision -> accepted SourceClaim/support -> candidate-only write. Preserve MemoryReviewGate as the separate promotion owner; never create MemoryRecord automatically. Used/selected/neutral/hurt/unknown, pending/rejected review, identity mismatch, missing application, foreign project, duplicate ambiguity, or forged refs fail closed before writes. Idempotency must prevent duplicate candidates for the same reviewed helped application. Rollback: disable the proposal seam while preserving existing reviewed records; do not weaken the promotion gate. Non-proof: store validation proves eligibility and identity, not future causal usefulness or broad retrieval quality.
acceptance_criteria: A focused red-capable public-seam falsifier demonstrates that caller-supplied strings can no longer stand in for reviewed helped authority; exactly one subject-bound later-verified helped SourceDecision with an accepted same-EvidenceBundle review produces one MemoryCandidate and no MemoryRecord; used subjects from f644, non-accepted review, wrong evidence bundle/project/run/application/subject, missing canonical application, and retry/duplicate races produce zero extra candidates and explicit reasons; the candidate carries derived run, FeedbackDelta, SourceDecision, SourceClaim, application, packet, review and does-not-prove provenance; existing generic source-decision seeding remains semantically distinct; a real PostgreSQL proof uses the f644 chain or an isolated equivalent and shows the next MemoryReviewGate/selection path remains intact; focused tests, narrow typechecks, independent review, Fallow when applicable, publication, and exact-head CI pass.
notes: Implemented one atomic store-backed candidate-only reviewed-helped proposal seam and CLI command. Authority chain now requires all evidence_feedback_v1 channels, admitted current packet binding on feedback and bundle, exact packet checksum/evidence ref/generatedAt/lifecycle, canonical application project/run/task/subject/appliedAt, accepted same-bundle exact-subject review metadata, adopted SourceDecision, accepted SourceClaim and decision-grade edge. Candidate validFrom derives from canonical application; idempotency compares complete immutable shape and only accepts a complete MemoryReviewGate-owned post-promotion metadata shape. Migration adds typed review/application refs, unique application identity, and RESTRICT lineage FKs without legacy metadata backfill. Isolated real-PostgreSQL test proves success, used/missing/wrong authority rejection, channel/bundle/project/packet/review/application mismatch, two-connection race, canonical conflict, FK retention, candidate-only persistence, real MemoryReviewGate promotion, post-promotion retry, and active selection. Local f644 command created candidate 8f937cdd then returned it idempotently; used-only remains rejected. Focused CLI tests 11/11, focused DB 12/12, DB package 201/201, root typecheck, migration generate/check/readiness, Fallow and diff check green. Independent final Standards/Spec review clean. Non-proof: one governed fixture and f644 replay do not prove broad future retrieval quality, arbitrary-task causality, or product readiness.
close_reason: Implemented and merged as PR #22 (2c16099d): reviewed helped-learning candidate proposal now validates the complete persisted feedback/review/evidence/application/source authority chain atomically and fails closed; candidate remains gated before MemoryRecord promotion. Local focused/full gates, independent review, and all four GitHub CI lanes passed.

title: Unify plan execution-brief readiness with the authoritative DecisionPacket

Two public readbacks therefore give contradictory execution authority for the same run.
design: Consumer: operator/Codex plan output and any automation deciding whether execution may proceed. Authority owner must be one current DecisionPacket readiness computation, not an independently inferred brief flag. Map plan compile result -> execution brief renderer and persisted run -> DecisionPacket read model; preserve true abstention and stale/inactive contract reasons. title: Bind paired post-application verification to the issued EvidenceContract
description: Fresh immutable passed run 876c41d2 persisted all three exact SourceDecision applications, but its differential unknown_first and finite_result_state outcomes were downgraded from helped to unknown. The recorder wraps executed checker commands as krn:post-application-* labels, while strict helped admission requires exact commands from the issued EvidenceContract; the controlled target also executes a typecheck fallback and commit-scoped diff command rather than the packet's generic strings. Consequently real later verification is present but cannot satisfy the command-identity authority boundary.
design: Consumer: source-usefulness return loop and later reviewed learning. Authority owner: issued EvidenceContract plus captured command-runner artifacts, not recorder labels. Invariant: helped requires exact, later, successful proof for every required verification role; presentation labels cannot replace or corrupt executed-command identity. Caller -> seam -> result: paired recorder -> evidence capture -> DB admission -> persisted helped readback. Non-proof: one controlled pair does not establish causal usefulness or arbitrary-repository portability.
acceptance_criteria: Define one honest identity between issued required verification and executed post-application evidence without claiming a command ran under a different string; exact application and target-state binding remain mandatory; missing, failed, pre-application, operator-reported, truncated, semantically different, or omitted required commands cannot prove helped; a focused public-seam falsifier admits only properly bound later verification; immutable run 876c41d2 remains unchanged; a subsequent fresh immutable run persists helped for every actually differential mapped subject and used for every nondifferential mapped subject; focused tests, typecheck, DB return-loop, review, Fallow, publication, and exact-head CI pass.

title: Authorize evidence usefulness against the persisted run project
description: Fresh exact win run 690e9677 persisted a bound-current feedback candidate containing three exact selected SourceDecision outcomes, but persisted zero usefulness_applications and the paired recorder returned unverified. Evidence capture derives the authoritative project from the persisted TaskContract for persistence, while DecisionPacket usefulness authorization is given the CLI fallback runtime project. For an explicitly scoped run these differ, so valid outcomes are silently excluded from application admission while remaining visible only as non-authoritative semantic-request metadata.
design: Consumer: paired DecisionPacket application recorder. Authority owner: persisted TaskContract project plus Postgres usefulness_applications. Invariant: all authorization and persisted identities for a run use one project authority; CLI fallback scope is only a fallback when the TaskContract has no project. Caller -> seam -> result: tracked scorer -> evidence capture -> recordUsefulnessApplicationOnce -> exact application readback. Missing application rows remain failure, never inferred from feedback metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence capture uses the persisted TaskContract project consistently for packet/usefulness authorization and application identity; a fallback runtime project cannot silently veto an explicitly scoped persisted run; genuinely foreign packet/project inputs remain rejected; the exact immutable run 690e9677 and its candidate row remain untouched; a focused falsifier reproduces fallback-project mismatch and proves exact selected application persistence/readback; DB return-loop and a new fresh immutable tracked pair persist selected then used/helped applications; typecheck, review, Fallow, and publication pass; one successful pair does not prove arbitrary-task causality or portability.

title: Replace syntax-shaped focused-test scoring with mutation proof
description: Fresh exact-identity run be06d537 was valid at the DecisionPacket boundary and both arms passed runtime, target test, typecheck, and diff checks, but the KRN arm was marked focused_tests=false because missing-email coverage used a table-driven loop (JSON.stringify(input)) instead of a direct JSON.stringify({}) expression. Static syntax matching again rejects real public-seam coverage. Replace the syntax-shaped observer with a behavioral proof that can establish each focused test protects malformed JSON, missing email, and unsupported role without depending on variable names, literal placement, or private result labels.
acceptance_criteria: Focused-test proof is invariant to direct, helper-based, and table-driven test structure; each of malformed JSON, missing email, and unsupported role has a distinct falsifier; removing any one test protection makes only its proof fail; production behavior is not inferred from test prose or result-label tokens; immutable run be06d537 remains invalid and is never retried; a fresh paired run can reach scoring and application persistence; focused tests, CLI typecheck, review, Fallow, and publication pass.
notes: Implemented in b28f87b3. Evidence: 4 focused files 52/52 on Node 22.23.1 and Node 26.2.0; CLI typecheck and clean test typecheck pass; Fallow CI reports no changed-file issues; real Node22 replay .local-lab/paired-live/replay-be06d537-mutation-proof-v5-node22-sync.json scored both arms 13/13 with all mutation markers; independent codex review of b28f87b3 clean after resolving its focused_test_control attribution-type finding. title: Remove leaked source-authority smoke fixtures blocking logical restore
description:
## Symptom

A logical pg_dump restore of the operator-designated local PostgreSQL store fails while recreating projects_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk.

## Proven Current-State Cause

Seven source-authority-integrity test markers created with session_replication_role=replica leaked 14 projects whose seven workspace parents are absent. The same project set owns 56 source artifacts, 35 source decisions, 7 search documents, and related source rows. All 14 projects are explicitly marked by metadata.smokeId and source-authority-integrity-* slugs.

## Repair Scope

On the designated local-PC store only, quarantine exact row identities/counts, delete the complete marked fixture graphs in dependency-safe order, and prevent recurrence by ensuring this destructive integrity test cannot target a designated persistent store. Do not touch unmarked rows. Preserve the verified physical backup until post-repair logical restore and integrity proof pass.

## Consumer / Authority

Consumer: local operator and DB readiness. Authority owner: operator-designated PostgreSQL store. Public seam: test/repair boundary -> logical backup restore -> readable store.

## Falsifier

Any unmarked row changes, any marked residue remains, logical restore still fails, source integrity worsens beyond removal of fixture-only violations, or the test can still run against a non-disposable database.

## Does Not Prove

Does not prove production correctness, source freshness, or semantic authority of retained records.
design: Delete only rows reachable from the six exact smokeId markers after recording preimages/counts; use the existing physical backup as rollback. Harden the test boundary at the caller so replica-mode fixture construction is confined to a disposable database.
acceptance_criteria: Exact marked preimages/counts are recorded; only the six leaked fixture graphs are removed; zero matching residue and zero project->workspace orphans remain; a fresh logical backup restores successfully with matching schema/data/migration hashes; recurrence is falsified at the test boundary; physical rollback remains available through verification.
notes:
Pre-repair preimage is preserved byte-for-byte in physical backup volume krn_backup_md7u126_20260716 and readable restore container krn-restore-md7u126-20260716. Exact fixture selector: metadata.smokeId LIKE source-authority-integrity-% across seven markers 0996aead-a28f-4847-9d3f-5982ad903729, 11c39095-ae73-40ff-a28a-cadc9f497d27, 6d9a8d63-16e7-48aa-b598-2594570927d4, c7c5b99f-70d2-495a-94e1-607137ca1680, d24dbd2a-37d7-4e23-9884-d02a67df5340, d5d975c1-ceaa-4a89-93b3-9a0cef5d85a7, d611d7ea-1c17-4d0e-b758-4293861ab490. title: Publish canonical Beads history to refs/dolt/data
description:
## What To Build

Configure and publish the designated Beads Dolt lineage through the repository's canonical Git remote channel.

## Priority

P0 — without `refs/dolt/data`, the durable graph is not recoverable canonically by a fresh clone.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

At current HEAD, `rtk bd dolt remote list` says `No remotes configured`, `rtk git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data` is empty, and the origin URL is `https://github.com/korneliuszburian/mise-en-palace.git`. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is pushed but Beads documentation states that export cannot replace Dolt pull because it cannot preserve complete history or absence semantics.

## Mechanism

After `mise-en-palace-md7u.184` designates the source lineage, add the Dolt-compatible origin, commit the non-secret `sync.remote` config, and perform a non-force `bd dolt push`.

## Violated Invariant

Canonical issue history must be published through `refs/dolt/data`; passive JSONL must never be the sole cross-machine recovery path.

## Runtime Consumer

`bd bootstrap`, `bd dolt pull`, post-checkout hooks, fresh agents, and maintainers recovering the task graph.

## Falsifier

`bd dolt push` cannot run because no remote exists, or a push would require force/overwrite because the designated lineage does not match the remote state.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk bd dolt push`

## Acceptance Criteria

The committed Beads config names `origin`, a non-force `bd dolt push` publishes the authorized lineage under `refs/dolt/data`, and local/remote ref identities are captured without changing issue semantics.

## Required Verification

Run `rtk bd dolt remote list`, non-force `rtk bd dolt push`, `rtk git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data`, and unchanged `rtk bd stats` plus `rtk bd graph check`.

## Proves

The designated lineage is reachable through the canonical remote ref and normal Dolt clients can discover its configured origin.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove fresh-clone bootstrap/readback, remote retention, backups, or that the issue content itself is correct.

## Rollback / Contraction

If publication cannot be proven non-destructive, remove only the uncommitted local remote configuration and remain blocked; never force-push or delete a remote ref without separate authority.

## Affected Files / Packages

`.beads/config.yaml`, local Dolt remote metadata, Git `refs/dolt/data`, Beads operational documentation if its executable contract differs.

title: Designate the authoritative unpublished Dolt lineage
description:
## What To Build

Make the smallest explicit authority decision required before first publication of the repository's Dolt issue history.

## Priority

P0 — publishing the wrong unpublished lineage can silently discard durable task history that JSONL cannot reconstruct.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`rtk bd dolt remote list` reports no remote and `rtk git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/data` reports no published lineage. The current workspace contains 1,152 issues and 1,088 interactions, but neither Git nor `.beads/config.yaml` identifies this local embedded database as the authorized first-publish source. Beads' repair guidance requires selecting the authoritative local database before adding a remote.

## Mechanism

Identify the owner of issue-history authority, capture the candidate local Dolt head and graph/readback counts, compare any other active workspace lineage, and explicitly authorize exactly one lineage or block on a named conflict.

## Violated Invariant

A first remote publication must originate from a deliberately designated complete lineage, never from whichever local database happens to run the command.

## Runtime Consumer

Beads operators, every future fresh clone, and all agents relying on dependency/history continuity.

## Falsifier

Two workspaces can contain divergent unpublished Dolt commits, or the current workspace is published without any recorded owner decision and immutable lineage identity.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk bd dolt remote list`

## Acceptance Criteria

The owner records one authorized local Dolt lineage with immutable head identity and matching issue/dependency/interaction evidence, or leaves publication blocked with each conflicting lineage named.

## Required Verification

Compare Dolt commit identity, `bd stats`, `bd graph check`, `bd lint`, and Beads history validation across every candidate workspace named by the owner.

## Proves

The selected lineage has explicit human authority for first publication and its observable graph matches the recorded evidence.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove that `refs/dolt/data` has been published, that a fresh clone can bootstrap, or that no unknown offline copy exists.

## Rollback / Contraction

Do not configure or push a remote until authority is explicit; if candidates conflict, preserve them read-only and narrow the decision to reconciliation evidence.

## Affected Files / Packages

Local `.beads/embeddeddolt` lineages, `.beads/config.yaml`, Beads history/readback commands, operator handoff.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on `mise-en-palace-md7u.183`.

## Human / Provider Authority

Human authority is required to designate the first-publish lineage; no provider write is authorized in this task.

Rollback: restore the verified backup; never delete quarantine history or relabel evidence current. Divergent stores: inventory first, add no alias without a separate reviewed decision. title: Split database inspect readiness and explicit migrate commands
description:
## What To Build

Make readiness use only read-only inspectors; add an explicit migrate command used by ephemeral setup before inspection.

## Priority

P0 — readiness mutates schema and migration 0029 differs across SQL schema snapshot and reachable local store

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`run-db-readiness-command.ts:76` invokes `runMigrationReadinessCheck`, which applies migrations at `migration-readiness.ts:227`. Migration 0029 adds NOT NULL/composite FK/unique/triggers at lines 276-336, but `schema/sources.ts:206` and snapshot `0029_snapshot.json:8308` remain nullable/simple. Read-only local non-authority probe found current 0029 SHA `057e6c47…` versus applied `a560a99e…`.

## Mechanism

Separate read-only inspect/readiness from explicit migration; inventory deployed immutable lineage before any forward repair; align TypeScript/schema snapshot/new migration and expose quarantine/backup proof.

## Violated Invariant

Readiness never writes; applied migration history is immutable and exactly ordered; all schema representations describe one store contract.

## Runtime Consumer

Operators, CI ephemeral DB setup, designated-store readiness, Drizzle queries and future migrations.

## Falsifier

Running readiness applies DDL, db:check passes while export omits manual constraints, or an applied filename/hash differs from current source.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/db db:check`; `rtk pnpm --filter @krn/db exec drizzle-kit export --config drizzle.config.ts`; read-only migration hash inspector.

## Acceptance Criteria

Readiness under read-only role performs zero writes; CI creates fresh DB via explicit migrate then inspect; missing migration is failed readiness.

## Required Verification

CLI tests, read-only PostgreSQL role proof and canonical verify:db flow.

## Proves

Inspection is non-mutating and migration/schema identity is explicit and forward-repairable.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove designated-store data correctness, backups, source truth or production readiness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Never rewrite applied history before inventory; use new forward migration and backup. Missing provider authority remains blocked.

## Affected Files / Packages

DB readiness/migration scripts, 0029 SQL/snapshot/schema, CLI/CI profiles, integrity/quarantine and backup proof.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.118.

## Human / Provider Authority

Lineage/designated-store and backup operations are human/provider-gated; disposable code/test work is autonomous.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review,beads

close_reason: Readiness is inspect-only, migration is explicit, and fresh Node-22 CI proves migrate-to-readiness flow.

Readiness and DB smokes now call the non-mutating inspector; krn db migrate is the only CLI path that applies migrations; verify:db and CI execute migrate before readiness. Proof: a real disposable PostgreSQL database stayed byte-for-byte unchanged after inspect on an absent schema, then explicit migrate created the exact ordered checked-in hash@createdAt identity sequence; a generated LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT role with no INSERT or public CREATE privilege also completed inspect with no state change. The actual CLI readiness command passed through a default_transaction_read_only connection with unchanged migration state. A fresh full verify:db passed, as did root typecheck, root tests (561 passed, 3 skipped), broad Fallow (0 dead/dupes; one pre-existing health signal), committed-range Fallow, git diff --check, and Beads validation/roundtrip/lint/orphans. Canonical Node-22 CI passed all jobs for cbeb71a: https://github.com/korneliuszburian/mise-en-palace/actions/runs/29205900412. Review classified Fallow's new output-format clone warning as non-actionable boilerplate: extracting two short command-specific report formats would hide the direct operator boundary without reducing behavioral duplication. Does not prove migration 0029 schema/snapshot alignment, immutable repair of any designated store lineage, backups/quarantine, persisted data quality, source truth, or product readiness; those remain separately owned.

title: Derive deterministic source import identity from project and corpus digest
description:
## What To Build

Canonicalize fixture/evidence manifest, hash with project identity, use it as import identity and print it.

## Priority

P0 — operator-facing corpus retry generates a new importId and semantic duplicate corpus

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`run-source-decision-import-command.ts:245-260` passes `runtime.createId`; default factory at `run-cli.ts:131` uses Date.now. Parser `parse-source-args.ts:82` has no stable import identity. Local non-authority store contains duplicated named decisions under different import IDs.

## Mechanism

Derive deterministic project+canonical corpus/evidence digest identity, reject payload conflicts, and expose read-only reconciliation for partial/semantic duplicates.

## Violated Invariant

Lost response or concurrent retry of identical corpus creates exactly one semantic graph; changed corpus never aliases silently.

## Runtime Consumer

Corpus importer, authority graph, SearchDocument retrieval, integrity operators.

## Falsifier

Two CLI processes import byte-identical file and double artifact/chunk/claim/decision/edge/document rows.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/cli exec vitest run src/__tests__/decision-corpus-import.test.ts` plus two-process PostgreSQL smoke.

## Acceptance Criteria

Byte-identical same-project request has one identity across processes/clocks; changed bytes/project differ; hash conflict fails.

## Required Verification

Unit/property tests and CLI preview/persist identity parity.

## Proves

Import retry identity, exact row counts and conflict handling are stable.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove corpus quality, source truth or safe automated merge of historical duplicates.

## Rollback / Contraction

Reject conflict and quarantine duplicate authority; never delete/merge without designated-store approval.

## Affected Files / Packages

Import CLI/parser/store identity/repository, schema/readiness, DB smoke and reconciliation readback.

Excluded, stale, rejected, superseded, invalidated, unlinked, or foreign-project candidates must not contribute authority.

title: Bind governing source imports to captured evidence content
description:
## What To Build

Before an imported row can create an adopted SourceDecision, governing edge, or active SearchDocument, bind its evidence reference to captured content. Local references must resolve inside the authorized repository root and store a digest plus captured provenance. URL references require an already captured artifact or snapshot and digest; do not add a network crawler. Missing or mismatched references may remain preview, history, or review input but cannot govern. ## Consumer

## Acceptance Criteria

- Existing missing run-evidence references cannot persist adopted/current authority.
- A local evidence byte change changes the digest and conflicts with unchanged import identity.
- Path traversal or references outside the authorized repo fail closed.
- An HTTP URL without captured bytes and digest cannot create adopt, edge, or active search rows.
- A valid captured local source can still pass review and activate.
- Readback distinguishes captured, missing, digest_mismatch, and externally_unverified.

## Falsifier

A syntactically valid nonexistent path or arbitrary URL produces project-decision authority.

title: Bind new source authority writes to a project-scoped current SourceDecision
description:
## What To Build

Introduce one direct source-authority identity for new writes. SourceDecision project must match the owning SourceArtifact project. SourceDecisionEdge must name the exact reviewed SourceDecision and matching SourceClaim, not only a claim plus arbitrary target. Repository and CLI lookups are project scoped. New cross-project adopt, link, claim-edge, seed, and rejection writes fail closed. Use expand-contract fields and repository guards so ambiguous legacy rows are not silently relinked; final legacy contraction belongs to src005.

## Consumer

Source review, source linking, memory seeding, activation support boosts, DecisionPacket governingDecisionIds, and source readback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An edge cannot be created without an adopted current SourceDecision for the same claim and project.
- Defer, reject, stale, superseded, foreign-project, or different-claim decisions cannot govern.
- SourceDecision project is derived from or checked against the claim artifact project and is not caller-invented.
- Cross-project adopt, link, claim-edge, rejection, and seed calls fail before writes.
- Activation joins through the exact SourceDecision identity.
- Ambiguous legacy rows are excluded and reported for src004 rather than repaired by guess.

## Falsifier

An accepted claim plus arbitrary target, with no canonical SourceDecision, appears in governingDecisionIds, or project B can govern from project A evidence.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: repository tests, real-PG cross-project probes, activation and DecisionPacket falsifiers, migration expand tests.

Non-proof: project and decision coherence do not prove source bytes or semantic truth.

## Native Dependency Edges

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep new writes fail-closed even if final NOT NULL constraints must wait for legacy quarantine. Do not add compatibility aliases for claim-level authority.

## Open Questions

notes: Proves: new SourceDecisionEdge writes require an exact sourceDecisionId; repository guards require the matching adopted current decision, accepted matching claim, and equal non-null SourceDecision/SourceArtifact project. SourceDecision project is derived from the owning artifact and caller mismatch fails closed. Claim edges and linked rejections reject cross-project writes before insert. title: Arbitrate SourceClaim terminal review transitions in PostgreSQL
description:
## What To Build

Make adopt and reject of a SourceClaim a guarded PostgreSQL transition. Derive project identity through SourceClaim to SourceArtifact and reject caller disagreement. Concurrent adopt, reject, or duplicate terminal review must have one winner. Insert the SourceDecision, claim status transition and outbox event in one transaction. Defer and lab_test remain non-terminal and cannot overwrite terminal authority. Do not use a pre-read as a lock.

## Consumer

createSourceDecision, source review and import commands, canonical source authority, and downstream edge creation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two independent connections racing adopt versus reject commit exactly one terminal SourceDecision, one claim transition, and one outbox event.
- Double-adopt and double-reject each have one winner.
- A project-B decision over a project-A claim fails before any row or event is written.
- Accepted, rejected, or deprecated claims cannot be overwritten through a stale pre-read.
- Defer and lab_test preserve terminal authority.
- Readback identifies the winning review.

## Falsifier

Both competing reviewers commit, last-writer-wins changes claim authority, or decision project differs from artifact project.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: real PostgreSQL, two synchronized clients, exact decision/claim/outbox counts, rollback cleanup, focused repository tests.

Non-proof: arbitration does not prove that the winning review is correct or that the source is true.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This is an unblocked P0 authority frontier item.

## Rollback / Contraction

If revision semantics remain unsettled, contract to guarded proposed-to-accepted-or-rejected transitions. Never retain last-writer-wins.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

drizzle-source-repository.ts:407 performs read-before-write followed by an unguarded claim update; sources.ts:177 has no current-decision transition constraint.

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: One PostgreSQL-owned transition decides a SourceClaim terminal review. Project identity is derived from the claim artifact; no pre-read may act as a lock.

title: Make retrieval index subordinate to canonical authority
description:
## What To Build

Enforce canonical subject lifecycle and project scope before a SearchDocument can contribute an activation candidate. For documents linked to SourceClaim, MemoryRecord, or AntiMemoryRecord, resolve the canonical subject and require matching project plus current, activatable lifecycle. Treat SearchDocument validity as index health only, not authority. Fail closed on incoherent subjectType/subjectId/link columns or missing canonical rows. Preserve lexical/vector scores and document provenance when the canonical candidate is valid. Define the existing unlinked-document case explicitly as non-governing search evidence or exclude it if no current consumer requires it.

## Consumer

Activation context assembly, source search, brain search, and the DecisionPacket sent to Codex.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An active SearchDocument linked to a rejected, deprecated, stale, superseded, or invalidated canonical subject is excluded even when that canonical subject was not present in a pre-limited candidate list.
- A document labeled with project A but linked to a canonical subject in project B fails closed.
- Incoherent subject identity/link columns cannot create an independent search candidate.
- A valid current linked document still boosts and carries provenance into the canonical candidate.
- DB plus harness tests cover the bypass with the index row active and canonical lifecycle non-current.

## Falsifier

Keeping an index row active is sufficient to reintroduce rejected, stale, invalidated, or cross-project content into assembled context.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof:

Focused retrieval repository tests, activation merge/filter tests, a DB-backed search/activation smoke falsifier, root typecheck, Fallow, and git diff check.

Non-proof:

Canonical coherence does not prove semantic relevance, source truth, or vector ranking quality.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This ready P0 must block the paired live trial so the trial packet cannot contain index-only authority.

## Rollback / Contraction

If query-time canonical joins are too broad, resolve only returned top candidates before activation and fail closed there. Do not copy canonical lifecycle into another independent authority field.

## Open Questions

Implementation must record the existing owner, if any, for unlinked SearchDocuments; absent a proven owner, exclude them from governing activation.

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: Smallest decision: SearchDocument is an index projection, never a parallel truth record. Inclusion must fail closed when its canonical subject lifecycle or project cannot be verified as current.
acceptance_criteria: Active index rows linked to non-current or cross-project canonical subjects cannot enter context; coherent current links retain retrieval scores and provenance; unlinked documents have an explicit bounded policy.
notes:
Audit evidence: search queries filter only SearchDocument/Embedding validity and project labels. Raw search candidates are independently merged; source/memory authority filters apply to canonical kinds, so an unmerged active index row can bypass rejected/deprecated/invalidated lifecycle.
Implementation evidence (current main, before closure):
- Added canonical SearchDocument resolver in packages/harness/src/activation/search-document-authority.ts.
- Active index rows now enrich only current project-scoped SourceClaim/MemoryRecord candidates; anti-memory, stale/deprecated, missing, incoherent, cross-project links fail closed.
- Unlinked documents are explicitly tagged non-governing indexed evidence.
- Added exact project-scoped SourceClaim lookup and wired DB/runtime/compiler ports.
- Red/green harness falsifier covers valid source+memory projections, stale, cross-project, anti-memory, incoherent, and missing links.
- DB activation smoke creates active stale and cross-project index rows and asserts both are absent from ContextAssembly; cleanup is zero.
- Proof so far: focused harness 162 tests, db repository suite 114 tests, root typecheck, db:ready, db:smoke:activation, quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.
- Non-proof: not semantic relevance/vector quality, source truth, or live Codex advantage.
close_reason: Completed in commit 100086ce, pushed to origin/main; CI run 29054454521 passed both Typecheck/tests/eval and DB readiness/smoke jobs. SearchDocument resolution is fail-closed for stale/deprecated/missing/incoherent/anti-memory/cross-project links, valid current source/memory links project into canonical candidates with provenance, and unlinked documents are explicitly non-governing. Local proof: harness activation 162 tests, db repository suite 114 tests, root typecheck, db:ready, db:smoke:activation, quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check. Does not prove semantic relevance, source truth, vector quality, or live Codex advantage.

title: Fence DecisionPacket governing authority from feedback
description:
## What To Build

Remove FeedbackDelta as an independent source of DecisionPacket governing authority. governingDecisionIds and governingStatements must come only from the current activation trace, project-standard decisions, and their canonical SourceDecision support. Keep source usefulness outcomes as bounded ranking, warning, review, and maintenance signals. Update the existing core expectation and DecisionPacket return-loop smoke so a newly created or packet-unseen SourceDecision cannot become governing merely because a caller reports selected, used, or helped.

## Consumer

The DecisionPacket rendered through CLI and MCP to Codex, plus later activation that reads usefulness feedback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A red-capable test submits selected, used, and helped feedback for a SourceDecision absent from the bound activation and proves that no governing ID or statement is created.
- Caller-supplied feedback reason text never appears as a governing statement.
- An activation-backed SourceDecision with valid current support still appears as governing independently of feedback.
- Stale, noise, hurt, and unknown outcomes remain visible through warning, review, or maintenance readback without directly rewriting source truth.
- The DB return-loop smoke no longer proves authority by creating a SourceDecision after the first packet and feeding it back as helped.

## Falsifier

Positive feedback alone can still place an unseen SourceDecision ID or arbitrary reason text into the next packet governing section.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof:

Focused core DecisionPacket tests, focused CLI read-model tests, db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop, root typecheck, Fallow changed-files gate, and git diff check.

Non-proof:

Removing the bypass does not prove feedback quality, causal usefulness, source truth, or live Codex advantage.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This is a ready P0 authority correction. It must block the paired live trial and measured-outcome return work.

## Rollback / Contraction

If a consumer needs feedback prose, expose it only in a non-governing feedback/readback section; do not restore it to governingStatements or governingDecisionIds.

## Open Questions

None. FeedbackDelta remains canonical feedback; activation and source support remain canonical authority.

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: Smallest decision: FeedbackDelta may influence ranking, review, and maintenance, but it cannot create governing truth. Governing IDs and statements must be projections of current activated, source-supported authority.
acceptance_criteria: Positive feedback for a SourceDecision absent from current activation cannot add a governing ID or statement; activation-backed authority remains renderable; stale/noise feedback stays diagnostic; core and DB return-loop falsifiers pass.
notes:
Audit evidence: packages/core/src/decision-packet.ts currently unions selected/used/helped sourceDecisionIds into governingDecisionIds and copies caller-supplied outcome.reason into governingStatements. A core test codifies an unbound conflicted decision as governing.
Reviewer evidence after cc8f repair: db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop is red because it creates SourceDecision rows after the first packet, submits them as helped/stale against that packet, and expects feedback-only IDs to become governing plus enqueue maintenance. cc8f correctly rejects those subjects as packet-unselected. This smoke rewrite is part of rpjt authority fencing: use subjects actually selected by the current packet, refresh checksum after packet-changing feedback, and stop asserting feedback-minted governing IDs.
Implementation complete in 2c22928a. DecisionPacket governingDecisionIds and governingStatements now come only from activation-backed source support/project standards; feedback selected/used/helped cannot mint authority or governing prose. Return-loop smoke now prepares canonical source claims before the packet, refreshes packet checksum between feedback writes, keeps helped/stale feedback diagnostic/review-bound, and downgrades unseen source-decision feedback to unknown. Proof: core/CLI focused tests, full pnpm test, root typecheck, Fallow changed-files gate, diff check, local db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop, CI run 29055397116 (jobs 86245599089 and 86245599122). Does not prove feedback quality, source truth, causal usefulness, live Codex advantage, or any remaining audit finding.
close_reason: Feedback cannot mint DecisionPacket governing authority; implementation 2c22928a is pushed and CI 29055397116 is green.

title: Make public metadata safe by default
description:
Why: public IO metadata currently starts from a permissive catchall in packages/core/src/parsing/schema-primitives.ts, while private-reasoning rejection is opt-in in selected parsers. In an AI memory system this is an authority leak: model/private reasoning keys can cross public boundaries unless each schema remembers to reject them.

Scope: introduce a safe public metadata parser or equivalent default-deny path for public IO schemas. Audit current MetadataSchema consumers in packages/core/src/parsing/*.ts and preserve explicitly internal metadata only where the boundary is named and bounded.

Non-goals: do not ban all metadata; do not rewrite unrelated schema fields; do not recreate @krn/schema; do not add prose-only tests.
acceptance_criteria: Public candidate/task/source/retrieval/evidence-facing parsers reject private-reasoning keys by default; any internal-only metadata parser is explicit in name and consumer; tests prove private reasoning keys cannot cross public candidate, source-claim, task-contract, retrieval, or evidence-capture boundaries; typecheck stays green.

Added a focused parser-boundary test covering memory candidate, source claim, task contract, retrieval candidate, and evidence capture inputs. Applied pattern:ts-boundary-unknown-first-result-state. title: Fix source governance blocking semantics
description:
Why: KRN's differentiator is temporal, source-backed, falsifiable authority. The audit flags source governance as the highest-risk current crack: invalid source timestamps appear to fail open, assessSourceClaimOverride may only block weaker candidates when the candidate is newer, and accepted source claims without linked decisions can read as authority instead of a blocking missing-link state.

Scope: inspect packages/core/src/source.ts and the activation/source-search/decision-packet consumers. Correct the blocking semantics for temporal invalidity, stronger-current-consensus override, and accepted-claim-without-decision inclusion. Keep this as policy behavior, not a file-splitting exercise.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy cleanup, no broad source graph redesign, no CLI rewrite, no markdown/prose tests.

The decision must keep runtime memory store-backed, avoid markdown/Beads/local artifact as the brain, avoid broad operator/executor platform work, and compare local lifecycle against current agent-memory mechanisms such as mem0 and Mastra observational memory.

## Required Skills
beads,krn-memory-core,source-to-decision,codebase-design,code-review
acceptance_criteria: A Beads decision records current local prepare->tracked->persist->cleanup lifecycle, external source mechanisms with source->mechanism->KRN implication->adopt/reject/lab-test/defer, chosen lifecycle disposition, first implementation slice(s) as child Beads with dependencies, proof/non-proof boundaries, and branch/upstream state. No code is changed in this design slice unless a separate child implementation Bead is created and claimed.
notes:
Decision 2026-07-19: valid paired-live eval evidence should survive retained fixture cleanup through the existing store-backed evidence/feedback/eval-candidate path, not through retained smoke rows, Markdown, Beads notes, or .local-lab artifacts.

Question: after a valid checker-v3 temporal-policy paired-live win, what owns durable evidence after cleanup?
Consumer: DecisionPacket/eval readback and future ablation frontier deciding whether KRN Memory Core gives Codex advantage.
Owner: paired-live persistence and a small DB-backed eval evidence read model. Cleanup remains a containment owner only.
Current local lifecycle: prepare-retained materializes target source and writes manifest/fixture report while retaining smoke DB rows; tracked runner writes immutable phase journal and artifact with manifestHash/artifactHash/checkerRevision/packet validation and held-out score; persist validates current DecisionPacket readback, artifact hash, manifest hash, checker revision, command outputs, decision-application readback, then writes evidence bundle + feedback delta with proposal-only EvalCandidate; cleanup deletes only owned retained fixture rows and requires remainingRows=0. Aggregate still mostly reads local artifacts, so DB readback is the next gap.
Local evidence: temporal-policy-drift-v3-trial-02 manifest is ready, checkerRevision=paired-live-codex-repair-checker.v3, artifact status=passed, outcome=win, artifactHash=4efc7a14168c0bd8a685e45bded368217af4ba5d4acc39eb6fff553dad53233a, manifestHash=8b805ee0a41a5a34e5b6205fd07ff14a1b1cbd3fd301d57835d2387a3f476482. HEAD f77b81ef is upstream-equal on fix/reviewed-memory-authority-upgrade.

Source decisions:
- mem0 docs: memory is scoped by user/session/agent/app/run, add extracts facts/decisions/preferences into additive storage, search uses semantic/filter/rerank, graph memory links shared entities, history exposes memory changes, and evaluation balances accuracy/cost/latency. KRN disposition: adopt scope + exact identity + lifecycle/readback discipline; reject opaque hosted Mem0 as runtime brain and reject additive-only truth promotion without review. Sources: https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-types, https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-operations/add, https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-operations/search, https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/features/graph-memory, https://docs.mem0.ai/api-reference/memory/history-memory, https://docs.mem0.ai/core-concepts/memory-evaluation.
- Mastra Observational Memory docs: observer/reflector condense long conversation history into dense observations, require persistent storage, keep range metadata to raw messages and provide recall/search for underlying raw history. KRN disposition: adopt derived observation with provenance/range/readback as a pattern; lab-test only behind current eval evidence and review; reject autonomous background observer/daemon as next step. Sources: https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/observational-memory and https://mastra.ai/docs/storage/overview.
- LangGraph/Zep/Graphiti docs: long-term memory uses store namespaces/keys and temporal graphs preserve changing facts/provenance better than static RAG. KRN disposition: adopt conceptually for temporal/source relation direction; defer new graph substrate until a named DecisionPacket query cannot be answered by current source/memory/retrieval read models. Sources: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/long-term-memory, https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/getting-started/overview, https://arxiv.org/html/2501.13956v1.
- OpenAI docs/cookbooks: Codex reads AGENTS.md as instruction context; Agents SDK sessions maintain conversation history and support storage/compaction; cookbook context management warns uncurated history can distract and stale summaries can poison future turns. KRN disposition: adopt AGENTS/skills as operating instructions and use bounded context; reject AGENTS.md, sessions, or summaries as governed runtime memory truth. Sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md, https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/, https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/agents_sdk/session_memory, https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/agents_sdk/context_personalization.

Chosen lifecycle: persist first, then cleanup. Artifact files are citable raw provenance and may be retained temporarily for audit, but the reusable brain surface is the DB readback: EvalCandidate + evidence bundle + feedback delta + exact refs (packet/artifact/manifest/checker/environment/patches) + decision applications. A helped EvalCandidate is not a MemoryRecord or SourceClaim truth mutation. Promotion requires a separate reviewed maintenance decision with falsifier.
Non-proof: this decision does not prove causal KRN advantage beyond the one temporal-policy v3 win, arbitrary-repo portability, product readiness, or that future eval families have enough metadata.
Frontier after consolidation: canonical child slices are mise-en-palace-n6g8p.1 store-backed paired-live eval evidence readback, mise-en-palace-n6g8p.3 guarded retained cleanup with persistence readback, mise-en-palace-n6g8p.6 reviewed eval-to-memory promotion gate decision, and mise-en-palace-n6g8p.8 next paired-live ablation with durable readback. Duplicate child slices mise-en-palace-n6g8p.2, .4, .5, and .7 were closed as absorbed so bd ready does not expose parallel work on the same seam. Dependency graph has no cycles. Branch state before export: fix/reviewed-memory-authority-upgrade, upstream-equal at f77b81ef before Beads commit; out-of-scope dirty state remains .beads/interactions.jsonl and new-audit/. Proof for this design slice: local code inspection of prepare/tracked/persist/cleanup/schema, current external source checks for Mem0, Mastra, and OpenAI docs, Beads dependency graph verification. Non-proof: no production code changed, no durable eval evidence implementation yet, no new live trial run yet.
close_reason: Lifecycle decision recorded with source dispositions, local lifecycle map, canonical child Beads, proof/non-proof, branch state, and duplicate frontier cleanup.

title: Design next discriminating Memory Core trial family
description:

Do not tune the completed weak-json checker, broaden operator/executor behavior, or claim advantage without preregistered evidence.

## Required Skills

design:
# Next discriminating Memory Core trial design

Current evidence:
- rerun17 artifact 0b7d54c2db898d867bb837cbf494934b875f7352ce198c6aa1de8980674fcfe3 is the first verified plain Codex vs semantic_governed KRN live trial result; outcome=tie on weak-json. This is valid evidence of no demonstrated advantage for that weak-json slice, not product readiness or broad no-effect.
- Local harness already contains async-job family scoring/runtime support, but retained fixture preparation is weak-json-only, the live repair prompt still names user-creation even for other families, and retained decision-application paths are weak-json-specific. Running async-job before fixing those would create a low-quality or misleading trial.

Source-to-decision synthesis:
1. Mem0 docs describe memory add/search as storing interaction-derived facts and retrieving relevant memories; v3 emphasizes ADD-only extraction plus explicit update/delete/entity-link mechanisms. Mechanism: retrieval alone is not enough; correction and lifecycle must be explicit. KRN implication: DecisionPacket must carry bounded current context plus stale/rejected/non-proof state, not a raw memory dump. Decision: adopt as a mechanism hypothesis for bounded semantic-governed retrieval. Consumer: paired live Codex eval. Falsifier: KRN arm does not use the packet or ties/loses on tasks where lifecycle should matter. Non-proof: Mem0 docs do not prove KRN advantage or source truth.
2. Mastra Observational Memory describes background observation logs and reflector compaction to preserve useful context while keeping runtime context smaller. Mechanism: long-running context can be summarized into maintained observations. KRN implication: observational treatment is worth a later isolated arm, but it is not needed to run the next semantic_governed trial and must not become a daemon/operator project. Decision: defer observational_summary until it has its own evidence contract. Consumer: later ablation, not current slice. Falsifier: no bounded observation readback or no benefit versus semantic-only. Non-proof: published benchmark/blog numbers are hypotheses, not KRN evidence.
3. LangChain/LangGraph memory material separates semantic facts, episodic experiences, and procedural rules. Mechanism: memory types have different consumers and failure modes. KRN implication: keep treatment labels isolated: semantic_governed first; episodic_examples and procedural_skills need separate readbacks, not silent mixing. Decision: adopt isolation rule; defer non-semantic arms until each has capability/application evidence. Consumer: paired-trial manifest and aggregation. Falsifier: treatment arms cannot be told apart in artifacts. Non-proof: taxonomy does not choose KRN architecture.
4. Zep temporal graph material emphasizes invalidating old facts while preserving history/time. Mechanism: temporal status is product behavior, not cleanup prose. KRN implication: next trial should force current-vs-stale-vs-rejected boundaries and non-proof/abstention behavior. Decision: adopt async-job temporal boundary as the next family. Consumer: DecisionPacket selection and live obedience validation. Falsifier: packet lacks stale/rejected visibility, or baseline solves equally without using lifecycle. Non-proof: one temporal trial does not prove arbitrary memory quality.
5. OpenAI Codex manual recommends durable AGENTS.md guidance, clear goal/context/constraints/done criteria, relevant tests/typecheck/review, and subagents only for independent work when explicitly requested or instructed. Mechanism: workflow quality comes from scoped context, verification, and review, not dumping more instructions. KRN implication: keep review as maker/checker separation and advisory local verification; encode stable gotchas in AGENTS/CONTEXT only after repeated failures. Decision: adopt for repo workflow; reject broad operator/executor expansion. Consumer: current branch workflow and future PR handoffs. Falsifier: branch accumulates unverified claims, unrelated dirty work, or review findings are applied without local proof. Non-proof: manual workflow guidance does not prove Memory Core product behavior.

Chosen next family:
- Name: async-job-temporal-boundary using the existing async-job checker family as the next live repair family.
- Arms: baseline plain Codex with target repo only; KRN semantic_governed Codex with the same target plus DecisionPacket through MCP/obedience contract.
- Packet-visible information target: current decisions for unknown-first enqueue, non-empty idempotencyKey, finite retryBudget, explicit leaseTimeoutMs, finite states queued/leased/completed/retryable_failed/dead_lettered, injected clock, owner files, and no daemon/scheduler/dashboard/queue-service expansion; stale/rejected paths for throw-only failures, forever retry, no idempotency, global time mutation, and daemon expansion; non-proof and evidence-gap state must remain visible.
- Baseline-visible information: the materialized target repo, its AGENTS/docs/source/tests, and task text. No KRN packet, no KRN MCP authority.
- Held-out checks: async-job family_contract; target test/typecheck/diff-check; held-out runtime enqueue/lease readback with clock-derived value; forbidden-file boundary; capability-use observation; KRN obedience JSON validation against packet; decision-application persistence only when mapped changed files/checks are observed.
- Readbacks: artifact must include outcome, family, checkerRevision, prompt delta bytes/hash, capability observation, live obedience status, decisionApplicationObservation, token/latency where currently available, and non-proof. A passed artifact can still be a tie.
- Falsifiers: invalid packet/capability/obedience/application evidence; KRN ties or loses; baseline passes same held-out checks; KRN changes forbidden files; KRN increases complexity/cost without quality signal; checker observes target pass without packet-derived obedience.

Falsifier: doctor says ready from historical rows, stale/foreign proof, or smoke pass with failed cleanup; proof missing remains unverified. First design the owning table/record and lifecycle before implementation; avoid a generic dashboard or broad runtime memory layer.

Non-proof: persisted smoke proof does not establish broad activation quality, Codex obedience, arbitrary-repo portability, or product readiness.

title: Evaluate observational memory layer for Codex/KRN
description: Compare Mem0-style extract/update/retrieve memory and Mastra Observational Memory observer/reflector compression against KRN DecisionPacket authority. design: Sources converge on distinct mechanisms: Mem0 extract/update/retrieve; Mastra Observer/Reflector background compression; Letta in-context core blocks plus archival retrieval; LangGraph thread checkpoints plus namespaced semantic/episodic/procedural stores; Graphiti temporal episodes/provenance with hybrid retrieval. KRN should not copy a vendor architecture. Run a bounded comparison against KRN DecisionPacket authority, candidate-only writes, provenance and abstention.
notes: Research disposition: lab-test observational/session compression as an adapter around governed KRN, never as an alternate authority. Include token budget, latency, retrieval/usefulness, temporal-update, provenance, stale/rejected-path, and memory-poisoning falsifiers. Vendor benchmark claims are non-proof of KRN quality.

comments.author: korneliuszburian

Proposed implementation: remove only the precondition, retain post-decision accepted readback and repository transaction; do not auto-create edges or memory. Baseline therefore stopped without repairing and the KRN arm timed out; the invalid result is not a capability comparison.

## Context
Follow-up to mise-en-palace-rusew. Fresh run ad737ac8-8033-480e-808e-a193e3a52ee8, packet checksum 68036a16578a8ab2b55b32e7392b0d365fc90c3c5703cf837d870ba23c9fbed8, invalid because baseline was blocked by missing docs/repair-contract.md while fixture has docs/config-contract.md and KRN timed out.
design: Keep the participant contract honest and fixture-owned. Replace the hard-coded filename with wording that requires reading AGENTS.md and the contract documentation actually present in the target, while preserving the baseline/KRN prompt identity except for the packet delta. Add a focused prompt falsifier and rerun one fresh task-specific pilot after the seam is published. Do not change DecisionPacket authority or add an executor/operator layer.
acceptance_criteria: The paired baseline prompt no longer assumes a non-existent contract filename and tells Codex to inspect present target contract docs; focused tests prove packet-only delta and absence of the stale hard-coded path; one fresh packet-valid env-config attempt after publication is either a quality outcome or explicit unavailable/invalid aggregate with diagnostic reason; no operator/executor behavior is introduced.
notes: Published d681e29e and ran fresh packet-valid task-specific attempt: executionRun 5e70c579-a688-4095-b34a-2bb0c2e6cdd5, task 5726e21c-3097-4d29-95f9-d53edc090e32, packet checksum 0f870d74f0af1ce89f4ca3b37655cfb28a12093b84bda14c9af5dde942ffd2b2. Prompt no longer assumed docs/repair-contract.md; KRN arm completed exitCode=0/timedOut=false, baseline arm timedOut=true. Aggregate task-specific-env-aligned: totalInputs=1, qualityTrials=0, invalidTrials=1, unreadableInputs=0. Result remains unavailable, not a quality outcome; prompt contract confound is removed but 120s shared budget is now the next confound.
close_reason: Prompt now follows fixture-owned contract docs and focused falsifier passes; fresh packet-valid pilot after publication was aggregated as invalid because baseline timed out while KRN completed, with no quality claim.

title: Make paired eval arm availability diagnosable and reproducible
description:

title: Falsify bounded KRN advantage on a novel env boundary
description: The balanced pilot found one KRN win in env-config and ties in async-job/weak-json. Before broadening any claim, run a novel env-boundary fixture with a different hidden requirement and the same paired baseline/KRN protocol to test whether the observed information advantage replicates.
design: Create one bounded target fixture with an independently held-out runtime observer and a hidden requirement not copied from the previous getter-redaction task. Keep prompts matched except packet bytes, use the aggregate readback, and predeclare what counts as quality, invalid, tie, and unavailable. Compare per-family, not pooled causal claims.
acceptance_criteria: A novel env-boundary fixture has a contract, hidden observer, matched baseline/KRN run, validated aggregate artifact, and a decision that explicitly adopts, rejects, or defers replication. A failure/tie is valid evidence and cannot be relabeled setup failure unless the predeclared conditions were unmet. No operator/executor implementation.
notes:
Prior bounded decision: env-config win, async-job tie, weak-json tie; next work must test replication rather than accumulate same-fixture wins.
Novel fixture completed 2026-07-17: .local-lab/paired-live/asymmetric-env-whitespace with hidden whitespace MODE rejection observer (KRN_PAIRED_VARIANT=whitespace-mode). Fresh matched run used packet 88eb9732bb1af12495678fd1a2170bc7a1364e68ce6a65e6b5ee8fc41fc8bbb5 and result .local-lab/paired-live/fresh-20260717-novel-env-whitespace.json; baseline failed held-out whitespace rejection, KRN passed; aggregate readback .local-lab/paired-live/fresh-20260717-novel-env-whitespace-aggregate.json = 1 win / 0 ties / 0 losses / 0 invalid. First attempt was honestly invalid due fixture node:assert/type setup and was rerun after removing confound. Decision: adopt bounded replication of information-advantage hypothesis for strict config-boundary tasks, but same packet reuse is non-proof of task-specific causal memory usefulness or general portability. Falsifier: task-specific packet on another boundary or balanced replicate fails to beat/tie baseline.
close_reason: Novel env-boundary fixture produced a valid held-out runtime KRN win after one explicitly invalid setup attempt; bounded replication decision and limitations recorded.

title: Run balanced paired-live pilot and make bounded capability decision
description: Use the published paired artifact aggregate readback to run a fresh balanced pilot across env-config, async-job, and weak-json families with the same model/profile and independent held-out observers, then turn the aggregate into an explicit adopt/reject/lab-test/defer decision. This is the evidence frontier for whether KRN context creates a bounded advantage over baseline Codex.
design: Use matched fixtures and packet-only prompt delta. Record environment fingerprints, arm exits, target verification, held-out runtime outcomes, latency/byte costs, and invalid/unavailable reasons. Aggregate only validated unique runs; keep per-family results separate and do not infer causality from a small sample. Route the resulting source-to-decision artifact through the existing KRN decision owner, not a new operator layer.
acceptance_criteria: At least one fresh run per family is attempted with auditable manifests/artifacts; aggregate readback reports quality vs invalid inputs and per-family counts; a bounded decision names mechanism, KRN implication, consumer, falsifier, and non-proof; runtime unavailability or model capacity errors are recorded honestly; no executor/operator code is introduced.
notes:
Frontier after eae49b60. Existing prior evidence: static 3 wins; runtime prior 2 wins + 1 tie; fresh env-config runtime win. Need balanced current evidence before any broad claim.

title: Own the FeedbackDelta governing lifecycle or remove its inert suppression branch

design: Decision: FeedbackDelta is immutable review-only evidence/candidate readback, never selection authority. ReviewAssessment assesses evidence but does not promote memory. Negative governing change has one owner and public transition: AntiMemoryCandidate -> explicit reviewed promotion -> AntiMemoryRecord -> activation exclusion. Positive governing change remains explicit MemoryCandidate/SourceDecision review/promotion. Remove direct accepted/applied FeedbackDelta suppression and DecisionPacket authority effects. Preserve legacy lifecycle values for stored read compatibility only; rejected stays hidden, all other deltas remain review caveats until a governed artifact exists. Rollback: restore status-gated projection only if a future explicit lifecycle owner can prove atomic linkage to the promoted governed artifact. Non-proof: removing the bypass does not itself prove the subsequent helped-learning loop.
acceptance_criteria: Map review assessment, feedback delta, maintenance, anti-memory and both selection surfaces; choose one owner and public transition; preserve candidate feedback as review-only; no review result silently becomes governing feedback; prove the selected path through real PostgreSQL and the next plan/search readback; record rollback and non-proof.

title: Run one fresh exact-head paired OAuth trial from canonical ready authority
description:
## What To Run

Create one fresh canonical paired-live ExecutionRun in the operator-designated local per-PC store through the public krn plan --persist path, bind its exact run/task/project IDs and ready packet checksum into one secret-free local manifest, and execute the existing tracked ChatGPT-OAuth paired runner exactly once in a new immutable attempt directory. Persist the mechanical outcome through the existing paired-trial return path.

## Preconditions

Current diagnosis proves the public provisioning path emits a status=ready packet with the exact three required weak-JSON governing decisions, their canonical SourceDecision IDs and formal SourceRejection. Host Codex OAuth is authorized by the operator. The prior valid pair was neutral 3-3 and must not be reused as current evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pin exact current KRN commit, Node 22, Codex CLI/model/profile, checker, source tree and local store fingerprint.
- Create a new ExecutionRun via public KRN commands; verify MCP packet readback is exact run/project/task bound, ready, checksum-current, and includes all required governing decisions before claiming an attempt.
- Generate the one-shot manifest only in ignored local-lab state; include no credential material and hash it into the artifact.
- Materialize byte-identical baseline/KRN targets, hold all conditions equal except the bounded packet prompt delta, and run each arm once. Never retry one arm alone.
- Accept win, tie, loss or invalid mechanically; missing auth/tool/version/containment/packet makes blocked or invalid, never pass.
- Persist the artifact, command evidence, target diff/checker result and neutral/eval candidate through the existing return path. Record application/usefulness only if existing authority can prove the exact selected subject was applied and fresh verification supports the claimed state.
- A tie/loss/invalid is valid completion but cannot become helped evidence and leaves ready001 DEFER.

## Falsifier

The trial uses a stale packet, different starting bytes/conditions, a hand-edited winning transcript, a reused attempt, an arm-only retry, or classifies mere selection/exit-0 as helped.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: immutable verified trial artifact, exact current packet and environment identity, held-out score, persisted readback and reviewed outcome. Non-proof: one result does not prove broad model obedience, arbitrary-repo portability, source truth, commercial validation or product readiness.

## Boundary

No product/schema/API/MCP changes. Do not modify new-audit or retained research worktrees. If the existing runner/persistence path fails for a proven code defect, stop and create one repair Bead instead of patching inside the live attempt.

title: Determine whether paired-live authority can honestly issue a ready packet
description:
## Question

At exact current main and against a disposable copy of the designated per-PC store state, can the existing paired-live weak-JSON task receive a canonical status=ready DecisionPacket with its exact required governing decisions through current source, activation, and issuance authority? If not, what single missing or invalid authority link causes weak_context/abstention or prevents issuance?

## Current Counterexample

The designated store is healthy, but run paired-live-codex-repair-current is absent, so the tracked OAuth runner cannot fetch its packet. The newly proven target-repo path issues a different ephemeral packet with exact governing/source-decision IDs but status weak_context and then cleans up. The tracked runner correctly requires ready plus exact run/project/task/decision identity.

## Consumer

The existing tracked paired-live OAuth runner and, only after a valid run, the existing application/evidence/review return path.

## Caller And Seams

paired-live manifest -> canonical task/run/source provisioning -> activation -> issueDecisionPacketForExecutionRun -> read-only krn_decision_packet MCP -> validateTrialPacket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reproduce the absent-run failure and then exercise the closest current canonical provisioning path in disposable state.
- Map each manifest requiredDecisionId to current SourceClaim, SourceDecision, architecture_decision edge, temporal/review state, activation inclusion/exclusion and abstention reason.
- Prove whether status ready is reachable without aliases, fabricated support, manual DB writes or weakening abstention.
- If reachable through existing behavior, record the exact secret-free preparation recipe and create only the one-shot live execution Bead; do not execute it inside this diagnostic ticket.
- If not reachable, identify one proven owner/seam/cause and create exactly one agent-sized repair or bounded corpus decision Bead with a red-capable falsifier.
- A correct weak_context/abstain result is a valid outcome and leaves ready001 DEFER.

## Falsifier

A packet is called ready by inserting arbitrary governing IDs, reusing a different run, treating weak_context as ready, bypassing captured source authority, or relying on an old packet/artifact.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: exact current code/store readback, disposable canonical provisioning attempt, activation trace and packet checksum/MCP validation. Non-proof: ready reachability would not prove Codex use, a KRN win, helped evidence, portability, source truth or product readiness.

## Boundary And Contraction

Diagnosis only. Do not add schema, public API/MCP, benchmark lanes or production indirection. Do not modify new-audit. If the cause is not proven, close with explicit unknown/blocker rather than designing a repair.

## Required Skills
beads,diagnosing-bugs,krn-memory-core,codebase-design

Run independent bounded shards for: (1) current-repo architecture and ownership, (2) temporal/agent-memory mechanisms from pinned sources, (3) real-task application/usefulness proof, and (4) current source coverage/abstention. Research and design selection do not prove the chosen mechanism works or that KRN beats plain Codex.
