title: Wayfind the next real-task Memory Core slice
description:
## Destination
Expose a truthful, agent-sized route from the current internal-alpha kernel to a Memory Core that demonstrably helps on real engineering tasks: selected current standards and rejected/stale paths alter Codex behavior, subject-bound evidence returns through review/feedback, and later activation changes without bypassing authority.

## Consumer
The KRN operator and Codex executor need the next highest-leverage production slice after the valid but neutral 3-3 live pair and the DEFER decision for broader MCP.

## Decisions So Far
- Build the Memory Core, not UI, broad API/MCP, scheduler, crawler, benchmark platform, prompt archive, or markdown runtime memory.
- Keep the existing read-only krn_decision_packet transport.
- Use real tasks as bounded falsifiers; deterministic/recorded/DB evidence remain separate from live usefulness.
- Current designated per-PC store and provider enforcement are usable local-alpha infrastructure, not production proof.
- One neutral live pair and incomplete declared source coverage do not establish helped.

## Not Yet Specified
- Which current kernel boundary most limits subject-bound helped evidence: activation/abstention, temporal consensus, evidence application identity, feedback policy, or task/repo recognition.
- Which real engineering task family can exercise the missing mechanism without creating a benchmark lane.
- Which source-coverage gaps are product blockers versus honest abstention inputs.
- Whether the next slice is a missing mechanism, a deeper existing interface, or only a new current trial.

## Open Questions Blocking Slicing
1. Map caller -> DecisionPacket selection -> Codex application -> evidence/review/feedback -> later activation at current HEAD and rank at most three evidenced ownership/mechanism gaps.
2. Derive a bounded real-task battle protocol that can prove packet-selected subject application and later helped/hurt/neutral outcome without prompt archives or retry gaming.
3. Compare current temporal/source consensus and abstention behavior with selected external mechanisms, then adopt/reject/defer each with a KRN consumer and falsifier.
4. Synthesize exactly one first vertical implementation or trial slice and explicit non-goals.

## Out Of Scope
Dashboard, broad MCP/API, daemon/scheduler, large ingest, generic multi-agent orchestration, unbounded benchmark platform, test-count goals, speculative refactors, and claims of perfection/readiness.

## Frontier
The first child is a source-bound architecture/usefulness research ticket. Implementation tickets are forbidden until its synthesis selects a concrete consumer, owner, seam, and falsifier.

## Native Dependency Edges
This map depends on its research child; later children may be added only when the current answer makes them specific.

## Falsifier
The map is too vague if research returns package-layer tasks, generic best practices, a broad benchmark roadmap, or more than one first vertical slice without current-code evidence.
design: Wayfinding, not implementation planning. Use a current-repo architecture shard, external mechanism shards, a real-task usefulness shard, and one synthesis. Keep evidence classes distinct and create only the first earned vertical ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A validated research synthesis at a pinned current HEAD ranks no more than three current gaps, selects one next vertical slice or a no-op/trial decision, records consumer/owner/falsifier/non-proof, and leaves bd ready with an honest agent-sized frontier.

title: Tag stale-import deprecation outbox for exact smoke cleanup
description:
## What To Fix
Make stale decision-corpus import deprecation outbox events carry the import smoke marker so source smoke cleanup can count and delete them. A green decision-corpus DB smoke currently leaks source.claim.deprecated rows with dangling sourceClaimId values.

## Red Reproduction
On designated local-alpha at d8f3b461, source.claim.deprecated totals were 98 unmarked / 87 dangling. One green pnpm db:smoke:decision-corpus-import run reported Cleanup: completed but increased them to 107 unmarked / 96 dangling.

## Proven Cause
DeprecateSourceClaimInput has no metadata, source-decision-store-import drops prepared row metadata when deprecating stale claims, and DrizzleSourceRepository.deprecateSourceClaim emits payload {sourceClaimId,revisitWhen} without smokePayload. cleanupSourceSmokeMarkers and countSourceSmokeMarkers can only see payload.smokeId/source.

## Consumer
Decision-corpus DB smoke cleanup and outbox/maintenance consumers that must not receive orphaned smoke-only deprecation events.

## Boundary
Preserve the real production deprecation event and lifecycle. Carry optional operation metadata only to outbox evidence; do not delete arbitrary historical unmarked events, weaken source lifecycle, or broaden cleanup by topic alone.

## Falsifier
A primary stale import emits source.claim.deprecated with its exact smokeId; after the smoke finishes, the pre-existing unmarked total does not increase and zero events for the current smokeId remain.

## Non-Proof
Clean smoke outbox markers do not prove source truth, maintenance consumption, arbitrary event cleanup, or Memory Core readiness.
design: Extend the existing deprecation input with optional metadata, pass the prepared import-row metadata through the stale-claim lifecycle call, and reuse the repository's existing smokePayload policy for the outbox event. Add one focused public-seam falsifier that fails if the stale import event loses its smokeId again.
acceptance_criteria: The designated-store red repro is green: a run emits tagged stale-deprecation events, cleanup removes them, unmarked/dangling historical counts do not increase, current-smoke event count is zero, focused DB/repository proof and narrow TypeScript checks pass, fixed-point Standards/Spec review has no unresolved finding, and publication state is recorded.
notes:
Second-opinion diagnosis at d8f3b461 confirmed a source.claim.deprecated cleanup leak. Red designated-store measurement: 98 unmarked/87 dangling -> 107 unmarked/96 dangling after one green decision-corpus smoke. Proven cause: deprecation input/importer/outbox path dropped smoke metadata. Production slice now carries optional metadata through the public repository input, passes prepared import lineage, and reuses smokePayload; activation smoke proof also counts/deletes tagged outbox rows. Green: focused DB historical-warning test 2/2; decision-corpus CLI tests 13/13; original designated-store smoke passed and left counts unchanged at 107 unmarked/96 dangling/0 tagged remaining; canonical Node 22 root typecheck and clean CLI test typecheck passed; Fallow found no new issues. Fixed-point Standards/Spec review: no findings. Historical unmarked rows are intentionally not deleted by this slice.
Published fix: commit 86e99ec3b0085e4215787d45d5130cd7e279751d, PR #7, GitHub Actions run 29525790362 with all four required checks green, squash merge 5acee934dda524952318d4dba65240e724d3e7e3. Local main equals origin/main. Second-opinion pass result was schema/freshness validated and locally dispositioned: one accepted finding (this fix), sound design confirmations rejected as backlog, shared deterministic smokeId concurrency retained only as a future trigger. Runtime green remained 107 historical unmarked / 96 historical dangling / 0 tagged remaining after the fixed smoke; this slice intentionally did not delete history. Non-proof: no claim of source truth, maintenance consumption correctness, concurrency safety, or Memory Core readiness.

title: Close SourceClaimEdge concurrency races at ownership and retry boundaries
description:
## What To Build

Make SourceClaimEdge project validation and semantic retry identity safe under concurrent transactions.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

Migration 0049 `enforce_source_claim_edge_same_project()` and migration 0050 `enforce_retained_source_claim_edge_same_project()` use plain SELECTs and acquire no shared/advisory lock spanning endpoint ownership and edge writes. `DrizzleSourceRepository.createSourceClaimEdge()` performs select-then-insert; a concurrent exact retry can lose the race to the unique index and surface raw 23505 instead of returning the canonical row.

## Violated Invariant

No serializable interleaving may commit a cross-project canonical edge, and concurrent exact retries produce one semantic edge/outbox identity.

## Runtime Consumer

Source import/preview, consensus, ranking, DecisionPacket graph consumers.

## Falsifier

Two coordinated clients pause after validation: one inserts an edge while the other moves endpoint ownership; both commit and readiness reports cross-project identity. Two exact retries race and one returns 23505.

## Non-Proof

Concurrency integrity does not prove allowed relation semantics or source truth.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,implement,code-review
design: Use one deterministic lock order over endpoint ownership/identity rows (or equivalent transaction-safe mechanism), then make repository unique conflicts re-read and compare canonical metadata without duplicating outbox emission.
acceptance_criteria: A coordinated two-client PostgreSQL test proves edge-vs-ownership interleavings cannot both commit cross-project state; concurrent exact retries return one canonical ID with one outbox event, while conflicting metadata fails explicitly.
notes:
Implemented migrations 0051-0052 with one transaction-scoped advisory lock across SourceClaimEdge identity writes and endpoint ownership changes; retained read-committed requirement and ordered new triggers after the existing SearchDocument isolation contract. Repository insert now uses semantic ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, re-reads the canonical row, compares canonical metadata, and emits outbox only for the winner. Deterministic PostgreSQL falsifiers observe actual pg_stat_activity lock waits for ownership-vs-edge and two exact retries. Evidence: focused integrity 5/5; regression target 1/1; DB package 199/199; @krn/db typecheck; drizzle db:check; local-alpha readiness 53/53 migrations, 0 authority violations; quality:fallow:ci green with advisory inherited duplication only. Read-only fixed-point review found no actionable Standards or Spec defect. krn-implementation catalog owner unavailable; global implement used as recorded installation gap.
Published commit 567a0eb4eb6be331525a0120f28fb85b95716bf0 to origin/main. Exact-SHA KRN CI run 29506864054 passed all four jobs, including Linux DB readiness/smoke, macOS disposable Postgres, full typecheck/tests/evals/Fallow, and dependency/secret/license policy.
close_reason: Implemented and published as 567a0eb4eb6be331525a0120f28fb85b95716bf0; exact-SHA CI run 29506864054 passed all four required checks and fixed-point Standards/Spec review found no actionable defect.

title: Repair source graph readiness probe after captured-authority enforcement
description:

title: Prevent graph expansion from promoting non-governing endpoints
description:
## What To Build

Gate bounded negative-edge endpoint expansion so a seed without current rank-down authority cannot introduce a lexically unrelated endpoint as governing context.

## Priority

P1 — stale or otherwise non-governing graph seeds can bypass task relevance and promote unrelated authority.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

activation-engine.ts expands endpoints from every current supersedes/invalidates edge around seedSourceClaims before source consensus assesses whether the seed can drive rank-down. seedSourceClaims includes historical warnings. The expanded endpoint is then assessed normally and can become accepted authority.

## Steps to Reproduce

Return a historical seed from listHistoricalClaimWarningsForProject, attach a current supersedes edge to a lexically unrelated current claim, and give both claims decision-support edges. retrieveActivationCandidates materializes the endpoint before the historical seed is denied rank-down authority, allowing the unrelated endpoint to remain accepted.

## Mechanism

Prove the stale-seed promotion at retrieveActivationCandidates, then require endpoint expansion to preserve the same rank-down authority boundary used by source consensus without adding recursive traversal.

## Violated Invariant

Graph expansion may recover negative evidence but must not create a new governing path from a non-governing seed.

## Runtime Consumer

Activation candidates, ContextAssembly, source consensus and DecisionPacket.

## Falsifier

A historical lexically matched seed has a current supersedes edge to a lexically unrelated current decision-linked endpoint; the endpoint appears in context inclusions or governing packet IDs.

## Reproduction Command

rtk mise exec node@22.23.1 -- pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/activation/__tests__/index.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

The unrelated endpoint is not governing when its only recall path starts at a stale or otherwise non-rank-down-capable seed; current decision-linked seed expansion still yields exact superseded negative evidence; bounds and one-hop behavior remain unchanged.

## Required Verification

Red/green focused activation falsifier, harness tests and typecheck, PostgreSQL activation smoke, fixed-point review, Fallow and diff-check.

## Proves

Bounded graph recall cannot promote authority through a non-governing seed.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove relation truth, relevance beyond selected seeds, or justify recursive traversal.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail closed by skipping expansion when seed rank-down authority cannot be established.

## Affected Files / Packages

Harness activation engine and tests; PostgreSQL activation smoke only if its authority proof needs extension.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by and blocks mise-en-palace-md7u.25.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority; this preserves the existing source-consensus authority owner.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,implement,krn-memory-core,code-review
acceptance_criteria: No lexically unrelated endpoint can become governing when its only expansion seed lacks current rank-down authority; current authorized negative-edge recall remains bounded and exact.
notes: Red falsifier on current code: focused activation test failed because retrieval candidates contained claim-unrelated-current-endpoint when its only recall path was a current supersedes edge from historical claim-historical-graph-seed. Fixed in commit 21ffee0bf333175750e73ee1e813317c455f1cbd by deriving rankDownAuthoritySeedIds from the existing source-consensus owner before endpoint materialization and expanding only from those seeds. Seed decision edges/rejections are read once and reused; one-hop traversal and 4-per-seed/20-global/project limits are unchanged. Existing bounds fixtures were completed with falsifiers so they now represent real current authority. Verification: red then green focused test, activation 55/55, harness 184/184, harness typecheck, diff-check, fresh PostgreSQL activation smoke exact 0 lexical seeds / 1 exclusion / 1 superseded path / 0 governing refs, fixed-point Standards/Spec review no further findings, exact-range Fallow no new issues, exact-SHA CI 29491773982 all four jobs successful. Does not prove relation truth or justify graph traversal beyond authorized seeds and one hop.
close_reason: Graph endpoint expansion now reuses source-consensus current authority and cannot promote unrelated authority from historical seeds.

title: Bind reviewed memory revisions to their proposed source record
description:
## What To Build

Reject an atomic reviewed-memory revision unless the repository input sourceMemoryRecordId exactly matches the source identity persisted with the proposal candidate.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

proposeMemoryRevision writes metadata.memoryRevision.sourceMemoryRecordId in packages/harness/src/memory/memory-consolidation.ts. applyReviewedMemoryRevision accepts a second sourceMemoryRecordId. DrizzleMemoryRepository.applyReviewedMemoryRevision reads the candidate, but checks only that the supplied source and generated replacement share a project and that the supplied source is active; it never compares the supplied source to the candidates proposed source identity.

## Mechanism

Parse the persisted candidate revision identity unknown-first at the repository authority boundary, require an exact candidate/source match before candidate acceptance or replacement creation, and keep the existing transaction rollback/CAS behavior. Do not accept a caller metadata override or add an alias.

## Violated Invariant

A reviewed revision may replace only the exact MemoryRecord for which it was proposed and evidenced.

## Runtime Consumer

Memory consolidation review, canonical MemoryRecord lineage, listActiveMemory, activation, and revision audit.

## Falsifier

Create two active records in one project and a revision candidate proposed for source A; apply it with source B. Any accepted candidate, replacement row, superseded B row, version, or outbox event fails the boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

Same-project source substitution rejects before canonical change; exact source applies atomically; retry/conflict behavior remains deterministic; no partial rows or events survive.

## Required Verification

Focused disposable-PostgreSQL mismatch and exact-control test, Memory Core typecheck, Fallow, independent Standards/Spec review, and exact-SHA Node22 CI.

## Proves

Persisted proposal identity owns which source record a reviewed revision may supersede.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove reviewer judgment, semantic superiority, source truth, or designated-store cleanliness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail closed on absent or malformed revision source identity; do not infer a source from same-project status or caller metadata.

## Affected Files / Packages

Core MemoryRepository revision contract if needed, harness proposal/apply boundary, Drizzle memory repository, focused PostgreSQL proof.

## Human / Provider Authority

No external authority; Memory Core owns the temporal identity boundary.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-memory-core,implement,code-review
notes: Bound applyReviewedMemoryRevision to the persisted candidate metadata.memoryRevision.sourceMemoryRecordId before mutation and made candidate-owned revision metadata canonical across accepted candidate, replacement, and replacement version. Does not prove reviewer judgment, semantic superiority, source truth, or designated-store cleanliness.

title: Prevent deprecated memory warnings from regaining activation authority
description:
## What To Build

Make every deprecated MemoryRecord retrieved as a bounded historical warning remain non-governing through activation and context assembly.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

DrizzleMemoryRepository.listHistoricalMemoryWarnings deliberately returns deprecated records. retrieveActivationCandidates merges them into ordinary memoryCandidates, while applyTemporalFilter excludes invalidated, superseded, and stale statuses but not deprecated. A deprecated record with a current temporal window can therefore remain selectable.

## Mechanism

Map the deprecated memory lifecycle to a concrete non-governing exclusion at the existing activation filter boundary. Preserve exact record identity and warning visibility; do not remove deprecated records from the historical-warning read model.

## Violated Invariant

Historical warnings may inform an explicit exclusion but can never regain current governing authority.

## Runtime Consumer

Activation context assembly and downstream DecisionPacket/Codex brief selection.

## Falsifier

A project-scoped deprecated MemoryRecord with a still-current temporal window appears in ContextAssembly.inclusions or DecisionPacket selected memory.

## Required Verification

One focused public-seam activation falsifier covering deprecated lifecycle, existing temporal/filter tests, narrow TypeScript typecheck, fresh PostgreSQL historical-warning traversal if repository wiring changes, Fallow if production package surface qualifies, diff check, independent Standards and Spec review, exact-SHA CI after publication.

## Proves

Deprecated retained memory remains visible only as non-governing warning/exclusion.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove source-claim lifecycle safety, all stale evidence recall, semantic usefulness, or product readiness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep the change at the existing activation authority filter; do not add a parallel lifecycle model or hide retained history.
design: Treat deprecated as a retained historical warning at the singular activation filter, preserving identity and visibility while preventing positive selection.

title: Filter non-current dissent edges from activation authority
description:
## What To Build

Keep historical SourceClaimEdges visible as typed relation evidence, but exclude every non-current dissent/support/supersession relation from semantic endpoint summaries consumed by activation.

## Priority

P1 — expired or invalidated dissent edges are reintroduced after canonical consensus filtering and can caveat current authority.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

At HEAD 032005cf, source-consensus-timeline.ts derives dissentingSourceClaimIds at line 485 from every incoming dissent edge without sourceClaimEdgeIsCurrent. activation-engine.ts line 756 consumes that unfiltered list as acceptedDissentingSourceClaimIds and filters only whether the endpoint claim is current. A Node 22 pure repro with two accepted current decision-supported claims and a contradicts edge whose validUntil equals now produced timeline state current_authority and relation temporal status historical, yet activation reassessment returned caveated with accepted_with_dissenting_source_claims.

## Mechanism

Derive activation-facing semantic relation endpoint IDs only from edges whose shared temporal assessment is current. Preserve all edges in relationEvidence with typed historical or invalid status; do not delete history or add a second inequality.

## Violated Invariant

A before-valid, expired, invalidated, equal-boundary, or malformed SourceClaimEdge cannot change current authority even when both endpoint claims remain current.

## Runtime Consumer

Activation authority assessment, ContextAssembly, DecisionPacket selection, source search consensus readback.

## Steps to Reproduce

Persist two accepted current decision-supported claims A and B. Connect A to B with contradicts and validUntil equal to now. Build the consensus timeline, then perform the activation authority reassessment from its endpoint summaries. Timeline relationEvidence is historical, but B changes from current_authority to caveated.

## Falsifier

Two independently current accepted claims connected only by a non-current contradicts edge cause the target to become caveated or excluded.

## Reproduction Command

rtk mise exec node@22.23.1 -- pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/activation/__tests__/index.test.ts -t non-current dissent

## Acceptance Criteria

At validUntil equal to now, validUntil before now, invalidatedAt equal to now, future validFrom, and malformed temporal metadata, the target remains uncaveated current authority and packet-selected; the relation remains visible only as typed non-current relationEvidence. Current dissent still caveats exactly once.

## Required Verification

Focused Core timeline and harness activation tests under Node 22, persisted PostgreSQL activation packet smoke with exact IDs, producer and consumer typechecks, Fallow, diff check, and independent Standards/Spec review.

## Proves

Non-current relation metadata cannot be reintroduced into activation authority through timeline endpoint summaries.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove endpoint truth, semantic adequacy of a current dissent relation, ideal TTL, or universal history recall.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail closed by omitting non-current semantic influence while preserving historical relation evidence; never normalize an invalid timestamp into current authority.

## Affected Files / Packages

Core source consensus timeline and tests; harness activation engine and tests; DB activation smoke only if needed for persisted packet proof.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.136.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.
design: Use the shared source relation temporal evaluator once when deriving activation-facing endpoint summaries; preserve the complete edge only in typed relationEvidence.
acceptance_criteria: Non-current dissent edges never caveat current endpoint claims or persisted packet selection; current dissent behavior and historical relation readback remain exact.
notes: Fixed the alternate expired-dissent authority path at the canonical source consensus read-model boundary. supportingSourceClaimIds, dissentingSourceClaimIds, and supersedesSourceClaimIds now derive only from SourceClaimEdges whose shared temporal assessment is current; full unfiltered relationEvidence remains persisted with typed current/historical/invalid status. Core falsifier matrix covers future validFrom, expired and equal validUntil, equal invalidatedAt, malformed and non-string metadata with both endpoint claims current, while asserting retained historical evidence. Harness exercises the real retrieve-consensus-activation reassessment path and a live current dissent control. Fresh PostgreSQL activation smoke adds an independently current decision-linked peer and equal-boundary contradicts edge, proves governing claim remains exact packet/brief/SourceDecisionEdge authority, and reports zero historical dissent edge packet refs. Independent Standards and Spec reviews clean. Published commit 41c6655b3510a0ad5f9ffaffa379ad3b31be4a1f; exact KRN CI run 29464707132 completed success across Linux fast, DB, security, and macOS disposable PostgreSQL. Proves non-current relations cannot populate current semantic endpoint summaries or caveat activation/packet authority. Does not prove relation or endpoint truth, ideal TTL, complete historical recall, or truthful CLI formatting of retained temporal evidence; the latter remains reax.

title: Quarantine legacy mixed-claim graph edges
description:
## What To Build

Add a forward PostgreSQL migration that snapshots every source_claim_edges row incident to a SourceClaim quarantined for claim_chunk_artifact_mismatch, then deletes that edge before it can affect current consensus or ranking. Extend the 0029 upgrade fixture with a coherent peer and a current supported SourceClaimEdge.

## Priority

P1 — quarantined legacy mixed-artifact claims can still influence a coherent neighbor through retained graph edges.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

Migration 0030 quarantines and deletes source_decision_edges but never source_claim_edges. It resets the bad claim to proposed/chunkless. ## Steps to Reproduce

The legacy edge survives migration 0030 and can populate sourceClaimEdgeInfluence for the peer.

## Mechanism

One append-only correction migration snapshots affected SourceClaimEdges in source_authority_quarantines with exact endpoint/provenance metadata, deletes the live edges, and proves current readback cannot observe their influence.

## Violated Invariant

A record contracted out of source authority cannot retain an incident relation that changes another candidate's governing rank or consensus.

## Runtime Consumer

## Falsifier

After upgrading a pre-0030 accepted mixed-artifact claim linked by a current supported SourceClaimEdge to a coherent peer, the edge remains readable or produces sourceClaimEdgeInfluence/rank change for the peer.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Required Verification

Focused migration test on disposable PostgreSQL, DB package typecheck, db:check, migration identity/readback, diff check, and independent review.

## Proves

Legacy mixed-artifact claim relations cannot remain governing after quarantine.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove relation truth, claim text/chunk semantic correspondence, zero-downtime migration, or designated-store cleanliness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Retain the immutable quarantine snapshot; do not reconstruct deleted graph authority without a new reviewed relation.

## Affected Files / Packages

DB forward migration/journal/snapshot, SourceClaim provenance migration proof, and only the smallest activation observer needed to prove no influence.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on md7u.36 and was discovered by independent review md7u.37.

## Human / Provider Authority

None.

title: Downgrade stale lifecycle evidence binding in readback
description:
## What To Build

Make evidence bundle packet-binding readback lifecycle-aware. A bundle admitted against an earlier ExecutionRun revision must retain its stored checksum and provenance as historical evidence without rendering bound_current for the current run revision.

## Priority

P1 — stale persisted evidence can be rendered as current DecisionPacket authority after an ExecutionRun transition.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

At HEAD ee25ee9c256c76587eb4eb7c32fc755eac885bc4, decisionPacketEvidenceBundleResource calls decisionPacketBindingReadbackFromMetadata with bundle metadata only. evidenceBundleFreshness compares timestamps only. The repository race test transitions an admitted capture from lifecycle revision 2 to 3 and proves a retry returns the original bundle, but no readback check downgrades its stored bound_current state. Independent review md7u.45 confirmed the current renderer can therefore emit packetBinding bound_current and freshness fresh_current for historical lifecycle identity.

## Steps to Reproduce

Persist a valid DecisionPacket-bound evidence bundle for an ExecutionRun at lifecycle revision N. Transition the same run to revision N+1. Read the aggregate through run show JSON or text. Observe that the bundle metadata-only classifier still emits packetBinding bound_current and timestamp freshness may emit fresh_current.

## Mechanism

At the aggregate/read-model boundary, compare the admitted stored sourceRunLifecycleRevision with the owning current ExecutionRun lifecycleRevision. Preserve stored checksum, evidence ref, generatedAt and revision for traceability, while exposing a typed stale or mismatch status that cannot govern current evidence. Do not rewrite historical rows and do not redefine timestamp freshness as authority.

## Violated Invariant

Evidence returned for a DecisionPacket is current only for the exact admitted ExecutionRun lifecycle identity; later run transitions must not leave old evidence labeled current.

## Runtime Consumer

run show JSON/text, DecisionPacket diagnostics, review, memory application, usefulness authorization and evidence return-channel operators.

## Falsifier

Persist valid packet-bound evidence at revision N, transition the run to N+1, then read the aggregate; packetBinding remains bound_current or timestamp freshness remains the only apparent current signal.

## Reproduction Command

rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/cli exec vitest run src/__tests__/run-run-show-command.test.ts -t "downgrades packet binding after lifecycle revision advances"

## Acceptance Criteria

After an admitted evidence capture at revision N and a run transition to N+1, run show JSON and text classify the bundle as stale or mismatched rather than bound_current/fresh_current; same-revision evidence remains bound_current; legacy metadata stays explicitly legacy_unknown.

## Required Verification

Focused Node-22 CLI readback test, PostgreSQL lifecycle transition readback proof, affected package typechecks, Fallow and diff-check, followed by independent review.

## Proves

Current readback cannot present an earlier lifecycle packet binding as current authority.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove command correctness, source truth, target-state freshness, provider clock accuracy or database immutability after readback.

## Rollback / Contraction

Prefer explicit stale/mismatch readback over mutating history or weakening lifecycle identity. If the current run revision is unavailable, fail closed to unknown rather than bound_current.

## Affected Files / Packages

Core evidence binding readback model as needed, CLI DecisionPacket read-model builders/renderers/tests, DB aggregate transition proof.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.45 after repository admission hardening mise-en-palace-md7u.200.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.

## Required Skills

diagnosing-bugs,implement,krn-memory-core,typescript-engineering,code-review
design: Compare persisted packet lifecycle identity with the owning current ExecutionRun during aggregate readback; preserve the stored historical identity as evidence, but never label it bound_current for a later revision.

title: Decide canonical memory application authority
description:
## Decision

Choose one canonical persisted owner for memory_record application evidence and define how memory_applications relates to usefulness_applications before changing either public store boundary.

## Rationale

Current code has two independently persisted application concepts for the same memory or knowledge consumer. One owns applicationId, appliedAt and target identity; the other owns outcome effects and counters. The split currently permits verification-before-application helped authority, so implementation cannot proceed safely until ownership and legacy migration are explicit.

## Alternatives Considered

1. Make usefulness_applications the canonical application fact for memory_record or knowledge subjects, then derive memory outcome effects only from later admitted feedback.
2. Evolve memory_applications into the canonical two-phase application fact with applicationId and appliedAt, exact target binding and later verification, then contract the generic usefulness application boundary for memory.
3. Keep both only if each has a distinct named consumer and an executable invariant preventing duplicate or contradictory authority.

## Current Evidence

At HEAD 7da15f07, usefulness_applications owns explicit applicationId, appliedAt, exact packet/run/task identity and target snapshot for knowledge and source_claim. Separately, memory_applications owns memory_record outcome, counters and effects but has only createdAt. DrizzleMemoryRepository validates an already-persisted verification bundle before inserting a helped MemoryApplication, so verification can precede application and still increment positiveFeedbackCount. The memory-governance smoke intentionally exercises that order. The direct CLI rejects helped and points to the two-phase evidence return channel, while its usage still advertises direct helped persistence.

## Runtime Consumer

MemoryRepository, HarnessRunRepository, evidence capture return channel, MemoryApplication readback, FeedbackDelta, positive and negative counters, maintenance, ranking and counter rebuild.

## Falsifier

A successful verifier captured before any exact persisted memory application can later authorize helped or increase positiveFeedbackCount, or one packet and memory subject can produce two independent application identities with different authority.

## Does Not Prove

Choosing an owner does not prove semantic causality, verifier adequacy, source truth, or live usefulness.

## Authority

Repository product and architecture authority; no external provider or human-only decision is required unless the migration changes retained historical meaning.

## Required Skills

domain-modeling,code-review

## Required Skills
domain-modeling,code-review
design: Prefer one canonical application fact with appliedAt and packet/subject/target identity; model outcome and later verification separately, preserve legacy rows as distinguishable history, and remove contradictory direct helped guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Record one canonical owner and migration or contraction rule; pre-application verification cannot authorize helped at any public repository seam; direct CLI help and store behavior use the same selected-used-helped language; existing historical rows remain readable without governing current counters.
notes:
Independent .58 Standards review added a second temporal falsifier: authorizeDecisionPacketUsefulness reconstructs a checksum from callerPacketGeneratedAt, so a caller can choose a future valid ISO timestamp and persist a memory application before its claimed packet issuance. memory_applications stores packetGeneratedAt only in metadata and has no createdAt >= packetGeneratedAt constraint; mapper and counter rebuild can still classify it packet_bound. The canonical-owner decision and follow-on migration must make packet issuance time first-class and reject future-bound application before application, counter, effects or outbox writes. This does not replace the broader issuance-seam follow-up pk2o; it is the memory authority consumer invariant.
Decision fixed point published in commit dc8f4ecdac5338dff7e56906928fd445de18e45d. ADR 0003 now chooses usefulness_applications as the sole post-cutover application ledger for memory_record and source_claim, with exact persisted issuance, packetGeneratedAt <= appliedAt, target identity, and later FeedbackDelta-owned effects. The cutover contracts persisted memory record apply, treats all memory_applications and historical knowledge application rows as non-governing readable history, and rebuilds current counters only from post-cutover exact application-bound outcomes. ADR 0004 now retains generic DB-owned application/feedback idempotency and explicitly supersedes the old memory_applications authority. Initial independent reviews found present-tense drift, undecided writer/cutover, contradictory falsifier, ADR conflict, and missing issuance-time owner; all were fixed. Final Spec and Standards reviews are clean. Exact pushed CI 29412713743 passed all four Linux, DB, macOS Node22 disposable PostgreSQL, and policy jobs. This decision does not claim the migration is implemented; current gaps are explicit and move to the md7u.59-.65 implementation chain plus issuance seam pk2o.
close_reason: Canonical memory application owner, cutover, temporal issuance rule, legacy contraction and exact-once effect ownership recorded in ADRs at dc8f4ecd; independent reviews and exact CI 29412713743 are green.

A current application subject exists that can never be selected and successfully authorized by the current packet.

title: Replace retired pnpm audit endpoints with bulk advisory gate
description:
## What To Build

The security gate must fail on high/critical advisories or an unverifiable scanner response, not permanently fail because its transport is retired.

GitHub KRN CI dependency, secret, and license policy job.

A committed lockfile with a known high advisory passes, or registry/network/non-JSON failure exits zero; a clean verifiable bulk report exits nonzero.

## Does Not Prove

Registry truth, undisclosed vulnerabilities, malicious lockfile edits, or dependency runtime safety.

description:
## What To Build

Replace the ambiguous KRN agent instruction surface with a compact repo contract and a polished, collision-free skill set that reliably routes planning, implementation, diagnosis, review, source decisions, target-repo work, and advisory external review.

## Consumer

Current repo skill review found broad descriptions, missing branch-specific stop gates, stale fixture-catalog ritual, and no explicit user/model invocation design.

## Violated Invariant

One repeated workflow must have one unambiguous trigger, one procedural owner, checkable completion criteria, and evidence that the workflow changed behavior. Repo guidance must route to skills instead of duplicating them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No repo-local skill name collides with an active global skill name.
- Root AGENTS.md is compact, KRN-specific, positive-form, RTK-correct, and routes every repeated workflow to one skill.
- Every repo-local skill explicitly chooses implicit or explicit invocation and has matching agents/openai.yaml metadata.
- Implementation work composes pre-code seam selection, one red-green vertical slice, focused verification, independent Standards and Spec review, and owned publication state without turning all work into multi-agent ceremony.
- Diagnosis, review, domain, source, target-repo, Beads, and external-review branches each have checkable mode-specific stop conditions.
- Practitioner input from current mattpocock/skills and official Codex mechanics is mapped to KRN mechanisms, consumers, falsifiers, and does-not-prove boundaries.
- Claude second opinion is advisory, secret-safe, bounded, and invalid unless factual findings cite current repo evidence that survives deterministic local validation.

## Proves

The checked-in instruction surface is collision-free, internally coherent, and exercises representative workflows predictably in the tested Codex environment.

## Does Not Prove

Prompt artifacts cannot guarantee every future model invocation, eliminate all code defects, prove broad product readiness, or replace deterministic tests, typecheck, DB smokes, Fallow, review, or human product decisions.

## Rollback / Contraction

title: Own ExecutionRun lifecycle event identity at the transition boundary
description:
## What To Build

Make lifecycle events repository-derived records of the committed ExecutionRun transition. Bind each event to from status, to status, and resulting lifecycle revision; remove or contract the unguarded generic append seam, and define exact same-state retry behavior.

## Priority

P1 — caller-authored or independently appended events can contradict the run state and cannot identify the lifecycle revision they claim to observe.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

UpdateExecutionRunStatusInput accepts an arbitrary RunEventInput and updateExecutionRunStatus copies its type, message, and payload after the row update without storing the resulting lifecycle revision. DrizzleEventLedgerRepository is exported through the public adapters entrypoint and appendRunEvent inserts arbitrary events without a run lock or expected revision; Fallow currently exempts that unused method. A same-state retry returns the row without persisting or explicitly classifying the supplied event.

## Steps to Reproduce

Transition a running run to succeeded while supplying an event that claims failure, or call appendRunEvent directly with an arbitrary sequence and payload. Read observations and see an event that conflicts with the committed lifecycle or has no revision identity. Retry the same state with a new event sequence and observe silent discard.

## Mechanism

Derive one typed lifecycle event from the locked current row and successful transition result. Persist from status, to status, and resulting revision in the same transaction. Remove appendRunEvent if it has no owner, or require a distinct non-lifecycle event type with explicit revision authority. Return an explicit idempotent retry classification.

## Violated Invariant

A lifecycle event is an immutable audit record of exactly one committed ExecutionRun revision and cannot contradict or bypass that revision.

## Runtime Consumer

Run observations, operator audit, replay, DecisionPacket freshness diagnostics, evidence authorization diagnostics, and lifecycle smokes.

## Falsifier

A succeeded row can receive a failure lifecycle event, an event can be appended without expected revision authority, or a same-state retry silently consumes a distinct event identity.

## Reproduction Command

Run focused real-PostgreSQL lifecycle and event-ledger tests with conflicting event payloads, direct append, and same-state retry cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

Lifecycle events are derived from the committed transition, identify the resulting revision, and cannot be appended through an unguarded public seam; same-state retry behavior is explicit and deterministic.

## Required Verification

Red real-PostgreSQL falsifiers, Node-22 focused tests, root typecheck, Fallow, Standards and Spec review, and diff check.

## Proves

Repository-owned lifecycle events match the ExecutionRun revision committed in the same transaction.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove external work occurred, provider clock accuracy, semantic truth of non-lifecycle observations, or safety from an unrestricted database principal.

## Rollback / Contraction

Prefer one narrow typed lifecycle event over preserving a generic append API with no runtime owner.

## Affected Files / Packages

Core lifecycle repository types, DB harness and event-ledger repositories, run event schema or payload parser, observations, tests and Fallow configuration.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.149. Timestamp projection remains owned by mise-en-palace-md7u.198.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,domain-modeling,krn-implementation,code-review
design: Treat the successful row transition as the sole owner of lifecycle event identity. Separate ordinary observations from lifecycle events rather than sharing caller-authored semantics.
acceptance_criteria: No lifecycle event can contradict or bypass its committed ExecutionRun revision; same-state retry has explicit deterministic semantics.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
Red and domain decision before implementation. Real-PostgreSQL focused lifecycle test failed because create and both transitions persisted caller-authored smoke event types, messages, and payloads instead of canonical created and transitioned facts. Independent unit probes also persisted running revision 2 with a run.failed event, allowed exported DrizzleEventLedgerRepository.appendRunEvent to append run.succeeded without run authority, and silently accepted a distinct same-state event while inserting nothing.

Smallest direct model: ExecutionRun owns two reserved event subtypes in the existing run_events timeline: execution_run.lifecycle.created with status and lifecycleRevision, and execution_run.lifecycle.transitioned with fromStatus, toStatus, and lifecycleRevision. Derive identity, message, severity, payload, timestamp, and sequence from persisted rows under the run transaction. Remove create initialEvent, update event and unused metadata inputs; return transitioned with run plus event or already_at_status with run. Remove the unused EventLedger interface/adapter/export/Fallow exemption. Ordinary evidence events remain generic but must reject reserved types and obtain sequence under the run lock. No migration or legacy backfill: old caller-authored rows remain noncanonical observations. Fixture cleanup must delete derived lifecycle events through execution-run linkage instead of contaminating canonical payload with smoke metadata. Non-proofs remain unrestricted SQL, historical reconstruction, external execution, and provider clocks.

comments.text:
Implementation complete before publication. ExecutionRun is now the sole lifecycle-event authority: creation emits execution_run.lifecycle.created with status and lifecycleRevision; successful updates emit execution_run.lifecycle.transitioned with fromStatus, toStatus, and resulting lifecycleRevision. title: Reject unauthorized evidence and feedback authority at the repository boundary
description:
## What To Build

Falsify and close direct repository paths that can persist DecisionPacket binding or usefulness-bearing feedback without current ExecutionRun authority. Cover createEvidenceBundle, createFeedbackDelta, and createEvalFeedbackDeltaOnce; generic and eval writes must not impersonate the authorized atomic evidence return channel.

## Priority

P1 — repository callers can mint authority-bearing evidence and feedback that downstream packet and ranking consumers trust.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

drizzle-harness-run-repository.ts createEvidenceBundle and createFeedbackDelta persist caller metadata without the run lock, project, lifecycle revision, or exact packet reconstruction used by createEvidenceFeedbackOnce. createEvalFeedbackDeltaOnce has the same persistence bypass. evidenceBundleProvesHelped accepts self-consistent raw checksum, generatedAt, and revision metadata without requiring canonical bound_current admission. Feedback metadata readers consume knowledgeUsefulnessOutcomes and sourceUsefulnessOutcomes as live packet caveats.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call each generic or eval repository method directly with a current run ID plus forged checksum, stale revision, cross-project identity, or knowledge usefulness metadata. Read the persisted bundle or list feedback for the forged subject and observe that downstream consumers accept the row without canonical packet admission.

## Mechanism

Define one repository-owned authority admission for packet-bound evidence and usefulness. Under one transaction, lock the run, validate project and lifecycle revision, reconstruct exact current packet identity, and admit bound_current metadata. Generic and eval paths must reject or strip authority-bearing binding and usefulness fields.

## Violated Invariant

Only evidence and usefulness admitted against the exact current DecisionPacket may affect helped proof, feedback selection, ranking, or maintenance.

## Runtime Consumer

EvidenceBundle readback, FeedbackDelta subject selection, MemoryApplication helped proof, DecisionPacket caveats, ranking, maintenance, and outbox consumers.

## Falsifier

A direct repository call with fabricated bound_current metadata or usefulness outcomes creates a row that renders current, proves helped, or changes next-run subject behavior.

## Reproduction Command

Run focused real-PostgreSQL repository tests that call each generic and eval method directly with forged checksum, stale revision, cross-project identity, and usefulness metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

Direct generic or eval calls cannot create a bundle rendered as current or feedback that influences subject usefulness without canonical current packet admission; the authorized atomic evidence path still persists exactly once.

## Required Verification

Red real-PostgreSQL falsifiers, Node-22 focused tests, root typecheck, Fallow, Standards and Spec review, and diff check.

## Proves

Authority-bearing evidence and usefulness enter through one transactionally current repository boundary.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove command correctness, source truth, causal usefulness, historical packet reconstruction, or protection from an unrestricted database principal.

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep generic rows explicitly unbound and non-governing, or remove the public generic creators when no runtime owner remains.

## Affected Files / Packages

Core evidence binding and feedback metadata, harness repository contract and implementation, read-model consumers, database tests and smokes.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.149. Existing memory-application authority remains owned by mise-en-palace-md7u.59 through mise-en-palace-md7u.61.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,domain-modeling,krn-implementation,code-review
design: Use one deep repository admission seam for exact current packet authority. Keep unbound generic history structurally unable to influence usefulness.
acceptance_criteria: Forged generic and eval writes reject or remain explicitly non-governing; canonical atomic evidence admission succeeds once.
close_reason: Repository-owned current_v1 evidence/usefulness admission is enforced and independently verified; generic/eval forgery paths are structurally non-governing; exact-SHA CI 29367817906 is green at 15b6ecee.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text:
Current-HEAD map and smallest authority decision before edits. The issue prose is stale only about createEvidenceBundle locking: .201 now serializes its event sequence on the run, but it still copies caller packet metadata. The larger live falsifier is confirmed: createEvidenceFeedbackOnce checks project, lifecycle revision, and self-consistent metadata shape, while exact checksum reconstruction and selected-subject authorization live only in CLI. A direct repository caller can therefore forge the supposedly canonical channel. Generic captureIdentity and evalExecutionIdentity metadata can also pre-seed exactly-once lookups.

One direct model: the core aggregate-to-DecisionPacket contract becomes the packet authority projection used by issuance, CLI preflight, and the DB repository. The diagnostic DecisionPacketReadModel remains explanatory and is not an authority model. CreateEvidenceFeedbackOnce receives an explicit optional DecisionPacket claim plus typed usefulness outcomes outside generic metadata. Under the existing advisory lock and ExecutionRun row lock, the repository validates stored project, preserves historical retry semantics, validates the expected lifecycle revision for a new chain, reconstructs the exact current packet for the claimed generatedAt, validates checksum and selected subjects/evidence refs, and only then persists canonical binding/usefulness. A present invalid claim rejects atomically. No claim persists explicitly unbound evidence and no governing usefulness or maintenance.

Persisted governing rows receive one versioned repository admission marker, decisionPacketAuthorityAdmission=current_v1, together with validated bound_current identity. Binding state without that marker is historical/self-reported and non-governing; there is no backfill. Generic createEvidenceBundle strips all packet/identity fields, cannot accept captureIdentity, and writes explicit unbound history. Generic createFeedbackDelta strips packet admission and both usefulness arrays. Eval exactly-once gains an expected lifecycle revision, validates the run project for new or existing calls, uses the existing capture_identity uniqueness boundary with a repository-owned eval namespace, and persists only unbound candidate/history metadata. The canonical capture namespace rejects that eval prefix.

Governing consumers require both admitted current binding and exact identity: evidenceBundleProvesHelped, usefulness metadata readers used by selection/DecisionPacket/maintenance, and usefulness subject SQL. Candidate-only feedback remains available independently. title: Isolate source-authority read-only proof from parallel DB cleanup
description:
## What To Build

Make the controlled source-authority integrity read-only proof independent of parallel marker-scoped fixture cleanup in the shared PostgreSQL test database.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

KRN CI run 29339693328 job 87107880775 failed because source-authority-integrity-readiness.test.ts compared the entire source_artifacts table before and after inspection: expected 11, received 10. The test owns exactly 10 artifacts and passes alone 3/3, so the eleventh row was a foreign fixture removed concurrently. source-authority-write-boundary.test.ts performs marker-scoped artifact cleanup in the same parallel suite.

## Mechanism

Compare the existing fixtureResidueCount for the unique smokeId before and after inspection. Retain the exact mismatched-claim row readback and report.readOnly assertion. The runtime inspector itself opens a PostgreSQL repeatable read read only transaction and verifies transaction_read_only.

## Violated Invariant

A test falsifier must observe only writes caused by the unit under test, not unrelated parallel fixture cleanup.

## Runtime Consumer

The DB verification CI profile and source-authority integrity readiness proof.

## Falsifier

The focused file passes alone while the full parallel suite changes an unrelated global table count.

## Required Verification

Focused real PostgreSQL test, full DB suite on a fresh database, Node 22 typecheck, Fallow changed-files gate, exact-SHA CI.

## Proves

The read-only inspector leaves every marker-owned fixture row and the exact invalid claim identity unchanged.

## Does Not Prove

It does not serialize unrelated test writers or prove production writer serialization; PostgreSQL enforces the inspected transaction as read only.

## Rollback / Contraction

Do not serialize the suite or change production code. Revert to a disposable database only if a future proof genuinely requires a globally quiescent database.

## Affected Files / Packages

packages/db/src/__tests__/source-authority-integrity-readiness.test.ts

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.
design: Use the existing marker-scoped fixtureResidueCount before and after inspection; retain exact row readback and the runtime read-only transaction proof.

title: Persist coherent timestamps for direct planned-to-terminal runs
description:
## What To Build

Persist the validated startedAt when a planned ExecutionRun transitions directly to blocked or cancelled, or contract the legal matrix so that direct planned-to-terminal transitions are rejected.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

validateExecutionRunTransition accepts planned→blocked/cancelled and requires a coherent startedAt, but updateExecutionRunStatus writes startedAt only when next status is running. A legal direct terminal transition can therefore commit completedAt with NULL startedAt.

## Mechanism

Keep one lifecycle matrix and one persistence projection: every timestamp accepted by transition validation must be written atomically with status, lifecycle revision, and the lifecycle event.

## Violated Invariant

A terminal ExecutionRun reached through a legal transition has coherent persisted startedAt/completedAt matching the validated transition.

## Runtime Consumer

ExecutionRun readback, DecisionPacket freshness, lifecycle operators, and audit/replay consumers.

## Falsifier

planned→blocked or planned→cancelled succeeds while persisted startedAt remains NULL.

## Reproduction Command

Run the focused real-PostgreSQL ExecutionRun lifecycle test with a direct planned→blocked/cancelled case and assert exact timestamp readback.

## Acceptance Criteria

The direct transition either persists both validated timestamps or is rejected by the domain matrix; row, revision, and event remain atomic.

## Required Verification

Node-22 focused repository tests, real PostgreSQL smoke, typecheck, Fallow changed-files gate, and diff check.

## Proves

Persisted lifecycle timestamps match the accepted domain transition for direct terminal outcomes.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove external work occurred, provider clock accuracy, or packet-write concurrency.

## Rollback / Contraction

Prefer rejecting the transition over storing an incoherent terminal row if direct planned-to-terminal semantics are not product-owned.

## Affected Files / Packages

ExecutionRun transition validation/persistence and focused PostgreSQL repository tests.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered while reviewing md7u.147 after md7u.146 closed.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human/provider authority.

## Required Skills

diagnosing-bugs,domain-modeling,krn-implementation,code-review

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,domain-modeling,krn-implementation,code-review
acceptance_criteria: Direct planned→blocked/cancelled either persists validated startedAt/completedAt atomically or is rejected; revision/event behavior remains coherent.
close_reason: Direct planned-to-blocked and planned-to-cancelled transitions now persist validated startedAt and completedAt atomically with revision and event. Red and green real-PostgreSQL proof, full fresh-DB verification, Fallow, dual review, advisory review, and exact implementation CI are recorded.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text: Independent .149 review reconfirmed the exact fixed-point counterexample: planned to blocked or cancelled validates caller startedAt for completedAt ordering, then updateExecutionRunStatus persists startedAt only for target running, so the committed terminal row has NULL startedAt. This is a must-fix current-code defect; keep row, revision, completedAt, startedAt, and event atomic. Review also found strict ISO parsing as a separate low-priority owner .203.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text:
Implementation proof before commit. Domain decision: retain explicit planned to blocked or cancelled transitions because they retire an active planned EvidenceContract without inventing running; persist the already-required attempt startedAt rather than contract the matrix. Red real-PostgreSQL reproduction on fresh krn_m198_red_20260714_1814: focused test failed with blocked status, lifecycle revision 2, expected completedAt, and missing startedAt. Fix: updateExecutionRunStatus now writes input.startedAt only when the locked current row has no persisted start, so direct terminal transitions persist the validated timestamp while running to terminal cannot rewrite history.

Behavior proof: the focused real-PostgreSQL file passes 22 of 22. It covers exact startedAt and completedAt for both blocked and cancelled, revision 2, fresh aggregate readback, rejected completion-before-start leaving planned revision 1 and exactly no transition event, plus a differing startedAt on running to succeeded remaining unchanged. Full fresh-DB Node-22 verify:db passed all 32 migrations, readiness, Drizzle schema check, 29 DB files and 157 tests, required smokes, and retrieval-substrate, DecisionPacket return-loop, and target-repo evals. Root typecheck and Node-22 root typecheck passed. Fallow changed-files gate passed with dead code 0, duplication 0, and one inherited validateExecutionRunTransition complexity finding excluded; broad report remained dead/dupes 0 and health 1. Diff-check passed.

Independent Standards review: CLEAN. Independent Spec review: CLEAN. Requested claude-second-opinion-review skill remained unavailable; local Claude Code read-only fallback returned CLEAN and verified validation/persistence alignment, no running-start rewrite, and genuine event-count atomicity. Its only actionable-looking residual was closed by the final differing-start regression assertion. Advisory output was not a gate.

Proves: every startedAt accepted for the supported direct terminal transition is persisted atomically with status, lifecycle revision, completedAt, and event, while invalid ordering has no transition side effects. Does not prove external work began, provider clock accuracy, raw-SQL enforcement, event semantic authority owned by .201, strict ISO parsing owned by .203, or packet-write concurrency. title: Serialize fallback project initialization across concurrent CLI processes
description:
## What To Build

Make fallback workspace/project resolution idempotent when two independent CLI processes start against the same migrated database before the default project exists.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

The source import concurrency falsifier must pre-create defaultWorkspaceSlug/defaultProjectSlug before Promise.all. The earlier unseeded run exposed a separate project-bootstrap race, so the import test now isolates import serialization instead of proving project initialization.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create and migrate a disposable PostgreSQL database without initializing the fallback project.
2. Launch two independent persisted CLI processes without an explicit project against that database.
3. Observe whether both resolve the same fallback project and whether exactly one workspace/project remains.

## Mechanism

Reproduce the empty-store race, then make the project repository or runtime resolution converge on one workspace/project under the existing unique authority boundary. Do not add compatibility aliases or process-local locking.

## Runtime Consumer

Every persisted CLI command using fallback project resolution on a newly initialized store.

## Falsifier

Two independent processes resolving the same absent fallback workspace/project produce a unique violation, different project IDs, or one failed caller.

## Required Verification

Red-capable two-process disposable PostgreSQL test on an empty migrated database, exact workspace/project counts, Node 22 typecheck and exact-SHA CI.

## Does Not Prove

Does not prove source import graph idempotency, connected-repo resolution, or cross-database identity.
design: Converge concurrent fallback project creation at the database authority boundary and return the same persisted identity to both callers.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent fallback resolutions on an empty migrated PostgreSQL database both succeed, return one project identity, and leave exactly one workspace and one project.
close_reason: Fallback project initialization now serializes at workspace authority and exact-SHA CI is green.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text: Implemented and verified at commit 4d9a8f417d1fefea04d7c967995467bbe6943754. Red evidence: connected-path unit falsifier observed one unwanted fallback transaction; deterministic PostgreSQL same-workspace/different-project race observed statuses fulfilled/rejected. Fix: resolve explicit and connected projects before locking; only unresolved fallback enters one transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by global workspace slug identity, then re-runs resolution inside the transaction. Green evidence: database-runtime unit tests 7/7; source-decision-import-retry PostgreSQL tests 3/3; root typecheck, clean test typecheck, full workspace tests, required evals, Fallow report and changed-files gate, diff check, Beads validate/roundtrip/lint all passed. Independent Standards and Spec reviews report no P0/P1 and closure-ready. Exact-SHA KRN CI run 29294250792 passed all four jobs; DB log explicitly shows both concurrent first-use and same-workspace/different-project tests passed unskipped, 3/3 total. Proof: concurrent empty-store callers converge to one fallback identity, and workspace creation serializes before different child projects. Non-proof: source import graph idempotency, connected-repo semantics beyond bypassing the fallback lock, and cross-database identity.

title: Enforce canonical revision coverage for selected memory and source inclusions
description:
## What To Build

Require every selected memory_record or source_claim inclusion persisted in ContextAssembly to have a validated canonical revision token bound to that exact subject. Reject a selected canonical subject when metadata omits its token or carries a token for a different subject. Keep non-canonical projection subjects explicit and non-authoritative.

## Priority

P1 — the current revalidation boundary validates supplied tokens but can accept a canonical inclusion with no corresponding token.

## Mechanism

Derive canonical inclusion keys from ContextAssembly inclusions, compare them with the typed canonicalRevisionTokens set, fail closed on missing/duplicate/mismatched coverage, then lock and revalidate each covered row before insert.

## Violated Invariant

No selected canonical record reaches persisted context without a packet-bound current revision.

## Runtime Consumer

ContextAssembly, DecisionPacket, activation trace and later usefulness authorization.

## Falsifier

A memory_record or source_claim inclusion with absent, duplicate, wrong-subject, stale or incomplete revision metadata is persisted successfully.

## Reproduction Command

rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/db exec vitest run src/repositories/__tests__/drizzle-harness-run-repository.test.ts -t 'canonical revision coverage'

## Acceptance Criteria

The false-positive matrix fails closed before insert; valid memory/source coverage persists; non-canonical subjects remain explicitly non-authoritative; exact inclusion/token keys are asserted.

## Required Verification

Focused red/green DB repository tests, full db and harness tests, Node-22 typecheck, Fallow, diff-check and disposable PostgreSQL smoke.

## Proves

Selected canonical context subjects are bound to the revisions revalidated at persistence.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove global serializability, post-issuance immutability, source truth or live usefulness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail closed to an explicit persistence error; do not infer revisions from SearchDocument or other projections.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human/provider authority.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review

title: Diagnose repeated Ubuntu DB verification timeout
description:
## What To Build

Investigate and repair the canonical Ubuntu DB verification profile when the full verify:db chain reaches the portable deadline with exit 124, while the same commit's macOS fast and DB profiles pass.

## Priority

P1 — the required Linux DB gate is not reliably completing and the bounded timeout must not hide a slow or stuck smoke.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

GitHub Actions run 29262585641 on commit 101e03123c8e5e98c8b6d4bb9c9dd6dbadc657e8:
- macOS Node22 and disposable Postgres verification passed fast and DB profiles;
- Ubuntu DB readiness and smoke failed in verify:db with exit code 124;
- the same Ubuntu DB job failed with exit code 124 in run 29262370547 on commit 1e6f870790e7127523d29e0ae13df69f47e08add;
- the portable runner intentionally returns 124 after its bounded deadline.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run GitHub Actions KRN CI for commit 101e03123c8e5e98c8b6d4bb9c9dd6dbadc657e8.
2. Inspect job DB readiness and smoke, step DB verification profile.
3. Observe exit code 124 without a recorded responsible subcommand.

## Mechanism

Capture per-command duration and last completed gate in the Ubuntu DB profile, determine whether the timeout is caused by a slow smoke, a child-process leak, or an environment/resource condition, then either optimize the responsible gate or set a justified bounded deadline with proof.

## Violated Invariant

A canonical verification gate must either complete within its declared deadline or expose a typed, actionable failure; it must not repeatedly end as an unexplained timeout.

## Runtime Consumer

GitHub Ubuntu DB readiness gate and developers relying on verify:db.

## Falsifier

A clean exact-commit Ubuntu run repeats exit 124 without identifying a responsible subcommand, or a claimed fix still times out under the same bounded environment.

## Reproduction Command

GitHub Actions run 29262585641, job DB readiness and smoke, step DB verification profile; locally use real PostgreSQL and the exact committed verify:db command with the same deadline.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Red proof captures the exact subcommand, elapsed duration, environment and exit status.
2. Green proof completes the full Ubuntu DB profile on a clean exact commit.
3. Deadline remains bounded and process cleanup is verified.
4. No smoke is skipped, weakened, or converted to a mock.
5. macOS proof remains green.

## Required Verification

Independent Ubuntu GitHub run, real PostgreSQL, focused timing/fault test, package tests, Node22 typecheck, exact committed-range Fallow, diff-check, and full CI.

## Proves

The canonical Ubuntu DB profile is bounded, diagnosable and completing under the declared CI environment.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove product READY, designated-store integrity, live Codex usefulness, PostgreSQL major-version parity across providers, or every external runner configuration.

## Rollback / Contraction

Revert only timing instrumentation and the narrowly scoped deadline/profile changes; never remove DB smoke coverage to make the gate green.

## Native Dependencies

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.181 and is discovered from the portable deadline work.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review

title: Classify historical paired-trial fixture for full-history secret scans
description:
## What To Build

On a disposable clone, derive only secret-free provenance and exact match hash for the historical secret-shaped assignment in the paired-trial test history. If and only if it is demonstrably synthetic test data, add a path, pattern, and hash-bound baseline exception plus a behavior test. Otherwise leave the full-history scan failing and classify the workflow blocked.

## Priority

P1 - workflow_dispatch and scheduled security cannot reach a green result while this historical fixture is unresolved.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

Manual workflow_dispatch run 29254383741 used an empty provider base, fast and DB jobs passed, but Secret policy failed on packages/cli/src/__tests__/tracked-paired-live-codex-repair.test.ts with secret-shaped assignment. security-policy historySecretFindings scans root to HEAD for no-base events and exceptionMatches requires exact path, pattern, and SHA-256. security-baseline has no exception for that historical paired-trial path or historical match hash.

## Mechanism

Retain full-history security scanning. Permit only one reviewed synthetic historical marker through a content-addressed exception; all changed text, paths, patterns, and unknown history remain fail-closed.

## Violated Invariant

Every supported manual or schedule trigger either has a green full-history security proof or is explicitly blocked by a non-synthetic finding; no broad fallback reduction hides historic secrets.

## Runtime Consumer

CI security job, operators using workflow_dispatch, scheduled policy runs, and maintainers reviewing secret-history evidence.

## Falsifier

A changed marker, a matching-looking value at a different path, or an unreviewed historical secret passes; alternatively the controlled historical synthetic marker remains unexceptioned after classification.

## Reproduction Command

rtk env KRN_COMMIT_EVENT=workflow_dispatch KRN_COMMIT_BEFORE= KRN_COMMIT_PR_BASE= pnpm security:secrets

## Acceptance Criteria

A disposable Git-history test proves full-history scanning rejects an unreviewed marker and accepts only the classified exact historical synthetic marker. workflow_dispatch Secret policy is green if classification succeeds; otherwise the Bead is blocked with secret-free provenance and no range-policy weakening.

## Required Verification

Focused Node 22 security-policy test, schedule-equivalent local command, one manual GitHub workflow run, exact baseline hash evidence without printing the marker, typecheck, and diff-check.

## Proves

The reviewed synthetic historical fixture is bounded by exact content and cannot broaden the security allowlist or weaken full-history scanning.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove all repository history is credential-free, that an unknown marker is safe, external secret revocation, general provider availability, or product readiness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Remove only the new exact exception to restore fail-closed behavior. Never shorten the security range, disable history scanning, redact history, or add a broad pattern exception without separate authority.

## Affected Files / Packages

security-baseline.json, scripts/security-policy.mjs behavior tests, CI verification documentation, and historical paired-trial test provenance.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.176.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human authority is needed to classify demonstrably synthetic local test data. If provenance cannot establish that boundary, stop blocked; do not inspect or publish a possible credential.

## Required Skills

diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review
design: Keep Fallow head-parent, whitespace root, and security root policies separate. Treat baseline exceptions as exact content-bound security decisions, never as a range workaround.

title: Keep compile-time DecisionPacket paths from minting rejected authority
description:
## What To Build

Make compile-time DecisionPacket constructors preserve unsafe, stale, invalidated, and superseded exclusions as typed non-governing state. They must not populate formal rejectedPathIds without an AntiMemoryRecord or persisted SourceRejection.

## Priority

P1 — direct plan and eval brief paths can publish false rejected-path authority after the persisted builder is fixed.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

packages/harness/src/compiler/compile-harness-plan.ts lines 169 and 183 maps every context exclusion to rejectedPathIds. packages/cli/src/run-plan-command.ts line 796 renders that packet, and packages/cli/src/internal/eval/run-memory-advantage-eval.ts line 2124 consumes it. A direct current-head harness reproduction with one unsafe source_claim returns status=abstain, rejectedPathIds=[claim-unsafe], and sourceRejectionIds=[]; no formal negative evidence exists. packages/cli/src/decision-packet-engine.ts lines 263 and 299 repeats the broad constructor for its pre-selection eval brief.

## Mechanism

Use one typed negative-state mapping for compile-time packet construction. Anti-memory may remain a rejected path; source exclusions remain explicit exclusions or superseded paths, while formal SourceRejection stays separate.

## Violated Invariant

Missing formal negative evidence cannot be hidden by relabeling an unsafe candidate as rejected.

## Runtime Consumer

run plan execution brief and the bounded memory-advantage evaluation brief.

## Falsifier

One unsafe source_claim exclusion, zero AntiMemoryRecord, and zero SourceRejection yields a non-empty rejectedPathIds list.

## Reproduction Command

rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/compiler/__tests__/index.test.ts with an unsafe compile-time packet fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria

Unsafe, stale, invalidated, and superseded source exclusions stay explicit and non-governing; rejectedPathIds contains only formal anti-memory paths; sourceRejectionIds remains empty unless backed by a real SourceRejection; plan and eval brief tests cover the boundary.

## Required Verification

Focused harness and CLI tests, rtk proxy pnpm typecheck, changed-range Fallow, git diff --check, and an independent Standards and Spec review.

## Proves

Compile-time DecisionPacket consumers do not mint formal rejected authority from context exclusions.

## Does Not Prove

This does not prove SourceRejection truth, persisted packet integrity, live Codex obedience, or universal negative coverage.

## Rollback / Contraction

Contract the compile-time packet to abstain with explicit exclusions rather than retain an alias for rejected authority.

## Affected Files / Packages

packages/harness/src/compiler/compile-harness-plan.ts, packages/cli/src/decision-packet-engine.ts, run-plan and eval tests.

## Native Dependency Edges

Parent remediation map: mise-en-palace-md7u.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority is required.

## Required Skills

diagnosing-bugs, krn-implementation, code-review, domain-modeling
