title: Make source import retry JSON readback deterministic in Node 22
description:
## What To Build

Make the source-decision import retry test and its JSON-output boundary deterministic when the root suite runs with a configured PostgreSQL store under Node 22.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

GitHub Actions run 29216988539 for 8d4f123db5d12f305c6785aea638802e285d13fe failed only in DB verification. The Node-22 root suite reached 86/87 files and 570/571 tests, then source-decision-import-retry.test.ts failed with JSON.parse: Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 2035, line 55. The failing parser slices stdout from the source_decision_import JSON object and assumes nothing follows it. The focused test passes locally on Node 26, which does not prove Node-22 behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a fresh migrated PostgreSQL database as KRN_DATABASE_URL and run pnpm --filter @krn/cli exec vitest run src/__tests__/source-decision-import-retry.test.ts under Node 22. The canonical red proof is the DB job in GitHub Actions run 29216988539.

## Mechanism

Capture the actual independent child-process stdout on a red Node-22 reproduction. Fix the narrow protocol/test boundary so --json has one parseable typed response or the test consumes the explicitly framed response without silently accepting arbitrary trailing output.

## Violated Invariant

The source decision import --json contract must be deterministic and machine-parseable across independent CLI processes; a configured DB test environment cannot turn a green retry/idempotency test into an output-framing failure.

## Runtime Consumer

Source import retry/idempotency verification, the DB verification profile, and callers consuming the JSON CLI response.

## Falsifier

A configured Node-22 PostgreSQL run of source-decision-import-retry.test.ts fails to parse one of its child CLI results, or a fixed parser accepts arbitrary non-protocol trailing output.

## Reproduction Command

Run the focused test with a fresh configured PostgreSQL database under the repository Node-22 toolchain, then run the root test plus the post-suite db:ready sequence.

## Acceptance Criteria

The focused Node-22 test is repeatable and green; the JSON boundary has an explicit exact framing rule; the full configured-store root suite and post-suite readiness are green; no unrelated CLI output is hidden or discarded without an asserted contract.

## Required Verification

Red/green focused Node-22 proof, relevant CLI tests, root typecheck, changed-range Fallow, fresh configured PostgreSQL full root suite then db:ready, and exact-commit GitHub CI.

## Proves

At the tested Node-22 environment, this retry path returns a deterministic machine-readable response and no longer blocks the configured-store root suite.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove all CLI commands have stable JSON framing, all runtime environments match GitHub Actions, or source-import semantic correctness beyond the retry path.

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep the CLI JSON contract strict. If protocol framing cannot be made explicit, do not weaken the parser by accepting arbitrary trailing text.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human decision is required; GitHub Actions Node-22 output is the canonical verification authority.

title: Leave no source-authority residue after DB-backed tests
description:
## What To Build

Make DB-backed tests leave their disposable store source-authority-clean, with a real regression proof that a full root test run does not poison subsequent readiness.

## Priority

P1 — a green test suite can leave a store that correctly fails the next readiness check, making local/CI proof order-dependent.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

On 2026-07-12, a fresh disposable PostgreSQL database was explicitly migrated, then the full root pnpm test completed green (85 files, 561 tests). The immediately following pnpm db:ready failed fail-closed with 15 Source authority violations: active search without canonical authority, captured evidence mismatch, claim/decision lifecycle mismatch, conflicting terminal review, governing edge without current reviewed decision, incomplete import lifecycle, missing terminal review, and project mismatch. The disposable database was dropped after capture. No existing Bead matched source-authority test cleanup, integrity violation cleanup, test residue, or these violation names.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create a fresh disposable PostgreSQL database; run pnpm db:migrate with its KRN_DATABASE_URL; run pnpm test with the same URL; then run pnpm db:ready with that URL. Observe that tests exit 0 while readiness exits nonzero with the captured integrity violations. Drop only that generated database.

## Mechanism

Identify the actual DB-backed test writers and their missing or incorrect lifecycle cleanup. Add the smallest ownership-bound teardown or database isolation so all rows created by the suite are removed before the shared disposable store is reused.

## Violated Invariant

A test suite that reports success must leave its explicitly supplied disposable store ready for the next independent verifier; test fixtures cannot persist canonical authority violations.

## Runtime Consumer

Developers, CI DB verification, local test/verify sequencing, source-authority readiness, and future integration tests.

## Falsifier

A freshly migrated disposable DB passes readiness, root pnpm test exits 0, and then readiness reports one or more source-authority violations or changed fixture residue.

## Reproduction Command

Create a fresh disposable PostgreSQL database; run pnpm db:migrate with its KRN_DATABASE_URL; run pnpm test with the same URL; then run pnpm db:ready with that URL. Capture the exact violation count before dropping only that generated database.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fresh migrated disposable database remains readiness-clean after the full root suite; all test-created authority rows are removed or isolated; Node-22 PostgreSQL proof asserts zero source-authority violations after the suite; no readiness rule is weakened and no designated-store data is touched.

## Required Verification

Focused red/green real-PostgreSQL regression, full root test suite against a generated DB, post-suite db:ready, exact cleanup/count assertions, root typecheck, Fallow, and canonical Node-22 CI.

## Proves

The tested suite preserves the source-authority integrity boundary of its disposable store across a real next-verifier handoff.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove designated-store data correctness, source truth, backup recovery, production isolation, or that unrelated external stores are clean.

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep readiness fail-closed. If a safe ownership boundary cannot be shown, isolate the test database rather than deleting broad rows; never run repair/delete against a designated store.

## Affected Files / Packages

DB and CLI integration tests, fixture cleanup helpers, source-authority writers, test setup/teardown, and verification scripts only as evidence requires.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.119 because readiness must first expose mutation-free integrity results.

## Human / Provider Authority

Autonomous only for generated disposable databases. Any investigation or repair of a designated persistent store is human/provider-gated.
design: Diagnose the exact writer first, then use the smallest ownership-bound teardown or per-test isolation. Do not weaken source-authority readiness or delete real store data.

title: Verify canonical Beads bootstrap from a fresh clone
description:
## What To Build

Perform the independent fresh-clone proof for the newly published canonical Beads history.

## Priority

P1 — publication is not useful until a new workspace can recover and navigate the same graph.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

Before remediation, the source workspace has 1,152 issues, 1,088 interactions, zero dependency cycles, zero orphans, and 38 ready tasks, while Git has no `refs/dolt/data`. The existing JSONL validators prove export consistency only; they do not prove canonical bootstrap or complete Dolt history.

## Mechanism

Clone the repository into a disposable path, run `bd bootstrap` against `refs/dolt/data`, and compare issue IDs, statuses, dependency edges, interaction history, blocked/ready frontiers, and representative `bd show` readback with the source snapshot.

## Violated Invariant

A canonical remote is complete only if an independent fresh workspace reconstructs the same navigable execution graph without treating JSONL as authority.

## Runtime Consumer

Fresh agents beginning with `bd prime` and operators recovering Beads after machine loss.

## Falsifier

Bootstrap uses the compatibility JSONL import, misses records/history/edges, changes blocked or ready membership, or cannot read representative existing and newly-created issue IDs.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk bd bootstrap`

## Acceptance Criteria

A clean clone bootstraps from `refs/dolt/data`, reports the same issues, dependencies, interactions, statuses and ready frontier as the source snapshot, and passes graph, lint, validate and round-trip checks without compatibility import.

## Required Verification

Run source/clone `bd stats`, `bd graph check`, `bd dep cycles`, `bd orphans`, `bd lint`, `pnpm beads:validate`, `pnpm beads:roundtrip`, and representative `bd show`/first-`bd ready` comparisons; record remote ref identity.

## Proves

At the tested ref and Beads version, canonical cross-machine bootstrap preserves the observable durable graph needed by a fresh agent.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove long-term GitHub retention, disaster recovery from every corruption mode, multi-writer conflict handling, or semantic correctness of each ticket.

## Rollback / Contraction

Delete the disposable clone only; if any mismatch appears, leave publication remediation open and do not normalize by importing JSONL.

## Affected Files / Packages

Disposable clone, `.beads/config.yaml`, Git `refs/dolt/data`, Beads bootstrap/readback and validation commands.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on `mise-en-palace-md7u.185`; serves as independent proof/review for the durability chain.

## Human / Provider Authority

No privileged human authority; public Git provider availability is required for readback, but no provider mutation is authorized.

## Required Skills

beads,target-repo-testing,code-review

title: Replace GNU timeout with a portable Node process deadline
description:
## What To Build

Add one tested Node runner that forwards stdout/stderr/exit, sends TERM then KILL after bounded grace, and use it in verify:db.

## Priority

P1 — the declared macOS platform cannot run the canonical DB profile with stock tools

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

README.md:112 and CONTRIBUTING.md:21 declare Linux/macOS/WSL POSIX support; `package.json:88` invokes GNU `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s`, which is not a stock macOS command/interface. `repository-policy.test.ts:224-259` simulates platform strings but never executes canonical profiles on macOS; CI runs Ubuntu only.

## Mechanism

Replace shell-specific timeout with a Node-owned process-group deadline wrapper and execute the canonical profiles on a real macOS runner/shell matrix.

## Violated Invariant

Every declared supported platform can run the same canonical verification entry points or support is contracted honestly.

## Runtime Consumer

Contributors/agents on macOS and local/CI verification parity.

A clean stock macOS checkout passes platform:check but `pnpm verify:db` fails before KRN checks because timeout is missing/incompatible.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk pnpm verify:db` on a stock macOS runner after `rtk pnpm platform:check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Success/failure/timeout/signal/process-child cases are deterministic on Linux/macOS; canonical command remains unchanged semantically.

## Required Verification

Node unit/integration process tests under bash/sh/zsh and Linux/macOS.

## Proves

Declared macOS environment can execute canonical gates with bounded processes.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove every filesystem/container setup, production deployment or Windows support.

If macOS DB profile cannot be supported, contract docs/platform checker explicitly; never keep a simulated green claim.

title: Bind paired-trial artifact to observed fair execution
description:
## What To Build

## Priority

`tracked-paired-live-codex-repair.ts:161-185` hashes all files including materialized `.git` and omits file modes; `:245-268` records manifest cliVersion/profileHash/permissions/maxTokens without verifying them and probes tools with full `process.env`; `:326-332` scores regardless of arm process exit and sets status from checker outcome only. ## Mechanism

Make the trial artifact bind source tree sans VCS metadata plus modes, observed executable/model/profile/permissions/budget/environment, one-shot attempt state, arm exit/timeout and pre/post patch/status before checker scoring.

## Does Not Prove

## Mechanism

Make the trial artifact bind source tree sans VCS metadata plus modes, observed executable/model/profile/permissions/budget/environment, one-shot attempt state, arm exit/timeout and pre/post patch/status before checker scoring.

title: Prove Fallow exact range in local schedule and manual profiles
description:
## What To Build

Run current local profile and controlled workflow_dispatch/schedule-equivalent execution, asserting printed base/head/file count and injected defect behavior.

## Priority

P1 — local scheduled and manual Fallow fallback audits repository history instead of the intended committed change

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`scripts/resolve-committed-range.mjs:10-15` selects root when no PR/push base exists; `run-fallow-ci.mjs:38` consumes it. Executed local command used root `8c3e667…`, 713 changed files and failed on 3 complexity/5 duplication findings; `KRN_COMMIT_EVENT=push KRN_COMMIT_BEFORE=cbfbacd4` used one file and passed. Workflow has no schedule/manual runs; repository-policy tests cover Fallow only PR/push.

## Mechanism

Give Fallow an explicit consumer-owned fixed point for local/schedule/manual execution while preserving separate full-history secret policy; never infer one shared range policy for every gate.

## Violated Invariant

Changed-files gate evaluates the exact submitted/current commit range on every trigger and reports its base/head.

## Runtime Consumer

Local verify:fast, push/PR/schedule/workflow_dispatch CI and reviewers.

## Falsifier

No-event/schedule/manual run silently selects root and fails/passes on unrelated historical debt.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci`; compare `rtk env KRN_COMMIT_EVENT=push KRN_COMMIT_BEFORE=cbfbacd4 pnpm quality:fallow:ci`.

## Acceptance Criteria

Correct changed defect fails in every path; unrelated historical baseline does not; exact current range passes after removal.

## Required Verification

Node-22 local profile plus GitHub run/API readback for manual trigger; schedule simulation if calendar event unavailable.

## Proves

Fallow gate result is bound to a deterministic explicit range for every supported trigger.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove full-repo health, secret history coverage or semantic correctness of Fallow findings.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail with actionable missing-base error rather than silently scan root; keep full report as advisory separate command.

## Affected Files / Packages

Range resolver, Fallow runner, workflow env, verification docs and repository-policy tests.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.174.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human/provider authority for code; manual GitHub run proof needs provider access already available.

diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review

title: Prove one winner for concurrent ExecutionRun transitions
description:
## What To Build

Run two connections attempting competing legal/illegal transitions and count rows/events/packet revisions.

## Priority

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`drizzle-harness-run-repository.ts:674` accepts arbitrary create status; update at `:705` uses WHERE id only, allows arbitrary timestamps, and does not reliably bind lifecycle revision. Schema `harness.ts:218` has no status/time checks. Executed planned/succeeded identity probe was unchanged when updatedAt stayed fixed.

## Mechanism

Define legal transition matrix, guarded expected-status update with coherent timestamps/event and lifecycle revision included in packet identity.

## Violated Invariant

One run has monotonic legal lifecycle; exactly one concurrent transition wins; packet/active contract identity changes with lifecycle.

## Runtime Consumer

DecisionPacket freshness, active EvidenceContract, events, evidence authorization and operators.

## Falsifier

terminal→running or running+completedAt succeeds; concurrent updates both win; lifecycle changes leave packet identity unchanged.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/db exec vitest run src/repositories/__tests__/drizzle-harness-run-repository.test.ts` with transition/race matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

Exactly one winner/event; loser gets typed conflict; timestamps and packet readback match winner.

## Required Verification

Node-22 PostgreSQL race smoke with deterministic barriers.

## Proves

Run lifecycle and packet issuance are temporally coherent and race-guarded.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove underlying external work occurred or provider clock accuracy.

## Rollback / Contraction

Reject unknown/illegal transitions; preserve legacy rows as invalid history rather than normalize silently.

ExecutionRun core/schema/repository/events, packet identity/read-model, EvidenceContract lifecycle tests.

title: Prove raw ingest isolation atomicity and temporal behavior
description:
## What To Build

Run two-project, same-input retry, concurrent, stale/current and fault cases on disposable PostgreSQL.

## Priority

P1 — exported raw ingest can leave partial graphs, drops stale history, and uses a collision-prone 32-bit identity

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`harness/src/corpus/raw-evidence-ingest.ts:62` uses FNV-1a 32-bit; `:90` rejects stale evidence before storage; `:163` performs three repository writes without one transaction. Executed probes found a real collision and artifact-only state after injected fault. No non-test runtime caller was found beyond export.

## Mechanism

First decide/contract the owner; if retained, use one transaction and deterministic SHA-256 span identity while preserving stale evidence as non-active history.

## Violated Invariant

An ingest surface has a named consumer; same input is atomic/idempotent; stale evidence is retained but cannot govern; identity is collision-resistant.

## Runtime Consumer

Currently tests/export only; potential source acquisition/import consumer must be named before retained implementation.

## Falsifier

Fault leaves artifact without projection, stale input leaves no history, or distinct payloads share checksum.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/corpus/__tests__/raw-evidence-ingest.test.ts` plus the recorded collision fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria

Exact per-project row counts, no partial graph, no shared authority and one historical stale readback.

## Required Verification

Node-22 DB smoke repeated once with exact IDs/counts.

## Proves

Retained raw ingest is owned, atomic, temporal and tamper-evident—or the unused surface is removed.

## Does Not Prove

It does not justify a crawler/broad ingest platform or prove source truth.

## Rollback / Contraction

Preferred contraction is remove/export-isolate if no runtime consumer; never harden speculative API without owner.

## Affected Files / Packages

Harness raw-evidence-ingest, repository transaction boundary, source schema/import tests and exports.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-md7u.115.

## Human / Provider Authority

Owner decision is human/product-gated; implementation after a retain decision is autonomous.

title: Review source evidence freshness authority independently
description:
## What To Build

Review importer mapping, coverage, integrity, retrieval and proof boundaries on disposable PostgreSQL.

## Priority

P1 — governing current imports accept captured evidence whose freshness is unknown or stale

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`source-decision-store-import.ts:423` requires only status=captured. Local and DB evidence set freshness unknown at `:330` and `drizzle-source-decision-import-repository.ts:109`; current tests still expect active governing SearchDocuments. Integrity inspector has no freshness violation.

## Mechanism

Only captured-current evidence may mint current governing authority; stale/unknown remain retained evidence with defer/gap, coverage and integrity report typed freshness separately.

## Violated Invariant

Current authority requires current evidence; captured is provenance state, not freshness.

## Runtime Consumer

SourceDecision import, SearchDocument activation, source coverage, integrity readiness and DecisionPacket.

## Falsifier

A current corpus row with captured+unknown/stale evidence creates accepted/adopted governing edge and active projection.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/cli exec vitest run src/__tests__/decision-corpus-import.test.ts src/__tests__/source-coverage.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

No stale/unknown path governs; current classification is explicit; designated-store result remains separate.

## Required Verification

Standards/Spec review, Node-22 import/coverage tests, DB smoke, typecheck, Fallow and diff-check.

## Proves

Governing imports and read-only integrity distinguish current/stale/unknown evidence.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove remote freshness oracle truth or universal source completeness.

## Rollback / Contraction

Fail closed to defer/evidence gap while retaining captured bytes; never relabel unknown as current.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text:
Independent freshness-authority review completed at exact HEAD
fbe81907edf6ce532ce4bd62c592a8912f5d0dcf.

Scoped decision: accept the source-decision corpus importer boundary. Only
captured evidence with literal freshness=current retains the current lifecycle.
Captured stale, unknown, missing freshness, and malformed persisted freshness
fail closed: retained artifact/chunk, deprecated claim, deferred decision, no
SourceDecisionEdge, expired SearchDocument. Coverage separately reports
captured current/stale/unknown and cannot call stale/unknown current-complete.
Integrity reports every unquarantined adopted non-current artifact in a
repeatable-read read-only snapshot. Retrieval SQL selects only active documents,
and source-decision knowledge selection requires accepted/adopted edge-backed
authority, so the scoped imported non-current rows do not reach governing packet
inputs.

Review triage:

- Standards found a real adjacent P0: the generic source claim-add -> decision
  adopt/link path can still mint accepted/adopted/edge authority with zero
  SourceChunks and no current-freshness proof. Disposable PostgreSQL reproduces
  claim=accepted, decision=1, edge=1, chunks=0 while readiness reports
  captured_evidence_missing_or_mismatched and governing_evidence_not_current.
  This is pre-existing and already owned by md7u.156, with direct-SQL hardening
  in md7u.157. It is outside this Bead's explicitly importer-scoped description,
  so this review does not claim a repository-wide invariant.
- PostgreSQL proof found a P2 evidence gap: unknown freshness is proven
  expired/no-edge and retrieval is proven active-only, but no single exact test
  traverses an imported unknown control through the real source-search and
  packet-source readbacks. New follow-up md7u.196 owns that focused falsifier.
  This is a proof gap, not an observed runtime leak.
- Designated-store results remain separate. No persistent store was inferred,
  inspected, or mutated. md7u.104/data001 retain store identity, backup,
  row-level approval, quarantine/demotion, and postflight authority.

Verification:

- Independent disposable PostgreSQL: 30/30 migrations; clean pre/post
  readiness; CLI freshness+coverage 2 files / 8 tests; integrity 1 file / 3
  tests; decision-corpus DB smoke passed with 11 rows, current selected, stale
  excluded, current=6/unknown=1 coverage, and zero cleanup residue.
- Local reproduction command: decision-corpus-import plus source-coverage 2
  files / 21 tests passed. Root typecheck via the required proxy command passed;
  git diff --check passed; broad Fallow reported dead/dupes=0 and one inherited
  health finding.
- Canonical Node-22 CI run 29298148014 is green in all four jobs for exact SHA
  fbe81907. Its macOS disposable-PostgreSQL profile includes freshness 1/1,
  coverage 7/7, integrity 3/3, and the generic-write repros.
- Actual Claude second-opinion wrapper was invoked on a 125337-byte filtered
  .101-.103 patch plus the .105 spec and project standards. It produced no JSON
  and timed out after 300 seconds with exit 1. No Claude verdict or approval is
  claimed.

Source-to-decision ledger: importer code plus the exact PG lifecycle matrix
supports the decision that captured provenance is distinct from current
authority; coverage and integrity are adopted as typed reporting/detection, not
remote truth or repair; retrieval filters make the importer result consumable
without activating expired evidence. Falsifier: any imported current row backed
by stale/unknown evidence yields accepted/adopted/edge/active or appears in a
governing packet input. Does not prove remote freshness truth, universal source
completeness, generic/direct-SQL write safety, source usefulness, or designated-
store cleanliness.

title: Derive memory application task and context from execution run

## What To Build

## Priority

Reconstruct current packet/task/context/selected-subject authority inside one store transaction, fingerprint immutable application request, and expose only the atomic effects-once seam.

Cross-run/project IDs reject before insert; omitted IDs resolve deterministically when canonical.

Memory application authority and idempotency are transactional and payload-exact.

title: Review anti-memory recall authority and boundedness independently
description:
## What To Build

Perform an independent Standards/Spec review of the completed anti-memory chain, checking project scope, temporal ordering, packet budget, non-authority, and negative-path terminology.

## Priority

P1 — a known rejected path can disappear entirely from the packet

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`packages/harness/src/activation/activation-engine.ts:698` loads anti-memory, but the merge at `:813` contains only memory/source/search/owner-file candidates. `conflict-filter.ts:138` can only block an already recalled positive candidate. The current-HEAD falsifier returned `antiMemoryRecordCount=1`, `candidateCount=0`.

## Mechanism

Recall active AntiMemoryRecord rows by task/target relevance before the channel limit, represent them as explicitly non-governing negative candidates, and preserve them through context and packet readback.

## Violated Invariant

A current, task-relevant rejected path is first-class negative evidence even when no matching positive MemoryRecord was recalled; it must never become governing authority.

## Runtime Consumer

`retrieveActivationCandidates`, `compileHarnessPlan`, ContextAssembly, Codex brief, and DecisionPacket CLI/MCP readback.

One active task-relevant AntiMemoryRecord and zero positive candidates yields no activation candidate or rejected-path warning.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/activation/__tests__/index.test.ts` with the standalone anti-memory fixture described above.

## Acceptance Criteria

Review either records no blocking finding or creates evidence-backed follow-up Beads; every claim cites current code and proof output.

## Required Verification

`rtk proxy pnpm typecheck`, focused tests, DB smoke artifact, Fallow changed-range gate, and `rtk git diff --check`.

## Proves

The bounded activation path can recall standalone negative evidence without promoting it.

## Does Not Prove

This does not prove optimal ranking weights, source truth, or usefulness.

## Rollback / Contraction

If a first-class candidate would broaden authority, contract it to an explicit bounded exclusion/warning channel; never reintroduce positive-authority semantics.

title: Falsify standalone task-relevant AntiMemoryRecord recall
description:
## What To Build

Add the smallest red-capable activation test that uses one current task-relevant AntiMemoryRecord with no positive twin and demonstrates the current empty candidate/readback result.

## Priority

P1 — a known rejected path can disappear entirely from the packet

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

`packages/harness/src/activation/activation-engine.ts:698` loads anti-memory, but the merge at `:813` contains only memory/source/search/owner-file candidates. `conflict-filter.ts:138` can only block an already recalled positive candidate. The current-HEAD falsifier returned `antiMemoryRecordCount=1`, `candidateCount=0`.

## Mechanism

Recall active AntiMemoryRecord rows by task/target relevance before the channel limit, represent them as explicitly non-governing negative candidates, and preserve them through context and packet readback.

## Violated Invariant

A current, task-relevant rejected path is first-class negative evidence even when no matching positive MemoryRecord was recalled; it must never become governing authority.

## Runtime Consumer

`retrieveActivationCandidates`, `compileHarnessPlan`, ContextAssembly, Codex brief, and DecisionPacket CLI/MCP readback.

## Falsifier

One active task-relevant AntiMemoryRecord and zero positive candidates yields no activation candidate or rejected-path warning.

## Reproduction Command

`rtk proxy pnpm --filter @krn/harness exec vitest run src/activation/__tests__/index.test.ts` with the standalone anti-memory fixture described above.

## Acceptance Criteria

The new test fails on the fixed-point code for the observed `candidateCount=0` reason and distinguishes setup failure from product failure.

## Required Verification

Run the focused harness test under Node 22 and retain the exact candidate/exclusion readback.

## Proves

The bounded activation path can recall standalone negative evidence without promoting it.

## Does Not Prove

This does not prove optimal ranking weights, source truth, or usefulness.

## Rollback / Contraction

If a first-class candidate would broaden authority, contract it to an explicit bounded exclusion/warning channel; never reintroduce positive-authority semantics.

## Affected Files / Packages

`packages/db/src/repositories/drizzle-memory-repository.ts`, `packages/core/src/repositories/memory-repository.ts`, `packages/harness/src/activation/*`, DecisionPacket tests/smokes.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-temp001.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human/provider authority is required; this is a fail-closed negative-evidence contract.

## Required Skills

diagnosing-bugs

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs
design: Recall active AntiMemoryRecord rows by task/target relevance before the channel limit, represent them as explicitly non-governing negative candidates, and preserve them through context and packet readback.
acceptance_criteria: The new test fails on the fixed-point code for the observed `candidateCount=0` reason and distinguishes setup failure from product failure.

Any child lacks exact current-code evidence, a runtime consumer, a red-capable falsifier, proof/non-proof boundaries, rollback/contraction, affected files, authority requirement, or native blocker edges; or `bd ready` exposes a broad audit shell instead of actionable slices.

## Does Not Prove

Backlog creation does not prove fixes, product readiness, designated-store integrity, live Codex usefulness, provider configuration, source truth, or completeness against unknown defect classes.

## Rollback / Contraction

Supersede or close a child with current evidence when duplicate, already satisfied, stale, or falsely split. Remove its dependency edges rather than preserving padding. If the full 969-issue workspace disappears, stop mutations and mark this map blocked.

title: Quarantine legacy source authority violations before final constraints
description:
## What To Build

Use the src004 integrity report in an explicit expand-contract migration. Populate new project and SourceDecision bindings only where claim, project, reviewed decision, target, and evidence are unambiguous. Mark cross-project, orphaned, conflicting, or unsupported legacy rows historical and non-governing and invalidate their active SearchDocument projections. Preserve provenance and quarantine reason. After clean preflight, enforce final database constraints for project coherence, current decision relation, and edge identity. Never auto-adopt or repair project IDs by guess.

## Consumer

Activation, DecisionPacket, source search, migrations, DB readiness, and operator data repair.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every preflight violation becomes valid under constraints or explicitly quarantined and non-governing.
- No ambiguous row is silently relinked or assigned a project.
- Active projections for quarantined authority are invalidated.
- Migration and preflight replay are idempotent.
- New cross-project, arbitrary-edge, and competing terminal writes fail at DB level.
- Clean canonical rows retain IDs and authority.

## Falsifier

An invalid legacy edge remains governing, or migration changes its project or target so it appears valid.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: migration fixture containing each violation, before/after integrity report, activation exclusion, rollback and replay.

Non-proof: quarantine does not prove historical content is false or retained rows are semantically true.

## Native Dependency Edges

## Rollback / Contraction

If classification is ambiguous, fail migration and leave the store unverified. Never mass-delete or auto-promote.

None.

title: Commit packet-bound MemoryApplication effects exactly once
description:
## What To Build

Create one repository unit-of-work for the winning packet-bound MemoryApplication. In one PostgreSQL transaction create the application, apply the counter delta, create required negative feedback, create or reuse the deterministic AntiMemoryCandidate, and enqueue corresponding outbox records. Neutral and positive outcomes must not create negative effects. The CLI calls this boundary once and returns its complete or replayed result. Do not add an outbox daemon.

## Consumer

krn memory record apply --persist, memory ranking, feedback history, anti-memory review, and retry recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Failure after application, counter, feedback, candidate, or outbox insert rolls back all effects.
- Two independent clients retrying the same semantic identity create exactly one application, one counter delta, and one applicable feedback, candidate, and outbox chain.
- Retry after lost CLI output returns the complete winning result.
- Candidate identity derives from the application identity.
- helped reaches this boundary only after anat evidence validation.
- hurt or stale cannot commit an application without required review effects.

## Falsifier

A crash after application commit leaves required feedback absent and retry skips it, or one retry doubles a counter or event.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: real-PG two-client race, barrier and per-stage fault injection, exact counts, focused CLI test.

Non-proof: atomicity does not prove that helped, hurt, or stale was correctly classified.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-anat. Blocks app003 and the live trial.

## Rollback / Contraction

Prefer one DB-local transaction. If an external effect is introduced later, persist a unique pending outbox row without claiming delivery.

None.

krn-implementation,code-review

title: Contain paired target checking and score only held-out behavior
description:
## What To Build

Separate the paired checker from the live runner. Before executing target code, collect tracked and untracked status and reject forbidden changes. Run target commands and held-out behavior in a constrained subprocess with an allowlisted environment and no host secrets; never import model-modified code into the KRN process. Treat typecheck, tests, diff, scope and containment as validity gates. Compute advantage only from predeclared held-out behavior. Preserve actual command status, exit code, timing, output refs and complete change manifest.

## Consumer

mise-en-palace-1rnc and the paired-trial persistence boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A forbidden untracked file makes the arm invalid.
- Forbidden changes are detected before model-modified code executes.
- A malicious target cannot read a sentinel host secret or arbitrary host file.
- Merely adding tokens such as unknown, CreateUserResult, or invalid_json does not improve score.
- Failed, missing, or timed-out commands are invalid and retain their real outcomes.
- Validity gates are not scored as KRN advantage.
- The checker returns tracked and untracked changes plus per-command observations.

## Falsifier

KRN wins through regex text, an untracked write is invisible, or model code executes with the full host environment.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: fake-executor tests, malicious-target containment falsifier, untracked preflight test, behavior-only scoring tests, Node 22 focused suite.

Non-proof: a safe checker does not prove Codex was invoked or that one task generalizes.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. Blocks mise-en-palace-1rnc.

## Rollback / Contraction

If containment cannot be guaranteed, return invalid or blocked before executing target code. Do not retain a host-import fallback.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

paired-live-codex-repair.ts:195 scores regexes, line 481 ignores untracked files, and line 517 imports target code into the reviewer process.

## Required Skills
target-repo-testing,krn-implementation,code-review
design: Validity gates establish whether an arm is comparable; only predeclared held-out behavior contributes to advantage. Model-modified code never runs in the KRN host process.
acceptance_criteria: Untracked or forbidden writes, secret access, missing/failed/timed-out commands, or containment failures make an arm invalid; regex tokens do not score; exact observations are returned.
notes: Implemented in commits 5b6bc2f and ac990da; pushed main. Proof: paired checker captures tracked and untracked manifests before target execution and rechecks after; forbidden paths invalidate before target commands run; commands have bounded timeout, sanitized env/HOME/TMP, real exit status, stderr/stdout, and duration; held-out runtime runs in a separate Node subprocess with experimental filesystem permissions limited to target/compiled/checker roots, with no host-import fallback. Static tokens/prose (unknown, CreateUserResult, invalid_json) are diagnostics only and cannot increase advantage; only three predeclared held-out runtime behaviors score. Validity gates (preflight, forbidden files, target test/typecheck/diff, containment) never score advantage; failed/missing/timed-out commands invalidate. Persisted paired evidence retains per-arm command status, exit code, duration/output refs, change manifest, and unknown ownership rather than fabricated KRN ownership. Does not prove: Codex was actually invoked, second-operator usability, arbitrary-repository portability, semantic target correctness beyond declared held-out behaviors, source truth, or product readiness.

description:
## What To Build

Define one temporal eligibility rule, validFrom <= now < validUntil with explicit invalidation semantics and fail-closed timestamp parsing. Apply project, lifecycle, time, and task relevance in SQL before limits for MemoryRecord, AntiMemoryRecord, and SourceClaim retrieval. Keep defensive activation and conflict filters so expired or malformed rows cannot block. Add deterministic ordering after eligibility.

## Consumer

Memory retrieval, anti-memory conflict filtering, source consensus activation, and DecisionPacket selection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Future validFrom records are excluded.
- validFrom and validUntil boundary behavior is explicit and tested.
- Invalid timestamps fail closed.
- Expired or invalidated AntiMemory cannot block.
- Twenty-five ineligible rows cannot hide the relevant current row at position 26.
- Source claims are filtered by lifecycle and task relevance before limit.
- Existing ordinary lexical memory relevance behavior remains intact.

## Falsifier

A future record activates now, an expired AntiMemory still blocks, or an eligible relevant source disappears solely because unrelated rows consumed the limit.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: focused boundary tests, real-PG position-26 smokes, exact retrieval readback, root typecheck.

Non-proof: correct eligibility does not prove semantic relevance or source truth.

## Native Dependency Edges

None.

## Rollback / Contraction

If source lexical matching needs separate tuning, first enforce lifecycle and time before limit; do not weaken temporal correctness.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

temporal-filter.ts:8 omits validFrom and accepts invalid dates; drizzle-memory-repository.ts:1299 limits AntiMemory before eligibility; drizzle-source-repository.ts:387 limits claims before lifecycle/relevance.

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: One half-open temporal eligibility rule and task relevance are applied in the store query before top-N; activation retains a defensive fail-closed check.
acceptance_criteria: Future, expired, invalidated, malformed, irrelevant and wrong-lifecycle candidates cannot consume top-N or block current knowledge; exact boundary tests and position-26 falsifiers pass.
notes: Implemented in commits 9e58bf7 and e5f9f58; pushed main. Proof: one half-open validFrom <= now < validUntil rule with future, exact-boundary, invalid validFrom/validUntil/invalid now, invalidatedAt, and stale behavior tests in harness; active MemoryRecord, AntiMemoryRecord, and SourceClaim SQL eligibility/relevance happens before LIMIT; activation passes one explicit runtime now and retains historical rejected/deprecated SourceClaims only as bounded non-governing paths; deterministic relevance/recency/ID ordering; anti-memory creation accepts explicit validity bounds. Real PostgreSQL proofs: db:smoke:retrieval-substrate with 25 expired memory rows and 25 unrelated source rows before current/relevant position 26; db:smoke:activation; db:smoke:memory-governance; db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop. Local proof: root Node 22 typecheck, full workspace tests (955 passed), Fallow CI, git diff --check. Remote proof: GitHub Actions run 29132319501 for exact SHA e5f9f580, all 3 jobs passed. Does not prove: semantic relevance quality, source truth, corpus completeness, or live Codex usefulness.
close_reason: Temporal and relevance eligibility is enforced before activation limits with local and exact remote CI proof.

title: Bind durable proof to exact clean or dirty environment identity
description:
## What To Build

Produce one secret-free environment fingerprint for durable DB, eval, live-trial, feedback, and doctor proof. Discover the actual Git/workspace root independent of checkout basename. Distinguish successful clean status from inspection failure. Bind staged, unstaged, and untracked state by a secret-free content/path digest, or mark all dirty artifacts explicitly unverified. Include lockfile, Node/pnpm, OS/arch, evaluator/checker, protocol, and ordered applied migration identity or explicit unavailable state. Attach it through the common proof envelope.

## Consumer

DB smokes, EvidenceBundle and FeedbackDelta metadata, paired trials, doctor, data001, and ready001.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A clean renamed clone reports gitDirty false.
- Failed Git inspection reports unknown, distinct from clean.
- Two different dirty contents cannot emit the same verified worktree identity.
- Staged, unstaged, and untracked state is represented without secret bytes.
- Divergent applied migration identity changes the DB fingerprint or yields unavailable.
- Changing a load-bearing runtime or checker changes the fingerprint.
- Durable proof artifacts include the exact fingerprint.

## Falsifier

Materially different repositories, dirty trees, or database histories produce indistinguishable verified artifacts.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: clean renamed clone, dirty-content collision, failed Git, divergent migration, deterministic artifact tests.

Non-proof: an environment fingerprint identifies conditions; it does not prove command success, source truth, or usefulness.

## Native Dependency Edges

Existing dependency on mise-en-palace-14dg remains. Closed tool001 and supply002 prerequisites remain recorded.

## Rollback / Contraction

If dirty content cannot be safely hashed, label dirty proof unverified. Do not collapse dirty and unknown.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

environment-fingerprint.ts:35 depends on repo basename, line 154 maps successful empty status to unknown, and line 164 hardcodes schema identity.
design: A secret-free deterministic fingerprint distinguishes clean, unknown, and exact dirty content and includes the applied migration identity. Different load-bearing environments cannot share verified proof.
acceptance_criteria: Clean renamed clones report false; failed Git inspection is unknown; different dirty contents differ or remain unverified; migration/runtime changes alter the fingerprint; durable artifacts carry it.
notes:
REOPENED after independent review of a100ccac. A successful empty git status is converted to unknown, so a clean checkout can never emit gitDirty:false. Repository root discovery also depends on the checkout basename and schemaVersion is a constant rather than applied migration identity. Make the fingerprint derive clean/unknown correctly, find the actual Git/workspace root under renamed clones, and bind DB-backed artifacts to a secret-free applied migration/schema identity or explicit unavailable state. Add clean-clone, renamed-root, and divergent-migration falsifiers.
2026-07-10 current-code audit: active scope replaced with the exact remediation contract above; prior completion notes remain historical evidence and do not close the reopened issue.
close_reason: Completed. Environment fingerprint now discovers the actual Git root via git rev-parse rather than checkout basename; distinguishes clean false from failed Git inspection unknown; hashes status, working-tree diff, staged diff, and untracked file paths/content into a secret-free worktreeIdentity; includes ordered applied Drizzle migration identity or explicit unavailable/unconfigured state; preserves Node/pnpm/OS/arch/evaluator/checker/MCP inputs and common output envelope. Added clean renamed-clone, no-Git unknown, deterministic dirty-content divergence, and secret-free regression tests. Proof: Node 22 CLI typecheck, environment fingerprint tests 4 passed, Fallow, diff check; remote commit a441666c662fb27b7a5dabeb3ad8b965a36a4738, GitHub Actions run 29137426109, all three jobs passed. Proves: materially different clean/dirty/unknown repository and DB identity states cannot share a verified fingerprint. Does not prove: command success, source truth, or usefulness.

title: Scan submitted history for secrets with exact reviewed exceptions
description:
## What To Build

Scan all tracked text, including .env.example, and every commit in the validated PR or push range. Secret exceptions bind path, pattern, and exact reviewed fake-match identity or hash; they cannot suppress a whole detector for a file. Unreadable tracked text is a blocking scanner failure. Diagnostics never print secret bytes. Preserve fail-closed dependency and license behavior and keep SBOM deferred to release.

## Consumer

PR, push, and scheduled security gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A supported credential in .env.example fails.
- A second same-pattern credential in an excepted fixture fails while the exact reviewed fake value remains allowed.
- A secret added and removed inside the submitted range is detected.
- Unreadable tracked input cannot become a pass.
- Output exposes path and detector only, not credential value.
- Scanner startup, network, and parse failures remain non-zero.
- Existing license and dependency policies remain bounded.

## Falsifier

A supported secret exists in submitted history or an excepted file while all required security gates are green.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: tracked temp-repo tests for HEAD, range, example, exception collision and read failure, reviewed baseline, real workflow log.

Non-proof: supported patterns do not prove absence of unknown, encoded, encrypted, or novel secrets.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on mise-en-palace-ci002 for the validated event range. Blocks gov003.

## Rollback / Contraction

Keep the current small pattern gate and exact exceptions. Do not add broad SAST, DLP, or SBOM infrastructure in this slice.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

security-policy.mjs:49 excludes .env.example, line 73 exceptions cover path plus detector rather than exact value, and read failures can be skipped.
design: The small secret gate scans tracked submitted history, treats unreadable input as failure, and binds exceptions to exact reviewed fake values without printing secret bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Secrets in .env.example, removed-in-range commits, or beside an excepted fake value fail; unreadable input fails; diagnostics redact values; dependency/license outage remains non-zero.
notes: Implemented in f4eea509b87412a220a611b256bcaf6a0c9a9e46. Tracked secret scan now includes .env.example, validates exact path/detector/matchSha256 exceptions, scans added lines across every commit in the resolved submitted range, fails on unreadable inputs, and emits only path/detector diagnostics. Security workflow passes the same PR/push event base resolver inputs; dependency and license gates remain separate and fail closed. Proof: security-policy/repository-policy 25/25, security:secrets, Node22 typecheck, Fallow, removed-secret/history/.env/exception-collision/unreadable tests, remote CI 29135386083 all 3 jobs passed. Does not prove unknown or encoded secrets, novel patterns, production security, or SBOM/release readiness.
close_reason: Tracked examples and submitted history are scanned with exact reviewed exceptions and fail-closed diagnostics; exact remote CI passed.

title: Conform and bound the minimal DecisionPacket MCP transport
description:
## What To Build

Make krn_decision_packet a bounded transport of the existing public packet contract. Return only packet identity, bounded DecisionPacket, explicit return channels, proof/non-proof, and minimal access metadata. title: Make doctor evidence labels match executed proof
description:
## What To Build

Make krn doctor distinguish static availability, historical readback, current executed proof, and store integrity. Symbols, scripts, parsers, table counts, or old rows may report available or historical only. Proven or ready requires a current bounded probe with command, status, captured time, freshness, project/store identity, environment fingerprint, and exact migration identity. Source authority or legacy usefulness integrity violations from src005/app003 force blocked or unverified. Keep doctor read-only; it must not secretly execute heavy smokes.

## Consumer

Operators inspecting DB, activation, DecisionPacket, target-repo, and retained-store readiness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Breaking current activation while preserving historical rows cannot yield proven or ready.
- Static reachability remains available, never verified.
- Current bounded probe evidence includes command, status, timestamp, freshness, project/store, environment, and migration identity.
- Missing, stale, failed, mismatched, or unavailable proof is unverified.
- Source authority or usefulness integrity violations prevent ready.
- Tests use typed probe results, not source text or command-list assertions.
- Doctor remains read-only and names the exact verification command.

## Falsifier

A broken runtime or contaminated store with intact symbols and historical rows still reports proven, verified, or ready.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: typed doctor tests, stale/broken/mismatched proof tests, integrity probe fixtures, current DB probe and readback.

Non-proof: truthful labels do not themselves execute product behavior or establish live usefulness or source truth.

## Native Dependency Edges

Depends on src005 and app003 for final integrity semantics. Closed 61ko and fchu predecessors remain historical prerequisites. Blocks ops001.

## Rollback / Contraction

Without current executable proof or clean integrity readback, downscope to available, historical, blocked, or unverified. Do not infer readiness.

## Open Questions

None.

## Current Evidence

doctor-db-checks.ts can build passed/current activation evidence from historical table counts without executing current activation.
design: Doctor labels evidence classes honestly; only current executed, identity-bound proof over an integrity-clean store may be verified or ready.
acceptance_criteria: Historical rows and static topology cannot yield ready; current typed proof and clean source/usefulness integrity are required; missing evidence is unverified.
notes:

title: Persist failed eval candidates through reviewed feedback
description:
## What To Build

Add an explicit opt-in persistence bridge for DecisionPacket eval failures using the existing EvidenceBundle -> ReviewAssessment -> FeedbackDelta path and existing evalCandidates JSON storage/readback. Persist case/suite ID, failure class, packet/checksum or evidence refs, observed vs expected signal, and doesNotProve. Passing evals must persist none. Deduplicate a retry of the same eval execution identity. Do not add a new table, scheduler, benchmark service, or automatic MemoryRecord/SourceClaim promotion.

## Consumer

Operator review, DecisionPacket/run readback, and later manual creation of durable eval cases or maintenance follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One red-capable failing case persists exactly one reviewable typed eval candidate with exact evidence refs and non-proof.
- A passing eval persists no candidate.
- Suite-threshold and case-level failures remain distinguishable and deterministic.
- Retrying the same execution identity does not duplicate candidates.
- Readback exposes stored candidates after process exit.
- No candidate automatically changes memory, source, governing authority, or activation.

## Falsifier

After an opted-in failing eval exits, stdout is the only record and store/readback still contains zero eval candidates.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof:

Focused failing/passing/retry tests, store repository test, DecisionPacket/readback test, root typecheck, Fallow, and git diff check.

Non-proof:

Persistence does not prove a failure is important, correctly classified, or suitable for promotion.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This is an independent ready P1 roadmap completion using existing storage.

## Rollback / Contraction

If automatic CLI persistence couples eval execution too tightly, emit a deterministic candidate artifact consumed by an explicit existing evidence-capture command; do not create a second store.

## Open Questions

None. The opt-in flag must require run/project identity rather than infer it from current working directory.

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: Smallest decision: an explicitly opted-in failed DecisionPacket eval can persist its existing typed candidates through the current reviewed feedback seam, without adding storage or promoting truth.
acceptance_criteria: Failing eval persists packet/case-bound candidates and readback; passing eval persists none; duplicate retry is deterministic; no memory/source truth changes automatically.
notes:
Audit evidence: DecisionPacket eval builds typed EvalCandidate objects but eval-main only prints JSON. FeedbackDelta, DB schema, and DecisionPacket readback already support evalCandidates; production writers hardcode empty arrays.
Implementation: opt-in DecisionPacket eval failure persistence through EvidenceBundle -> ReviewAssessment -> FeedbackDelta with advisory-lock idempotency, case/suite identity, evidence refs, observed/expected signal, doesNotProve, empty memory/source arrays, passing skip, and independent-connection readback smoke. Proves: focused case/suite/pass mapping tests, concurrent two-client Postgres persistence and duplicate prevention, one candidate readback, no memory/source mutation, root tests/typecheck, CI-only clean test typecheck, Fallow, diff check, CI run 29060776391 green. Does not prove: eval failure importance or classification correctness, source truth, live Codex behavior, promotion suitability, or automatic authority change.

title: Verify migration identity instead of migration count
description:
## What To Build

Strengthen database migration readiness to compare ordered applied migration identity with the repository migration set. Use the identity available in the migration journal and migration files, including hash or equivalent immutable identifier and ordering. Report missing, extra, reordered, and same-count-mismatched migrations distinctly. Doctor may say verified only for an exact match; unavailable metadata must be unknown/unverified, not inferred from count.

## Consumer

krn doctor DB readiness, CI migration checks, and operators deciding whether a store is safe to use.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A database with the same migration count but a changed hash/identity is not verified.
- Missing, extra, and reordered applied migrations have distinct actionable readback.
- An exact ordered identity match is verified.
- Legacy/unavailable identity data produces explicit unknown or migration-required state without a false positive.
- Existing empty/new database behavior remains intentional and tested.

## Falsifier

Changing an applied migration identity while preserving the count leaves doctor reporting migrations verified.

Proof:

Focused migration-readiness tests for exact/mismatch/missing/extra/order cases, doctor DB readback tests, DB migration check command, root typecheck, Fallow, and git diff check.

Non-proof:

Identity parity does not prove migration SQL correctness, data validity, backup safety, or production readiness.

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This is an independent ready P1 health correction.

## Rollback / Contraction

If the migration tool does not expose hashes at runtime, compare the strongest immutable ordered identity it does expose and report weaker evidence honestly; never revert to count-as-verified.

## Open Questions

## Required Skills
krn-implementation,code-review
design: Smallest decision: migration readiness is verified only when the ordered applied identities match the ordered repository migration identities, not merely when counts match.
acceptance_criteria: Same-count divergent, reordered, missing, and extra migrations are reported distinctly; exact identity match verifies; doctor wording reflects verified vs unavailable/unknown.

title: Enforce atomic memory lifecycle transitions
description:
## What To Build

Turn MemoryCandidate and AntiMemoryCandidate promotion/rejection plus MemoryRecord supersession into guarded atomic transitions. Use row locks or conditional updates from explicitly allowed source states. Enforce one accepted truth record per candidate, reject-after-accept failure, and deterministic concurrent behavior. Require a superseding MemoryRecord to be a different active record in the same project; reject self-links, cross-project replacements, and invalid lifecycle targets. Atomic lifecycle transitions do not prove promoted content is true or useful.

title: Make maintenance candidate effects idempotent
description:
## What To Build

## Acceptance Criteria

- An injected failure after the first of multiple candidate writes followed by retry produces exactly one candidate per semantic target.
- Concurrent or repeated execution of the same queue record cannot create duplicate candidates.
- Distinct subjects or distinct authorized outcomes still produce distinct candidates.
- Existing successful jobs settle normally; transient failures retry; terminal failures dead-letter under current policy.
- No handler directly promotes, rejects, expires, or supersedes durable truth as part of deduplication.

## Falsifier

title: Make source decision import content-addressed, atomic, and replay complete
description:
## What To Build

The public persist command must reuse that identity across process retry. Replay must validate exact status-aware graph completeness: current rows require the canonical decision edge and active search projection; stale rows require expired projection and no governing edge; rejected rows require canonical rejection history. - Two public persist invocations over byte-equivalent project input return the same semantic rows.
- Caller can supply stable identity; default identity is derived from project and normalized captured content.
- Process loss plus retry cannot create a second corpus because runtime createId changed.
- Changed statement, status, falsifier, note, or evidence digest under one identity conflicts.
- Missing or duplicate lifecycle-required edge, search, or rejection rows are partial/conflict.
- Injected row-N failure leaves no committed prefix.
- Current, stale, and rejected lifecycle semantics remain canonical.

## Falsifier

An identical public retry duplicates authority, or an incomplete graph is returned as complete replay.

## Proof / Non-Proof

title: Persist packet-bound usefulness writes atomically
description:
## What To Build

Make packet-bound evidence persistence one database-owned idempotent unit. Recompute and authenticate project, execution run, current DecisionPacket checksum, subject membership, and a typed capture identity. The winning write for that identity must create the EvidenceBundle, ReviewAssessment, FeedbackDelta, feedback outbox event, and deterministic maintenance queue record together, or create none. A later evidence upgrade uses a distinct capture identity; retry of the same capture cannot duplicate feedback or queue work. Evidence may remain unknown when binding fails, but cannot affect usefulness.

## Consumer

Evidence capture, FeedbackDelta, maintenance queue, memory/source counters, and future activation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fake, stale, cross-project, or packet-unselected subject binding cannot affect usefulness.
- Injected failure after every durable stage leaves zero partial chain rows.
- Two independent PostgreSQL connections submitting the same capture create exactly one semantic bundle, review, feedback, outbox, and queue chain.
- Retry returns the winning complete chain.
- A partial legacy chain is reported incomplete rather than success.
- A legitimate later evidence upgrade remains possible under a distinct typed identity.

## Falsifier

A caller invents binding, a crash leaves an orphan, or a concurrent retry duplicates semantic feedback or maintenance work.

title: Audit repository health after Phase 5/6
description:

Inspect architecture boundaries, store/schema/readbacks, maintenance, evals/smokes/CI, target-repo evidence, CLI/MCP, corpus and dead-code/duplication signals. ## Consumer

The operator choosing the next roadmap tranche and fresh agents consuming the resulting Beads frontier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Current main, CI, Beads, roadmap and package surfaces are revalidated.
- Findings are severity ordered with file and line evidence.
- Standards risks, product/spec gaps and verification gaps are separated.
- Existing open/deferred Beads are checked before any new ticket is created.
- Every retained finding becomes a precise Bead with acceptance, proof/non-proof, contraction and dependency edges; rejected findings are reported with evidence.
- No product code, schema, docs or runtime behavior is changed.

## Falsifier

The audit creates broad cleanup tickets, duplicates existing work, treats green tests as product proof, or retains a claim without a runtime consumer and current-code evidence.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof:

Read-only repository inspection, focused diagnostic commands, Beads graph validation, git diff check, and independent subagent findings rechecked by the primary agent.

Non-proof:

## Native Dependency Edges

None. This audit is planning work and does not block the existing task-usefulness frontier.

## Rollback / Contraction

Supersede or delete any newly created ticket whose evidence is disproven before implementation; do not preserve audit prose as authority.

## Open Questions

None. Roadmap and current runtime evidence decide routing.

## Required Skills
beads,code-review

title: Persist measured target outcomes without fabricating proof or usefulness

Future DecisionPacket feedback readback and ready001.

- Abstention or zero selected subjects permits at most an EvalCandidate observation.

Editing score outcome to win or supplying arbitrary roots is enough to create helped or green command proof.

title: Run one tracked, fair, live Codex target repair pair

None.

title: Require application and fresh verification before positive usefulness
description:
## What To Build

Enforce one selected, used, helped evidence-state transition at both evidence capture and memory record apply. Packet membership proves selected only. Used requires authenticated application evidence from the same run and packet. Helped requires that application plus a later fresh successful command or output captured from the active EvidenceContract. Operator notes, dirty files, declared ownership, unchanged targets, and operator_reported passed strings are not successful verification. Downgrade to selected, used, unknown, or reviewable before counters or maintenance effects.

## Consumer

FeedbackDelta classification, MemoryRecord application, ranking counters, target-repo observation-only behavior, and app002.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Packet receipt and checksum alone can record selected but not used or helped.
- memory record apply with outcome helped and notes alone cannot increment positiveFeedbackCount.
- Dirty target state or declared ownership alone cannot prove used.
- operator_reported passed without execution, output, exit code, capture time, and active-contract membership cannot prove helped.
- Used requires same-run packet-bound application.
- Helped requires a later fresh successful active-contract verifier.
- Unchanged observation-only target remains selected and does not change source or memory authority.

## Falsifier

A no-application or no-verification run creates helped, retain strengthening, or a positive counter.

## Proof / Non-Proof

Proof: focused evidence and memory-apply red/green tests, target observation-only smoke, DB return loop, exact counter assertions.

Non-proof: evidence-class validation does not prove broad causal attribution, live Codex obedience, source truth, or product readiness.

## Native Dependency Edges

## Rollback / Contraction

If one generic classifier conflicts with a proven consumer, contract it to packet-bound usefulness writes while preserving that packet receipt can never mean helped.

## Open Questions

None.

title: Align activation source authority with consensus timeline
description:

title: Delete prose-only target-repo skill test
description:
Why this exists: target-repo-testing-skill.test.ts reads .agents/skills/target-repo-testing/SKILL.md and agents/openai.yaml, then asserts prose and metadata strings. That is exactly the kind of docs/prose/topology test AGENTS.md and KRN_ROADMAP.md reject. It does not prove target-repo safety, DecisionPacket behavior, store-backed memory, or runtime write authority.

What needs to be done: delete the prose-only test without adding a replacement snapshot. Keep runtime target-repo behavior covered by existing target-repo harness / smoke / command tests. Verify with targeted package tests if needed, root typecheck, Fallow changed-file gate, and diff check.

Acceptance criteria:
- packages/cli/src/__tests__/target-repo-testing-skill.test.ts is removed.
- No new prose/topology test replaces it.
- Existing runtime target-repo tests remain untouched.
- typecheck and Fallow changed-file gates pass.

Proof/non-proof boundary: this cleanup proves one test-theater surface was removed; it does not prove all remaining tests are valuable or that target-repo runtime behavior is complete.
close_reason: Deleted the prose-only target-repo-testing skill test without replacement. Existing target-repo runtime lane still passes: rtk pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- target-repo-harness-smoke (73 files / 481 tests). Root verification passed: rtk proxy pnpm typecheck, rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci, rtk git diff --check. Non-proof: this removes one test-theater surface; it does not prove every remaining test is high-value.

title: Prove source consensus conflict creates DecisionPacket abstention
description:
Why: KRN_ROADMAP Phase 5 says consensus must surface support, dissent, missing evidence, and abstention instead of confident guidance. Current DB return-loop smoke proves current/superseded/rejected source paths, but not contested/unknown source consensus producing evidence gaps and an abstention signal in the DecisionPacket.

Acceptance criteria:
- A focused behavior test or DB smoke fixture creates conflicting or unsupported source-claim consensus for a run.
- The resulting DecisionPacket keeps conflicted/unsupported source authority out of clean governing guidance.
- The packet exposes sourceConsensus evidenceGapIds and an abstentionScore status/reason tied to the conflict or missing decision support.
- Rejected/superseded path behavior remains unchanged.
- No new eval lane, markdown proof, broad benchmark, or dashboard/API surface is added.

Proof/non-proof:
- Proves only bounded source-consensus conflict handling in DecisionPacket generation.
- Does not prove broad source truth, automated review quality, or large-corpus consensus.
close_reason: Rejected by evidence: existing core, CLI, evidence, and activation tests already prove caveated/conflicted/unsupported source consensus produces DecisionPacket evidence gaps and abstention while unsupported accepted-only claims cannot demote decision-linked authority. No duplicate test added.

comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text:
Rejected by current evidence; no code change.

Mapped path:

- Activation already refuses to let accepted-only unsupported invalidators rank down decision-linked authority; see packages/harness/src/activation/__tests__/index.test.ts test "does not rank down authority from accepted claims without decision support".
- DecisionPacket already converts caveated source authority and stale/conflicted authority into sourceConsensus.evidenceGapIds and abstentionScore.status = abstain; see packages/core/src/__tests__/decision-packet.test.ts and packages/cli/src/__tests__/decision-packet-command.test.ts.

Decision: do not add another test or smoke. The requested behavior has current behavior falsifiers. If a future Phase 5 gap appears, it should be narrower: live DB smoke for a specific unproven source-consensus state, not a duplicate packet abstention test.

title: Bind source-decision feedback smoke to persisted decisions
description:
Why: the feedback maintenance path now resolves source-decision usefulness feedback through the SourceRepository and only creates anti-memory candidates for persisted SourceDecision rows with sourceClaimId. The decision-packet return-loop smoke still emits synthetic sourceDecisionId values, so it can stop proving the runtime path or fail under live DB execution.

Acceptance criteria:
- decision-packet return-loop smoke uses persisted SourceDecision IDs for helped/stale source usefulness feedback.
- stale feedback maintenance still creates an anti-memory candidate linked to the feedback delta and the linked source claim.
- mismatched checksum feedback stays downgraded and out of the next packet.
- no direct durable truth mutation is introduced.

Proof/non-proof:
- Prove with focused compile/test and the existing smoke path where available.
- Do not claim broad source-review quality or autonomous maintenance scheduling.
close_reason: Completed: decision-packet return-loop feedback now uses persisted SourceDecision ids for helped/stale/mismatched feedback targets; live db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop proves stale feedback maintenance resolves the linked SourceClaim, creates the anti-memory candidate, leaves direct durable truth mutation at 0, and cleans up marker rows.

title: Implement explicit expire-stale-memory maintenance handler
description: Roadmap Phase 6 says maintenance execution is explicit per-record and proposes candidates without silently mutating truth. The executor and write-boundary check exist, but production CLI registers only review_feedback_delta. expire_stale_memory has a job contract and preview boundary, yet running the job has no real handler. Consumer: operator/headless agent running krn maintenance run for a queued stale-memory review record. Falsifier: an expire_stale_memory queue record is claimed and skipped because no handler exists, or a handler directly mutates MemoryRecord truth.
design: Implement the narrowest handler for expire_stale_memory. It should inspect project memory records older than the payload cutoff through repository ports and create reviewable MemoryCandidate or AntiMemoryCandidate records only. It must declare only allowed writes, pass the runtime boundary, and never promote/demote durable truth directly.
acceptance_criteria: A focused repository/CLI smoke proves an expire_stale_memory queue record runs through runMaintenanceQueueRecord, passes handler write-boundary validation, creates reviewable stale-memory candidate(s), settles the queue record, and does not mutate memory_records or anti_memory_records directly; no daemon/scheduler is introduced; relevant tests, rtk proxy pnpm typecheck, rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented explicit expire_stale_memory maintenance handler. It scans project memory records, builds stale-memory preview candidates, writes reviewable anti-memory candidates only, passes runtime write-boundary validation, and is wired into krn maintenance run. Verified focused db/maintenance-preview/cli tests, package typechecks, root typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Expose source consensus timeline from live DB
description: Roadmap Phase 5 requires KRN to explain why a standard changed, when it changed, and what evidence caused it. Core has SourceConsensusTimeline, and DB repositories store SourceClaim/SourceClaimEdge/SourceDecisionEdge/SourceRejection, but the operator/product path does not yet expose a live DB readback for a changed standard. Consumer: headless agent/operator deciding whether a current source-backed standard superseded older guidance. Falsifier: with persisted current/superseded/rejected claims, no CLI/DB path can answer current vs historical vs rejected with citation refs and relation evidence.
design: Use existing source repository methods and SourceConsensusTimeline rather than adding a new eval lane. Add the smallest CLI/readback or smoke extension that builds a timeline from persisted claims/edges/rejections for one project/task marker. Do not create docs-as-memory or a broad consensus engine.
acceptance_criteria: A focused live DB smoke or CLI test creates current, superseded, and rejected SourceClaims with SourceClaimEdge/SourceDecisionEdge/SourceRejection support and renders a SourceConsensusTimeline readback showing current_authority, historical/superseded, and rejected entries with evidence refs/source ranges where present; invalid/missing relation support remains an evidence gap; rtk proxy pnpm typecheck, relevant tests/smoke, rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Extended live source-graph smoke to prove SourceConsensusTimeline from persisted DB rows: current authority, historical/superseded claim, rejected claim, and relation evidence-gap readback. Fixed smoke fixture revisitWhen values to ISO timestamps so temporal authority remains fail-closed and deterministic. Verified db:smoke:source-graph, CLI db tests, root typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Prove source consensus in DB-backed DecisionPacket
description: Roadmap Phase 5 says accepted, superseded, rejected, and unsupported source claims must affect packets exactly as authority rules say. Current source-graph DB smoke proves persisted claim edges reach activation rank-down/influence, but the live DB DecisionPacket return-loop smoke does not yet falsify that source consensus reaches the final agent packet. Add the smallest source-consensus proof to the existing DecisionPacket return-loop path, not a new eval lane or docs artifact.
design: Use existing decision-packet-return-loop smoke because it already owns runDecisionPacketCommand over live repositories. Do not import CLI into @krn/db source-graph smoke. Keep proof narrow and deterministic; use repository methods, activation trace, and packet JSON fields as falsifier.
acceptance_criteria: Existing DB-backed DecisionPacket smoke creates current/superseded/rejected source evidence through repositories; runDecisionPacketCommand readback proves current decision-linked claim can govern, superseded source claim is excluded/rejected-path evidence, and rejected source path remains visible as source/rejected evidence; smoke report exposes concise booleans/ids; no markdown/runtime memory files added; no new docs/prose topology tests.
close_reason: DB-backed DecisionPacket return-loop smoke now proves source consensus: current decision-linked SourceClaim governs, superseded SourceClaim is excluded/rejected path, rejected SourceClaim remains rejected-path evidence. Verified with db:smoke:decision-packet-return-loop, core decision-packet tests, harness activation/compiler tests, root typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

description:
The Matt Pocock skills repository was cloned under .local-lab only to support the skills adoption analysis. The adoption decision is recorded in Beads and repo-local skills; keeping the clone leaves a large markdown/source forest in the workspace without runtime consumer. Remove the lab clone and verify the workspace no longer exposes it as local project material.

## Required Skills
beads
