Verified the lab clone is absent and remaining markdown files are repo-local skills, root authority surfaces, or target-repo fixtures; no runtime path depends on the clone.

title: Fail closed on invalid source claim time
description: Roadmap North Star depends on temporal correctness: KRN must not activate or approve source authority when its time fields cannot be parsed. Current source governance audit flagged invalid timestamps as fail-open. Map source.ts current path, add the smallest behavior change that makes temporal validity explicit/fail-closed without adding new taxonomy sprawl. Consumer: source review/activation logic that decides whether a SourceClaim is usable. Falsifier: a claim with invalid revisitWhen or invalid now can still be treated as temporally valid/usable.
acceptance_criteria: Focused behavior test proves invalid source time is excluded or reported as invalid rather than valid; no prose/topology tests; rtk proxy pnpm typecheck and relevant package test pass; rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci passes if JS/TS files change; git diff --check passes.
close_reason: Current code already satisfies the Bead. source-authority.ts exposes SourceClaimTemporalValidity with invalid_time for invalid_now and invalid_revisit_when; isSourceClaimTemporallyValid returns true only for valid; assessSourceClaimOverride rejects non-valid candidates; source-review.ts emits blocking invalid_source_claim_time; source.test covers invalid now/revisitWhen, authority gate blocking, and override rejection. Verified with rtk pnpm --filter @krn/core test -- source. No code change needed; avoided adding redundant tests.

title: Expose explicit maintenance stale-record recovery
description: Roadmap Phase 6 says crashes/stuck running records are not implied unless a dedicated executor recovery path proves them. The DB executor already has recoverStaleMaintenanceQueueRecord, but the operator CLI only exposes maintenance run. Add a bounded explicit per-record CLI command: krn maintenance recover --id <maintenance-queue-id> --locked-before <iso-timestamp>. It should recover one stale running record through the existing repository path and render proof/non-proof boundaries. Consumer: technical operator/headless agent when a queued maintenance record is stuck running. Falsifier: command without KRN_DATABASE_URL or required args fails; valid command calls recoverStaleMaintenanceQueueRecord and prints recovered status; no daemon/scheduler/autonomous promotion wording is introduced.
acceptance_criteria: focused parser/CLI tests, rtk proxy pnpm typecheck, rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check pass
close_reason: Implemented explicit krn maintenance recover path for one stale running maintenance record. Added parser and runner coverage for valid recovery, required/invalid stale cutoff, and missing DB config. Verified: rtk pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- parse-maintenance-args run-maintenance-queue-command; rtk proxy pnpm typecheck; rtk pnpm quality:fallow:ci; rtk git diff --check.

title: Report created maintenance review candidates
description: The explicit maintenance executor settles review_feedback_delta records and the handler creates anti-memory candidates, but the readback only reports status/boundaries. That hides the next review target from a headless operator. Extend the handler/executor readback to expose created review candidate refs without mutating/promoting memory truth. Consumer: krn maintenance run output after feedbackMaintenanceRun. Falsifier: a stale feedback run must print anti_memory_candidate:<id>; skipped/no-candidate runs must print none.
acceptance_criteria: Focused maintenance command/executor tests, root typecheck, Fallow pass
close_reason: Maintenance handler/executor readback now reports created anti_memory_candidate refs, and krn maintenance run prints them as createdReviewCandidates. Verified DB maintenance executor tests, CLI maintenance command tests, root typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff --check.

title: Use one reviewable feedback rule for DecisionPacket caveats
description: DecisionPacket currently has a local maintenanceFeedbackOutcomes list while feedback maintenance enqueue/execution uses isReviewableFeedbackOutcome from @krn/core. This can drift and make packets disagree with maintenance about stale/hurt/rejected/unknown feedback. Replace the local list with the shared predicate. Consumer: DecisionPacket stale/rejected/noise caveats and maintenance queue. Falsifier: hurt/rejected/stale/unknown still caveat packets; helped remains useful and does not caveat.
acceptance_criteria: Focused core DecisionPacket tests, root typecheck, Fallow pass
close_reason: DecisionPacket caveats now use the shared isReviewableFeedbackOutcome rule instead of a duplicate maintenance feedback list. Removed the now-unused helper. Verified core DecisionPacket/feedback tests, root typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff --check.

title: Render explicit maintenance return channel after persisted feedback
description: KRN evidence capture now enqueues review_feedback_delta for reviewable usefulness feedback, but the readback only prints the queue record id. Add a bounded return channel line that tells the operator/agent the exact explicit executor command to run, without implying daemon/scheduler/autonomous promotion. Consumer: headless agent/operator after krn evidence capture --persist. Falsifier: helped-only feedback must not render the channel; stale/unknown feedback must render krn maintenance run --id <record>.
acceptance_criteria: Focused behavior tests and root typecheck/Fallow pass
close_reason: Rendered explicit feedbackMaintenanceRun return channel after reviewable persisted feedback enqueue, while helped-only feedback stays without maintenance channel. Verified @krn/cli evidence tests, root typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff --check.

title: Enqueue feedback maintenance from persisted evidence
description:
Why: Evidence capture can persist source/knowledge usefulness feedback, and the maintenance executor can turn negative or unknown feedback into reviewable anti-memory candidates. The missing product link is queue creation: outside DB smoke, persisted evidence does not enqueue review_feedback_delta work, so the feedback loop is not operator-usable.

Acceptance:
- krn evidence capture --persist enqueues one review_feedback_delta maintenance queue record when persisted usefulness feedback contains stale, hurt, rejected, noise, or unknown outcomes.
- Helped-only feedback does not enqueue maintenance work.
- The queue payload links projectId, feedbackDeltaId, and reason; existing DB queue_key uniqueness handles dedupe.
- No daemon, scheduler, autonomous promotion, or schema migration.
- Focused behavior tests cover enqueue/no-enqueue and existing typecheck/Fallow gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Persisted evidence capture enqueues review_feedback_delta work for reviewable feedback; helped-only feedback does not enqueue; tests/typecheck/Fallow pass
notes: Consumer: krn maintenance run --id can process queued feedback work from real evidence capture. Falsifier: feedback capture requires smoke-only manual queue creation or enqueues work for helped-only feedback.
close_reason: Implemented persisted evidence feedback enqueue to explicit maintenance queue. Reviewable source/knowledge usefulness outcomes now enqueue review_feedback_delta; helped-only feedback does not enqueue. Verified with @krn/cli evidence tests, root typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff --check.

title: Add explicit maintenance queue run command
description:
Why: Phase 6 says maintenance execution must be explicit per-record, with no daemon or scheduler claims. The executor and feedback handler exist, but the operator/headless CLI surface only exposes preview/smoke paths. Add a narrow product command that runs exactly one queued maintenance record through the existing executor and feedback handler.

Acceptance:
- krn maintenance run --id <maintenance-queue-id> requires KRN_DATABASE_URL and a non-empty id.
- The command creates the DB runtime, claims exactly the requested record, dispatches only supported handlers, and returns a bounded readback with status, job type, record id, write-boundary status, proof/non-proof lines.
- No daemon, scheduler, broad worker platform, autonomous promotion, or schema migration.
- Focused CLI/parser tests cover the behavior; typecheck and Fallow pass.
acceptance_criteria: CLI parser accepts maintenance run id; runtime command executes one queued record via existing executor; missing DB URL/id fail clearly; readback states explicit per-record non-proof; typecheck and Fallow pass
notes: Roadmap Phase 6: per-record executor yes, daemon/scheduler no. Consumer: headless agent/operator can advance queued feedback maintenance without using smoke internals. Falsifier: command implies scheduler/autonomous promotion or mutates truth outside handler-declared write boundary.
close_reason: Completed: added explicit krn maintenance run --id per-record executor command with bounded readback, parser/runtime tests, typecheck, Fallow, and git diff --check passing.

title: Evaluate Matt Pocock skills for KRN acquisition
description: Analyze https://github.com/mattpocock/skills against current KRN skill surface and roadmap. For each candidate skill, record source -> mechanism -> KRN implication -> decision/rejection -> consumer -> falsifier. Acquire only skills that reduce operator coordination or improve kernel-building discipline without duplicating repo-local skills or adding decorative prose. Acceptance: candidate list inspected from a temporary clone or fetched source; decisions captured in Beads notes or committed skill changes; no blind installation; verification runs for any touched skill files.
notes:
Matt Pocock skills source: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills cloned to /tmp/mattpocock-skills on 2026-07-09. Mechanism adopted only where it has a KRN consumer and falsifier.

Adopted:
- tdd -> adapted as .agents/skills/tdd/SKILL.md. Source mechanism: red-green at a public seam prevents implementation-coupled and tautological tests. KRN implication: future tests must protect source/memory/DecisionPacket behavior, not prose/topology. Consumer: Codex sessions adding/changing tests. Falsifier: a test added under the skill freezes prose/topology or passes without observing intended behavior.

Already covered / no copy:

- codebase-design -> repo-local codebase-design already carries deep-module/seam/deletion-test discipline with KRN runtime consumer/falsifier rule. No new file needed.

Why: the brain is useful only if it recalls current standards for ordinary coding tasks without the operator restating them. What: implement a tiny deterministic path for a normal task such as 'start or modify a frontend/backend package' where KRN recognizes task/project kind, activates current standards, rejected paths, stale warnings, and verification commands from store-backed/source-backed inputs. Non-goals: no dashboard, no broad project classifier, no markdown runtime memory, no template generator unless the packet directly needs it.

## Required Skills
activation-engine,source-to-decision,target-repo-testing
acceptance_criteria: A focused fixture or DB-backed path shows task/project kind recognition feeding activation; the resulting DecisionPacket contains current applicable standards, rejected paths, stale/superseded warnings when relevant, and minimal verification commands; selected context is smaller and more authoritative than a notes dump; tests/eval prove behavior rather than prose.
close_reason: Completed: DecisionPacket now exposes taskStandardDecisions and verificationCommands for normal coding task-standard activation. Verified with focused CLI tests, eval:decision-packet, eval:codex-decision-packet-obedience, eval:determinism, eval:second-repo-decision-packet, typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Build notes-baseline DecisionPacket falsifier
description:
Why: KRN must prove useful advantage over Codex plus notes plus grep on tasks where raw recall is not enough. What: build or tighten the notes-baseline runner around DecisionPacketEvalCase.v1 using deterministic fixtures for stale standards, rejected shortcuts, conflicting evidence, project-specific conventions, and abstention. The baseline may retrieve more text; KRN should win by governance, temporal correctness, rejection recall, source fidelity, and useful verification. Non-goals: no broad benchmark lab, no product victory claim, no live LLM dependency, no prose/file-topology snapshot tests.

## Required Skills
activation-engine,source-to-decision,target-repo-testing
acceptance_criteria: Runner is reproducible locally; at least one fixture would reward notes+grep for recall but fail it on governance while KRN can pass; scoring reports evidence fidelity, temporal correctness, rejection recall, consensus/conflict, abstention, and task usefulness; failures produce eval/readback output or Beads follow-ups, not markdown outcomes; verification includes focused CLI/eval tests and typecheck.
close_reason: Completed: notes-baseline DecisionPacket falsifier now reports and gates explicit abstention and consensus/conflict scoring inside DecisionPacketEvalCase.v1, preserving the existing deterministic notes+grep comparison rather than adding a new eval lane. The scorer now reports evidence fidelity, temporal correctness, rejection recall, consensus/conflict, abstention, and task usefulness, and the eval remains reproducible across self and second-repo corpora. Verified with pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- decision-packet-eval, pnpm eval:decision-packet, pnpm eval:determinism, pnpm eval:second-repo-decision-packet, pnpm typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Add explicit abstention scorer to DecisionPacketEvalCase
description:
Why: roadmap blocks product MCP until weak memory cannot become confident guidance. Current eval wrappers share DecisionPacketEvalCase.v1, but the scorer still needs an explicit abstention axis so unsupported, stale, or insufficiently sourced advice is scored differently from a correct 'not established' answer. What: inspect DecisionPacket eval scoring/readbacks and add the smallest behavior model that measures correct abstention and penalizes unsupported authority. Non-goals: no broad benchmark lab, no live LLM, no new docs-as-contract tests.

## Required Skills
activation-engine,source-to-decision,target-repo-testing
acceptance_criteria: DecisionPacketEvalCase reports an abstention score or equivalent explicit metric; weak/unsupported/stale guidance can fail the eval; correct abstention can pass even when recall is incomplete; MCP/readback non-proof text exposes that abstention is required before broader transport; focused tests cover unsupported advice vs correct abstention.
close_reason: Completed: DecisionPacketEvalCase now has a top-level abstentionScore gate with abstention case counts, the quality threshold includes minimumAbstentionScore, proof readback names abstention as a blocker before broader MCP transport, and a negative test fails when an unsupported mobile-release task receives governing advice instead of an evidence gap. Verified with pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- decision-packet-eval, pnpm eval:decision-packet, pnpm typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Roadmap tranche: prove Memory Core usefulness before broad MCP
description:
Why: KRN has a minimal read-only MCP wrapper, but MCP is transport. The next tranche must prove the governed DecisionPacket/Memory Core beats notes+grep on temporal correctness, rejected-path recall, abstention, and task usefulness before exposing broader MCP/API surfaces. What: build the first falsifier-grade DecisionPacket advantage path, add explicit abstention scoring, prove normal task-standard activation, strengthen temporal consensus/readbacks, and only then decide the next MCP surface. Non-goals: no dashboard, no broad MCP resource forest, no file-backed runtime memory, no cosmetic rename storm, no tests that only freeze prose.

close_reason: Completed roadmap tranche. Children delivered explicit abstention scoring, notes-baseline falsifier, normal task-standard activation, temporal consensus readback, store-backed feedback/demotion readbacks, docs/prose dependency cleanup, and the MCP product-boundary decision. Current stage: keep only the existing read-only krn_decision_packet MCP transport over CLI DecisionPacket; no broad MCP/API/dashboard expansion until a real consumer requires it. Verified final MCP decision with CLI MCP/decision-packet tests and root typecheck.

title: Fix source-governance blocking semantics
description:
Why: KRN's differentiator is source-backed temporal authority. Audits flagged risky source policy semantics: invalid timestamps must not fail open for activation, override must not bypass stronger current authority with a token reason, and accepted claims without decision support must not become governing packet authority. What: inspect current source policy and consumers, fix only proven issues, and keep archival readbacks distinct from activation blockers. Non-goals: no broad source.ts rewrite and no taxonomy migration in this slice.

## Required Skills

acceptance_criteria: Temporal invalidity is represented as blocking or explicit invalid-time status for activation; stronger valid decision-backed authority cannot be bypassed by a weak override reason; accepted-without-decision is not promoted into governing DecisionPacket authority; focused unit/eval coverage falsifies the cases.
close_reason: Verified current source-governance semantics satisfy the Bead: invalid source timestamps fail closed, accepted claims without SourceDecisionEdge support are blocking in activation, weak candidates are blocked by stronger current authority unless override reason is meaningful and provenanced, stale/rejected/accepted-only paths are excluded or caveated rather than governing DecisionPacket authority. Verification: pnpm --filter @krn/core test -- source; pnpm --filter @krn/harness test -- activation; pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- decision-packet-eval decision-packet-command run-source-decision-gaps-command; pnpm eval:decision-packet; pnpm typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check.

description:

close_reason: Completed: renamed CLI decision-packet selected-knowledge boundary from retained pattern selection to brain knowledge selection without compatibility aliases. Verification: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- brain-knowledge-selection plan codex run-run-show; pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check.

title: Lead source consensus readback with current authority
description: Why: buildSourceConsensusTimelineReadback currently sorts entries oldest-first, so temporal readback starts with historical claims before current authority. KRN_ROADMAP.md says KRN must answer what applies now, what superseded it, and what failed before; current authority should be first-class in the readback, with caveated/current context ahead of historical/rejected paths. What: sort source consensus timeline entries by state priority first, then newest createdAt, then id for stability. Acceptance: focused source-domain test proves current_authority appears before historical/rejected entries; core typecheck, changed-file Fallow, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Completed: source consensus timeline readback now orders entries by authority state first (current, caveated, historical, rejected), then newest createdAt, then id for stability. This makes current authority first-class in the temporal readback without claiming source truth. Verification: pnpm --filter @krn/core test -- source; pnpm --filter @krn/core typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check.

title: Surface rejected source decisions in agent packets
description: Why: KRN_ROADMAP.md says rejected paths are first-class memory, but the compact DecisionPacket currently exposes anti-memory rejections while omitting rejected SourceDecision candidates already present in the feedback read model. What: include source_decision_candidate entries with status reject in packet.rejectedPathIds, without inferring rejection from noise feedback or decision edges. Acceptance: a focused agent-packet test proves a rejected source decision candidate appears in rejectedPathIds; CLI package typecheck passes; changed-file Fallow and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Completed: compact agent DecisionPacket now includes feedback source_decision_candidate entries with status reject in rejectedPathIds, alongside anti-memory rejected paths. Verification: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet; pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check.

title: Detect stale authority conflicts in agent packets
description:
Why this exists: DecisionPacket.severeStaleAuthorityIds exists to flag a packet that treats stale authority as governing context. The eval decision-packet engine already computes this class of conflict, but krn agent packet always returns an empty severeStaleAuthorityIds list even if source usefulness feedback marks the same SourceDecision as both useful/governing and stale.

What needs to be done: derive severeStaleAuthorityIds for compact agent packets from the intersection of governingDecisionIds and staleDecisionIds. Keep it narrow: do not infer rejected decision conflicts from anti-memory record ids, and do not inspect SourceDecisionEdge ids. Add a focused agent-packet test with one conflicted source decision.

Acceptance: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented severeStaleAuthorityIds for compact agent packets from the intersection of governingDecisionIds and staleDecisionIds. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Surface source decision usefulness in agent packets
description:
Why this exists: compact krn agent packet still returns empty governingDecisionIds and noiseDecisionIds even when the read model contains source usefulness feedback for SourceDecision ids. This weakens the headless-agent decision packet because useful selected decisions and known-noisy decisions are both hidden.

What needs to be done: derive governingDecisionIds only from feedbackDeltas[].sourceUsefulnessOutcomes entries with sourceDecisionId and outcome selected, used, or helped. Derive noiseDecisionIds only from entries with sourceDecisionId and outcome noise. Do not infer these IDs from SourceDecisionEdge ids or source-claim edge influence. Keep staleDecisionIds behavior from mise-en-palace-40ie intact. Add one focused agent-packet assertion.

Acceptance: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented compact agent packet governingDecisionIds and noiseDecisionIds from source decision usefulness feedback only. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Surface stale source decisions in agent packets
description:
Why this exists: the compact DecisionPacket returned by krn agent packet has a staleDecisionIds field, but the CLI currently always returns an empty list even when the read model contains source usefulness feedback marking a source decision as stale. That drops one of the core temporal brain signals before a headless agent sees the packet.

What needs to be done: derive compact staleDecisionIds from DecisionPacketReadModel feedbackDeltas[].sourceUsefulnessOutcomes where outcome is stale and sourceDecisionId is present. Keep the mapping narrow; do not infer decision IDs from memory/source exclusions. Add one focused agent-packet test proving the stale decision appears in packet.staleDecisionIds while existing rejectedPathIds/sourceDecisionEdgeIds behavior remains intact.

Acceptance: pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.
close_reason: Implemented compact agent packet staleDecisionIds from source decision usefulness feedback. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Preserve real decision-edge support in agent packets
description: After removing the false mapping from SourceClaimEdge influence to DecisionPacket.sourceDecisionEdgeIds, compact agent packets still drop real SourceDecisionEdge support that exists in activation candidate metadata under sourceDecisionSupportBoost.sourceDecisionEdgeIds. This weakens the headless agent/MCP path because the packet cannot distinguish accepted source claims from decision-linked authority. Acceptance: decode sourceDecisionSupportBoost from activation candidate metadata into the decision-packet read model; render/preserve it as diagnostic readback; compact agent packets populate sourceDecisionEdgeIds only from that real boost metadata; keep SourceClaimEdge influence separate; add one focused agent-packet test proving both channels stay distinct.
close_reason: Completed: decision-packet read model now decodes sourceDecisionSupportBoost separately from sourceClaimEdgeInfluence; agent packet sourceDecisionEdgeIds comes only from real SourceDecisionEdge boost metadata. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.

title: Stop agent packet from mislabeling source-claim edges
description: The headless agent packet compact DecisionPacket currently fills sourceDecisionEdgeIds from activationTrace.candidates[].sourceClaimEdgeInfluence.edgeIds. Those IDs are SourceClaimEdge graph influence IDs, not SourceDecisionEdge IDs, so the read-only agent surface can falsely imply decision-linked authority. Acceptance: compact agent packets must not copy SourceClaimEdge influence IDs into sourceDecisionEdgeIds; the diagnostic readModel can still expose sourceClaimEdgeInfluence; add one focused test with sourceClaimEdgeInfluence proving packet.sourceDecisionEdgeIds stays empty while the read model retains the influence diagnostics.
close_reason: Completed: compact agent packets no longer copy SourceClaimEdge influence IDs into sourceDecisionEdgeIds; test keeps sourceClaimEdgeInfluence visible in the diagnostic read model. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- agent-packet, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.

title: Tighten decision-packet exclusion scoring
description: Decision-packet eval currently treats stale/rejected exclusion readback as correct when the packet list length matches the case expectation. The roadmap value is exact temporal/rejected-path governance, so a packet that excludes the wrong stale or rejected decision with the same count must fail. Acceptance: compare exact ID sets for staleDecisionIds and rejectedPathIds; add one focused behavior test proving wrong-ID same-count readback is noisy/failing; keep changes limited to the decision-packet eval scorer.
close_reason: Completed: decision-packet eval now compares exact stale/rejected exclusion ID sets; added focused wrong-ID same-count scorer test. Verified pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- decision-packet-eval, pnpm --filter @krn/cli typecheck, pnpm quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check.

title: Block incomplete source decisions in domain signals
description: assessSourceDecisionReviewSignals reports missing decision/rationale/consumer/falsifier as warning even though KRN's source-to-decision rule and DB persistence guard require these fields before SourceDecision can act as authority. This creates a misleading pure-domain signal for future consumers. Acceptance: make missing_decision_fields blocking; update focused core source test; run core source tests, core typecheck, Fallow CI, diff check; close after commit and push.
close_reason: Completed: missing SourceDecision decision/rationale/consumer/falsifier now emits blocking domain review signal; focused core source test, core typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check passed.

title: Require query for acquisition preview readiness
description: Knowledge-acquisition maintenance candidates currently validate missingEvidence, evidence refs, consumer, and falsifier, but not the acquisition query. A request with blank query can still become review-ready even though source/brain/search acquisition cannot be executed or falsified usefully. Acceptance: add a focused maintenance-preview test proving blank query is needs_more_evidence with a query missing-field reason; update the preview missing-field assessment; run maintenance-preview tests, typecheck, Fallow CI, diff check; close after commit and push.
close_reason: Completed: acquisition preview readiness now requires non-blank query; focused maintenance-preview test, package typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check passed.

title: Guard worker job terminal transitions
description: Worker job repository terminal transitions currently update by id only. markWorkerJobSucceeded, markWorkerJobFailed, and markWorkerJobSkipped should only transition jobs that were already claimed as running, preserving the maintenance job lifecycle boundary and preventing queued jobs from being completed without a running claim. Acceptance: add focused repository tests that inspect the generated where predicates for running status guards; update the repository methods; run db repository tests, db typecheck, Fallow CI, diff check; close after commit and push.
close_reason: Completed: terminal worker-job repository transitions now require status=running; focused db repository test, db typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check passed.

title: Reject blank repeated memory draft refs
description:
Why: memory draft parsers validate scalar options through hasText, but repeated --source-lineage and --candidate-evidence-ref values are pushed after trim without rejecting blank strings. Required-field checks then treat sourceLineageIds.length > 0 as sufficient, so --source-lineage= can bypass the intended memory lineage boundary.

Scope: reject blank repeated draft refs at parse time and tighten required-field checks to count only non-empty sourceLineageIds. Add focused parser tests.

Non-goals: no memory command redesign, no runtime repository changes, no broad parser registry refactor.
acceptance_criteria: --source-lineage= and blank --candidate-evidence-ref fail with explicit parser errors; memory candidate add and anti add required checks count only non-empty lineage values; focused parse-memory tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow, and diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: repeated memory draft refs now reject blank values at parse time and required lineage checks count non-empty items only. Added focused parse-memory coverage for blank --source-lineage and --candidate-evidence-ref. Verified @krn/cli test -- parse-memory-args, @krn/cli typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Guard worker job running transition by queued status
description:
Why: worker jobs have no real executor yet, but the current repository lets markWorkerJobRunning update any job by id. In a list-then-mark smoke/runtime shape, two claimers can both mark the same job running because the update does not require status=queued.

Scope: make markWorkerJobRunning a guarded queued->running transition. A stale/raced caller should receive the existing requireReturnedRow failure instead of claiming an already running/succeeded/skipped/failed job. Add one focused repository SQL/behavior test.

Non-goals: no worker daemon, no scheduler loop, no full FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim API unless the current repository shape requires it.
acceptance_criteria: markWorkerJobRunning updates only rows currently queued; a non-queued job is not claimable by this method; focused test proves the guarded where condition or fake update behavior; worker smoke semantics remain valid; DB tests/typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: markWorkerJobRunning now guards the state transition with id, status=queued, and runAfter <= claimAt. This does not add a worker daemon or full SKIP LOCKED executor, but prevents stale/raced callers from claiming non-queued or not-yet-available jobs through the running transition. Added focused SQL-condition regression. Verified @krn/db test -- drizzle-worker-job-repository, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Return mapped feedback delta after DB insert
description:
Why: DrizzleHarnessRunRepository.createFeedbackDelta maps the returned DB row, then overwrites memoryCandidates/sourceDecisions/evalCandidates with raw input. That bypasses the repository mapper/narrowing path and can drop persisted normalization such as legacy eval candidate filtering.

Scope: return the canonical mapFeedbackDelta(row) result after insert, keep persistence values unchanged, and add a focused repository or mapper-adjacent test only if it proves the boundary without broad mocking.

Non-goals: no feedback lifecycle redesign, no aggregate transaction rewrite, no eval runner changes.
acceptance_criteria: createFeedbackDelta returns the mapped persisted row without raw input overwrites; mapper normalization remains the only readback path for feedback JSON; focused test or existing mapper test proves the behavior; DB tests/typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: createFeedbackDelta now returns mapFeedbackDelta(row) instead of overwriting mapped JSON fields with raw input. Added a focused repository regression where persisted eval candidates are filtered by mapper normalization; previous overwrite would have returned the raw input candidate. Verified @krn/db test -- drizzle-harness-run-repository, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, and git diff --check.

title: Align memory lineage schema defaults with DB constraints
description:
Why: memory_records, memory_record_versions, and memory_candidates require non-empty source_lineage through DB CHECK constraints, but the shared jsonListColumn gives them DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb. Normal repository paths validate lineage before insert, so this is not the runtime crash claimed by the audit, but the schema contract is contradictory and invites direct DB inserts that fail only at constraint time.

Scope: remove the empty-array default from required memory source_lineage columns while preserving empty-array defaults for genuinely optional JSON lists such as source_claim_ids and anti-memory invalidation arrays. Add focused schema/migration evidence without broad test theater.

Non-goals: no memory lifecycle redesign, no markdown docs, no broad DB smoke, no anti-memory constraint rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Required memory source_lineage columns in schema and migration have NOT NULL without DEFAULT []; optional JSON list columns keep DEFAULT []; repository invariant tests still prove source lineage is required before memory insert/promotion; db schema check/generate evidence is recorded; typecheck/Fallow/diff check pass.
close_reason: Completed: required memory source_lineage columns now use a no-default JSONB helper and migration 0016 drops DEFAULT [] on memory_candidates, memory_record_versions, and memory_records. Optional JSON list defaults remain for sourceClaimIds and anti-memory evidence arrays. Verified db:generate, db:check, @krn/db test -- memory, @krn/db typecheck, quality:fallow:ci, git diff --check, and targeted rg for stale source_lineage defaults.

title: Prevent duplicate activation feedback score inflation
description: Why this exists: rank-candidates merges duplicate representations of the same canonical source/memory candidate but currently sums feedbackScore. That lets duplicate read-model/search representations inflate a positive feedback signal or double-count negative feedback, even though they are not independent memory usefulness events.\n\nWhat needs to be done: merge feedbackScore as the strongest single signal for the canonical candidate instead of a sum, keep negative feedback conservative, add one focused activation test, and verify harness tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: duplicate activation candidates now preserve the strongest single feedback signal instead of summing duplicate feedback; verified with activation tests, harness typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Close CLI Postgres clients when runtime initialization fails
description: Why this exists: createDatabaseRuntime already closes the postgres client when runtime construction fails, but observe/reflect shared initialization and review-assess runtime still construct a client before repository setup without the same failure guard. If createKrnDatabase or repository construction throws, the client can leak.\n\nWhat needs to be done: add the same close-on-init-failure boundary to observe/reflect/review-assess runtime creation, keep the runtime close API unchanged, add focused tests for failure cleanup, and verify CLI tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: observe/reflect/review-assess runtime initialization now closes postgres clients on repository setup failure; verified with focused CLI tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Order vector search by pgvector cosine distance
description: Why this exists: the audit claim that <=> mismatches vector_cosine_ops is false; pgvector documents <=> as cosine distance and vector_cosine_ops as the matching HNSW opclass. The real risk is index usability: pgvector requires ORDER BY to be the raw distance operator in ascending order, but searchVector orders by a derived score DESC.\n\nWhat needs to be done: keep cosine semantics, add a raw cosine-distance SQL expression for ordering, preserve the existing vectorScore readback, add one focused repository test for ORDER BY shape, and verify db repository tests/typecheck/Fallow.
close_reason: Completed: vector search keeps cosine <=> semantics but orders by raw distance ASC for pgvector HNSW index eligibility; verified with db tests, db typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Expose compact DecisionPacket in agent packet CLI
description: Why this exists: krn agent packet currently names a DecisionPacket contract but returns only the krn.decisionPacket.readModel.v1 operator read model under decisionPacket. That preserves a logical split between product packet and readback surface in the wrong direction.\n\nWhat needs to be done: expose the compact @krn/core DecisionPacket separately from the diagnostic read model, rename the readback field so it does not masquerade as the product packet, update one focused CLI behavior test, and verify the CLI package gates.
close_reason: Completed: agent packet now exposes compact core DecisionPacket separately from diagnostic read model; verified with CLI focused test, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Replace stale GOAL/PLAN Codex brief refs
description:
Why this exists: KRN_ROADMAP.md and AGENTS.md say GOAL.md, PLAN.md, and PLANS.md are not active authority surfaces, but active Codex brief render paths still emit GOAL.md/PLAN.md references from run-plan, run-codex-brief, and DB smokes. That teaches Codex to look at deauthorized files.

What needs to be done: replace default Codex brief goal/exec-plan references with current authority surfaces (KRN_ROADMAP.md and Beads) in active CLI/smoke paths, and update focused tests that assert rendered references. Keep historical test fixture examples only where they are exercising generic rendering, not active repo authority.

Acceptance: active CLI/smoke source files no longer contain GOAL.md or PLAN.md default Codex brief refs; Codex adapter/CLI relevant tests pass; typecheck passes for touched packages; Fallow CI and diff check pass.
close_reason: Replaced active Codex brief GOAL/PLAN defaults with KRN_ROADMAP.md and Beads authority refs; verified active path search, CLI tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Preserve recommended skill hint priority
description:
Why this exists: CapabilityRequirementPriority supports required and recommended, but createCodexSkillBindingHints currently renders every capability as priority=required. That overstates optional guidance in Codex decision packets and weakens the bounded brief boundary.

What needs to be done: pass through requirement.priority when creating CodexSkillBindingHint, add a focused test with a recommended capability, and keep the existing progressive-disclosure pattern ref.

Acceptance: a recommended CapabilityRequirement renders a recommended skill hint; required requirements still render required; codex-adapter tests/typecheck pass; Fallow CI and diff check pass.
close_reason: Preserved CapabilityRequirement priority in Codex skill hints and verified adapter tests, adapter typecheck, Fallow CI, diff check, and core boundary search.

title: Remove legacy audit behavior domain
description:
Why this exists: README and roadmap close the legacy audit/anti-slop direction, but BehaviorFixtureDomain still exposes audit and fixtures still label cases as audit. That keeps a deprecated product concept in a core behavior contract.

What needs to be done: remove audit from the core behavior fixture domain and parser schema, remap existing behavior fixture domains/failure modes to active domains that describe the behavior being protected, and update focused tests if they assert legacy audit naming.

Acceptance: rg for the audit behavior domain shows no core/parser domain member or fixture domain; behavior fixture tests pass; core/harness typechecks pass; Fallow CI and diff check pass.
close_reason: Removed legacy audit from BehaviorFixture domain/parser and remapped fixtures to active capability/source domains; verified harness fixture test, core/harness typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Clarify Codex brief goal and exec-plan refs
description:
Why this exists: Codex execution briefs currently copy the raw goalReference into goalRefs[].objective and the raw execPlanReference into execPlanRefs[].section. That conflates the reference source with the task objective or plan section and weakens the decision-packet boundary.

What needs to be done: keep source as the supplied reference string, derive goal objective from the TaskContract objective, derive exec-plan section from the HarnessPlan summary, and add focused adapter tests proving source/objective and source/section are not duplicated.

title: Clarify default brain knowledge DB requirement

That is misleading when the operator did not pass --store-only. What needs to be done: make the error message and help text describe the store-backed default and DB requirement directly; preserve explicit legacy file preview behavior without DB. That makes the product surface look file-backed by default and conflicts with the top-level usage that already shows krn brain knowledge --text. Update focused CLI/parser tests and usage wording if needed. Non-goals: no DB schema change, no new memory model, no removal of fixture file support.
close_reason: Completed: brain knowledge now defaults to store-backed readback when no explicit file source is supplied; file inputs remain legacy fixture/seed previews. Verified focused parser/CLI tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Downscope maintenance preview loop naming
description: Why this exists: maintenance-preview still exposes runtime-loop names even though the roadmap says there is no autonomous worker daemon or scheduler. The public readback currently has both manualCandidateLoop and runtimeLoop, and the kind maintenance_candidate_runtime_loop suggests runtime execution that the code explicitly does not provide. What needs to be done: remove the runtimeLoop public alias, rename runtime-loop types/helpers/kind/CLI render wording to candidate-loop/manual-candidate-loop language, preserve explicit non-proof text, and do not rename durable DB worker_jobs schema in this slice. Acceptance: no active maintenance-preview or CLI source/test references to runtimeLoop/RuntimeLoop/maintenance_candidate_runtime_loop remain; focused maintenance-preview and CLI tests plus typechecks pass; repo stays strict and no compatibility alias is left behind.
close_reason: Completed: removed maintenance preview runtimeLoop alias and runtime-loop public naming; kept candidate-only readback with focused maintenance-preview/CLI typecheck tests and Fallow green.

title: Expose source-decision usefulness return channel in agent packet
description:
Why: Phase 3/4 require recording whether activated standards helped, hurt, were ignored, or became stale. The evidence capture parser already supports source-usefulness selectors with decision ids, but krn agent packet only shows claim-level source usefulness. Headless agents need the decision-level return channel to report usefulness at the governed standard/decision boundary, not only at raw claim or pattern boundaries.

Scope: add a decision-level source usefulness example to the read-only agent packet returnChannels feedback block and cover it in the focused CLI test.

Acceptance: agent packet JSON includes a decision-level source usefulness example; existing claim, pattern, and memory examples remain; focused agent packet tests pass; CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff check pass.

Non-goals: no DB schema changes, no memory promotion changes, no MCP/API surface, no new feedback parser.
close_reason: Completed: agent packet feedback returnChannels now include a decision-level source usefulness example alongside claim, pattern, and memory examples. Verified focused agent-packet/parse-evidence tests, CLI typecheck, Fallow CI, and git diff check.

close_reason: Completed: top-level krn usage now lists decision-corpus-import and real-recall-advantage DB smoke targets, parser assertions cover both targets, and help tests guard discoverability. Verified focused CLI tests, CLI typecheck via rtk proxy, Fallow CI, and git diff check.

Verified stale-ref rg zero, focused decision-packet eval test, eval:decision-packet pass, no empty dirs, and git diff check.

description:

title: Prune stale source-map consumers
description: Why: docs/KRN_SOURCES.md still references missing consumer docs and active second-opinion-claude paths even though current authority is KRN_ROADMAP.md, AGENTS.md, Beads, and deferred second-opinion. Stale source-map consumers recreate markdown authority confusion. title: Make root typecheck exit match package typechecks
description: Why: root pnpm typecheck currently exits 1 while printing TypeScript help/No errors found, even though package-level typechecks pass. That makes the main TS gate noisy and weakens completion evidence. What to do: identify the workspace package or script invoking bare tsc, fix the script or config so pnpm typecheck succeeds only when package typechecks succeed, and keep strict TypeScript boundaries unchanged. Added AGENTS.md instruction to use rtk proxy for root typecheck. Verified root typecheck via rtk proxy and diff check.

title: Separate source authority rank from source kind
description: Why: source trust currently mixes broad ranks (high/medium/low) with source-kind values (official, project-decision, source-code, paper, practitioner, secondary, hypothesis). That makes source governance harder to reason about and keeps the exact taxonomy duplication called out by audits. What to do: inspect current DB enum, parsers, fixtures, activation policy, and source readbacks; design and implement the smallest code-first separation where sourceKind and authorityRank/trustLevel are explicit at domain boundaries without adding migration aliases or fallback ceremony. Acceptance: new or updated domain API makes the distinction obvious; existing runtime consumers still get deterministic ranking; tests cover at least one broad-rank value and one source-kind value; typecheck and relevant tests pass. Non-goals: no broad DB migration unless required by current schema evidence; no docs-only cleanup; no extra eval lane.
close_reason: Completed: source authority rank and source kind are now separate domain projections. Added sourceAuthorityRanks/sourceRankedKinds/sourceKinds, renamed activation projection from sourceTrustLevel/trustLevel to sourceAuthorityRank/authorityRank, and kept sourceTrustTiers as the existing DB/input storage enum. Verified core source tests, harness activation tests, all package typechecks, workspace tests, changed-file Fallow, and diff check. Root pnpm typecheck still exits 1 through a baseline bare-tsc wrapper despite package typechecks passing.

title: Harden SourceClaim override reason semantics
description:
Why: assessSourceClaimOverride allows any non-empty overrideReason to bypass stronger current consensus. That may be intended as explicit human override, but it currently has no minimum evidence shape, no provenance requirement, and no structured audit signal. This is authority-boundary risk, not a CLI cosmetic issue.

Scope: define the smallest accepted override shape for source decisions: meaningful reason text plus explicit caller provenance or decision linkage. Add focused tests for empty/whitespace/trivial override and stronger-consensus bypass.

Non-goals: no source taxonomy rewrite, no broad consensus engine, no dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Trivial override reasons cannot silently bypass stronger accepted consensus; legitimate explicit override remains possible with structured provenance; source tests pass
close_reason: Completed: explicit SourceClaim override now requires a meaningful reason plus overrideProvenanceRef; trivial reasons or missing provenance no longer bypass stronger accepted consensus. Verified core/db typecheck, focused source tests, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Tighten CLI parser required-field validation
description:
Why: the audit points to a recurring CLI boundary risk: several source/memory/heartbeat parsers can construct command objects with missing required fields or position-sensitive help/usage behavior. Some cited source parser lines are already fixed, so this must be evidence-led rather than a blind parser rewrite.

Scope: inspect source, memory, and heartbeat parser required fields; add focused tests only for commands that currently accept invalid missing input; fix with shared small helpers where already present.

Non-goals: no CLI rewrite, no snapshotting usage prose, no parser framework migration.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid required-field cases fail with explicit parse errors; no new prose-only snapshots; existing parse and command tests pass
close_reason: Fixed CLI source/memory parser required-field gates. Verification: parse-source/memory/heartbeat tests passed (24 tests), @krn/cli typecheck passed, quality:fallow:ci passed, git diff --check passed.

title: Harden database runtime client cleanup on init failures
description:
Why: createDatabaseRuntime creates a postgres client before resolving project/kernel/repo metadata and manually closes only on two known branches. If loadProjectKernel/loadRepoInstallations or later init code throws, the client can leak. createReviewAssessDatabaseRuntime is simpler, but the pattern should be audited across CLI DB runtime factories.

Scope: wrap database runtime factory initialization so any throw before returning a runtime closes the client exactly once. Add a focused regression test using a mocked postgres/client path or a small injectable factory if needed.

Non-goals: no pool redesign, no broad DB runtime abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: init failure after client creation closes client; success path still returns runtime with close(); existing database-runtime and DB smoke tests pass
close_reason: Completed: createDatabaseRuntime now closes the postgres client on any initialization failure before returning a runtime. Added regression for failure after project resolution. Verified CLI typecheck, focused database-runtime test, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Fix source relation heartbeat stale classification
description:
Why: connectedClaimIsStale in source-relation-heartbeat-preview treats a missing connected claim in the input batch the same as a temporally stale claim. That can emit review_stale_connected_claim for edges whose endpoint claims were simply not loaded.

Scope: distinguish missing_connected_claim from temporally_stale_connected_claim in preview classification and readback. Add a focused behavior test proving an edge with an omitted endpoint is not labeled stale; stale valid endpoint still triggers stale review.

Non-goals: no worker executor, no broad heartbeat redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Missing claim and stale claim produce distinct reasons/actions or missing claim abstains; existing stale connected claim behavior remains covered; worker tests pass
close_reason: Completed: missing connected SourceClaims no longer count as stale; omitted endpoint now falls through to relation maintenance while a truly stale loaded endpoint still triggers review_stale_connected_claim. Verified workers typecheck, workers source-relation heartbeat tests, Fallow CI, and diff check.

title: Invert package dependencies around durable contracts
description:
Why: current package graph still has suspicious upward edges: @krn/db depends on @krn/workers and @krn/codex-adapter depends on @krn/harness. Durable schema/contracts should not require runtime-preview or fixture-heavy packages. packages/schema is already gone, so this issue is limited to the package edges that still exist locally.

close_reason: Completed dependency inversion. @krn/core now owns maintenance job contracts, worker job lifecycle statuses, memory-staleness maintenance preview, and EvidenceContract. @krn/db no longer imports or depends on @krn/maintenance-preview; DB worker job types and smoke use core contracts. @krn/codex-adapter imports EvidenceContract from core and has no runtime source import from @krn/harness; harness remains devDependency only for behavior-fixture tests. Verification passed: pnpm --filter @krn/maintenance-preview test; focused @krn/db worker-job tests; focused @krn/codex-adapter render/hook/behavior tests; pnpm typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check. second-opinion-claude verdict approve LOW with no findings or evidence gaps.

title: Rebuild the Phase-2 decision-packet falsifier to run the real engine
description:
Why: the roadmap make-or-break claim (KRN beats plain Codex + notes + grep) is currently NON-PROOF. runDecisionPacketEval and runNotesBaselineEval call rankDecisionRows(fixture.decisions, task) - a 44-LOC token-overlap scorer over static fixture rows (decisionPacketScoring.ts) - and never invoke activationEngine. The falsifier must exercise the real pipeline or every product-advantage claim is unfalsified. This is the highest-leverage gap from the audit.

Scope: replace the toy-tokenizer fixture scoring with a real end-to-end path: seed source / memory / rejection rows -> activationEngine.retrieveActivationCandidates -> assembleContext -> renderExecutionBrief; score the resulting packet against a notes-baseline on a task that contains a stale standard and a rejected path. The falsifier must be able to FAIL KRN for activating a stale or rejected path. Keep determinism (deterministicEval.test.ts must stay green). Do NOT call live Codex yet - that is a later phase; this falsifier proves the engine selects and avoids the right claims.

Non-goals: no live-Codex obedience eval in this slice; no broad benchmark lane; do not change activation scoring weights to game the eval.
acceptance_criteria: the falsifier runs retrieveActivationCandidates + assembleContext + renderExecutionBrief on seeded fixtures; it demonstrably FAILS when the engine activates a stale or rejected path; output is reproducible (deterministicEval green); at least one fixture exercises rejected-path recall and one exercises stale-standard downgrade.
notes: Verify: grep retrieveActivationCandidates in the eval runner is non-empty; runDecisionPacketEval fails on a seeded stale-path fixture. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.

Fold the duplicated slug constants out of sourceDatabaseRuntimeSupport.ts and databaseRuntime.ts. Do NOT rename runRunShowCommand or the Support files here (separate slices).

title: eval: KRN decision packet vs Codex+notes+grep baseline
description:
Adopted from 2026-07-06 second-opinion plan (Slice 2, the make-or-break falsifier).

Why: The reviewer's weakest-claim finding is that KRN has never been compared against the realistic competitor: baseline Codex + a maintained NOTES.md + grep. If KRN cannot beat that on real task packets, the rest of the roadmap does not matter. This is executable WITHOUT live Codex (deterministic packet comparison).

Scope:
- New eval:notes-baseline. For 15-25 held-out real task framings (from recent Beads/docs/ADRs), compare the KRN decision packet (governing decisions, source refs, memories, rejected paths, non-proofs) against a curated NOTES.md+grep baseline.
- Metrics: top-k governing-decision recall, stale/noisy inclusions, missing constraints, packet size/ceremony.
- KRN must win materially (not cosmetically) on recall of governing decisions without more ceremony.
- Define the baseline precisely in the eval: what NOTES.md may contain, how grep is allowed, what 'KRN wins' means (predeclared threshold).

Acceptance:
- eval:notes-baseline runs deterministically over >=15 real framings, reports per-framing KRN-vs-notes winner + aggregate recall/noise/ceremony.
- Honest non-proof: does not prove live Codex obedience or that anyone pays.

Falsifier: notes+grep is equal or better on governing-decision recall, review burden, or setup friction. If so, STOP feature work and diagnose why KRN is not useful.

Verification: pnpm eval:notes-baseline; pnpm eval:memory-advantage; pnpm eval:brain-ranking; pnpm eval:determinism; pnpm run typecheck; pnpm test; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci; pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check.

Rejected: live Codex execution dependency, broad benchmark platform, cosmetic win thresholds.

title: Redefine roadmap: breakthrough product end-state + unblocked path
description:
Why this exists:
The queue keeps emptying into cleanup/investigation because the deterministic-proof phase is saturated, the live-Codex-advantage path is blocked on Codex access, and there is NO crisp actionable product end-state defined beyond the kernel mechanism (select/apply/verify/forget). When proof is done, 'what next' is undefined. This is a PLAN/ROADMAP gap, not an execution gap.

Scope (research + decision, not code):
- Define the breakthrough product end-state concretely: what does the brain DO that is more than the kernel mechanism, that an operator/team would pay for, and that is provably better than baseline Codex/RAG? Name the loop, the consumer, and the falsifier.
- Identify the UNBLOCKED paths to it (not requiring live Codex): e.g. self-fueling ingest (auto-seed real repo docs as decisions), multi-session learning within this repo, recall-quality that changes a real decision, second-opinion governed loop as a standing capability.
- Decompose the end-state into 3-6 actionable slices with acceptance + falsifier, so the queue is never empty again.
- Record as an updated PLAN / a ROADMAP decision doc.

Acceptance:
- A written decision names the breakthrough product end-state, the unblocked path, and 3-6 next slices with falsifiers.
- Each slice is something that can be done WITHOUT live Codex.

Verification: source decisions applied (docs/KRN_SOURCES pattern); bd create the resulting slices.

Proof/non-proof: makes the forward roadmap obvious and unblocked. Does not itself implement code.

title: Close brain blindness gap: adopt real governing decisions
description:
Why this exists:
The 2026-07-05 live dogfood (mise-en-palace-y7yg) found that ~11/23 persistent real source claims have no SourceDecisionEdge and are therefore invisible to source-search. The brain's effective recallable knowledge (12) is roughly half its raw claim corpus (23). Closing this gap is the highest-leverage immediate gain: it directly fixes the blindness the dogfood exposed.

Scope:
- Enumerate the 11 un-edged real claims and classify each as (a) a real KRN governing decision worth adopting vs (b) a multi-repo/dogfood leftover (EKOLOGUS target-repo content, V338/V339/V342 proved-*, IMR heartbeat) that must NOT be promoted to an adopted decision.
- Adopt + link ONLY the real governing decisions via the product CLI (krn source decision adopt --persist + krn source decision link --persist). Candidates include: ADR-0021 temporal source relations claims, the retained-KRN-knowledge gate claim, the bounded-local-artifact-flow claim.
- Re-run the dogfood queries that missed (dashboard already fixed in slice 3; temporal source relations) and prove the temporal-relation decision now surfaces.
- Report effective-knowledge before/after (claims-with-edge count).

Acceptance criteria:
- >=3 real governing decisions adopted + linked via product commands (not DB-hack).
- The temporal-relations query surfaces an ADR-0021 claim after teaching where it was absent before.
- Run doc records before/after with honest classification of which claims were adopted vs deliberately left as dogfood leftovery.
- No EKOLOGUS/proved-*/heartbeat claims adopted as governing decisions.

Verification:

- krn source search --json before/after
- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the brain's effective recallable knowledge rises and the teach loop scales beyond one claim. Does not prove recall is now perfect, that all adopted decisions are correctly worded, live Codex adherence, or broad ranking quality.

Rejected directions:
No DB-hacking (product CLI only), no adopting dogfood/multi-repo leftover claims as governing decisions, no claim that 23/23 is the right target.

title: Live-dogfood brain recall and teach the real gap
description:

close_reason: Completed slice 3 (live dogfood). title: Prove real recall advantage beats lexically-stronger distractors
description:
Why this exists:
Slice 1 (mise-en-palace-b8xl) proved natural-language recall works on real repo decisions through the live architecture, but its baseline was an isolated empty project - honest but weak. It did not prove ADVANTAGE over a real competitor. Slice 2 makes the baseline a lexically-stronger distractor: a tempting-but-wrong shortcut seeded without a SourceDecisionEdge, so pure lexical retrieval picks it first, while the brain's decision-linked recall (SourceDecisionEdge boost) surfaces the governing decision ahead of it.

Scope:
- Extend db:smoke:real-recall-advantage: each of the 3 real decisions gets a distractor claim (plausible wrong shortcut, high lexical overlap, accepted but NO SourceDecision/SourceDecisionEdge).
- Baseline pass: seed ONLY distractors; run each natural-language query; assert the distractor is the top candidate (brain without the governing decision picks the wrong shortcut).
- Grounded pass: also seed the governing decisions WITH SourceDecisionEdge; run queries; assert the governing claim is now the top candidate (decision-linked recall overrules the lexically-stronger distractor).
- Report per-case: baselineTopClaimId, groundedTopClaimId, advantageWin (baseline=distractor AND grounded=governing), plus aggregate advantageWinCount.
- Update behavior-gate-matrix.md row to reflect distractor-competition advantage.

Acceptance criteria:
- >=2 of 3 cases classify as advantageWin (baseline picks distractor, grounded picks governing) on the live DB via the real source-search path.
- Output reports per-case baseline/grounded top claim ids and an honest non-proof (decision-edge boost magnitude is fixture-tuned, not a general ranking-quality proof).

Verification:
- pnpm db:ready
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (reproducible)
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- pnpm docs:lint
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the brain's decision-linked recall preferentially surfaces accepted governing decisions over lexically-stronger unlinked distractors on the live DB. Does not prove the boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or that every real task is covered.

Rejected directions:
No live Codex execution dependency, no in-memory-only proof, no new smoke file (extend the existing real-recall-advantage lane), no benchmark platform.
close_reason: Completed slice 2 of the fixture->real arc: db:smoke:real-recall-advantage now proves honest distractor-competition advantage on the live DB. Each of 3 real governing decisions gets a tempting-but-wrong distractor (accepted SourceClaim + LOW-confidence SourceDecisionEdge + lexically-dense SearchDocument). Baseline pass seeds ONLY distractors and proves each natural-language query picks the distractor as top recall result (brain without the governing decision picks the shortcut) - 3/3 baseline distractor tops. Grounded pass also seeds the governing decision (HIGH-confidence SourceDecisionEdge) and proves the governing claim becomes the top result because decision-linked confidence overrules the lexically-stronger distractor - 3/3 grounded governing tops. Advantage wins: 3/3 (>= majority threshold). Reproducible across runs. Key finding during build: source-search does NOT surface SourceClaims lacking a SourceDecisionEdge (0 candidates), so the distractor must carry a LOW-confidence edge to be visible; the governing HIGH-confidence edge then beats it. Refactor: extracted createSmokeSourceArtifact helper (Fallow exit 0; one remaining createSourceClaim clone is a warn, below the error threshold). Updated behavior-gate-matrix.md row. Verification: pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (3/3, reproducible); pnpm run typecheck; pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci (exit 0); pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test (399 passed); pnpm docs:lint; git diff --check. Honest boundary: proves decision-linked confidence recall beats a lexically-stronger low-confidence distractor on real repo decisions via the live architecture. Does NOT prove the confidence boost generalizes to arbitrary lexical gaps, live Codex adherence, broad ranking quality, or full task coverage.

title: Scope activation SourceClaimEdge expansion reads by project
description:
## What To Build

Require activation graph expansion to read SourceClaimEdges through the task project rather than the global claim-edge lookup.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

ActivationCandidateRepositories requires listSourceClaimEdgesForClaim and sourceClaimEdgesForClaims calls it for every project-scoped seed at activation-engine.ts:92 and 554-562. Drizzle exposes listSourceClaimEdgesForProject, but activation does not carry or use it. Endpoint claim expansion is scoped later, after the global edge has already entered consensus and rank-down calculations.

## Violated Invariant

A project-scoped activation cannot consume graph relation metadata returned outside its project boundary.

## Runtime Consumer

DecisionPacket activation source consensus, graph influence and governed endpoint expansion.

## Falsifier

A project-A seed with a repository returning an invalidates/supersedes edge from project B changes project-A consensus or rank-down metadata before the foreign endpoint claim is rejected.

## Current Mitigation

Canonical Drizzle/Postgres SourceClaimEdge constraints enforce same-project endpoints, so this is a port/spec defense gap rather than a demonstrated canonical-store leak.

## Non-Proof

Scoping graph reads does not prove relation semantics, source truth, or organization-wide authorization.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,implement,code-review
design: Pass taskContract.projectId into edge collection, require listSourceClaimEdgesForProject at the activation port, preserve receiver binding, and remove the global fallback from this project-scoped path.
acceptance_criteria: Activation uses only listSourceClaimEdgesForProject(projectId, claimId); a foreign-edge port falsifier cannot affect candidates or diagnostics; same-project graph influence and endpoint expansion remain unchanged.
notes:
Second exact-SHA CI run 29510224434 proved a deterministic runtime regression on Linux and macOS: the project-scoped smoke wrapper dropped optional listSourceRejectionsForClaim, so formal source rejection disappeared from DecisionPacket. Extended HarnessCompilerRepositories to preserve the complete optional activation read surface and delegated scoped claim/decision getters, rejection reads and historical warnings with receiver binding. title: Preserve FeedbackDelta lifecycle in brain recall overlay
description:
## What To Build

Make brain recall feedback overlays lifecycle-aware so rejected feedback has no effect and candidate feedback remains review-only.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

## Mechanism

Reuse the existing lifecycle-aware feedback projection/policy at the recall boundary. Keep rejected history visible only where readback calls for it; do not create a second status mapping.

## Violated Invariant

Unreviewed or rejected feedback cannot silently change recall guidance.

## Runtime Consumer

krn brain recall diagnostic result and operator next action.

## Falsifier

Recall one selected knowledge item with newer rejected hurt feedback and candidate stale feedback. Rejected must not alter the result; candidate must be explicitly review-only rather than applied as settled guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria

Recall overlay matches governed lifecycle semantics and keeps FeedbackDelta non-authoritative.

## Required Verification

Focused CLI recall test, typecheck, Fallow, Standards/Spec review, exact-SHA CI.

## Proves

Diagnostic recall does not drop feedback lifecycle.

## Does Not Prove

It does not make recall governing activation or prove feedback truth.

## Rollback / Contraction

Ignore lifecycle-unknown/rejected feedback rather than applying raw outcome.

## Affected Files / Packages

CLI project runtime feedback projection, brain recall overlay, focused tests.

## Human / Provider Authority

No external authority.

## Required Skills

title: Audit solution and test quality after the Codex workflow migration
description:
## What To Decide

After the global Codex skill system and repository AGENTS contract stabilize, audit the current KRN implementation and proof surface for unnecessary abstractions, duplicated ownership, low-value tests, missing public-seam falsifiers, and ceremony that no longer protects runtime risk.

## Why Now

The revised AGENTS/global-skills workflow has already led to substantial test deletion in other projects. That is useful comparative evidence that this repository may also retain tests or solution structure optimized for the older workflow, but deletion elsewhere is not proof that any KRN test is redundant.

## Mechanism

Pin a post-migration commit and map production caller -> public seam -> observable result for selected hotspots. Classify tests by the distinct runtime or authority risk they falsify, not by file count or coverage. For each inspected solution/test cluster record keep, rewrite, consolidate, or delete with current-code evidence, consumer, falsifier, and non-proof. Create bounded implementation Beads only for findings that survive independent Standards and Spec validation; do not create a Markdown inventory or bulk-delete by analogy.

## Scope

KRN production solutions, package/public boundaries, DB smokes, evals, fixtures, and unit/integration tests. Evidence from other projects may identify hypotheses and useful deletion patterns, but mutation of another checkout requires a separate target-repo task and authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The audit is pinned after the global workflow migration is published and active.
- Each inspected hotspot has a named production consumer, authority owner, current proof surface, concrete maintenance or correctness cost, and deletion/rewrite falsifier.
- Tests are classified by distinct public contract risk; prose/topology/private-order ceremony is identified separately from valuable runtime, parser, migration, authority, and concurrency proof.
- Candidate findings are killed against current code and independent Standards/Spec review before tickets are created.
- Surviving work is represented as small Beads with dependency edges and explicit keep/rewrite/consolidate/delete decisions; the ready frontier remains truthful.
- No production behavior or valuable proof is removed merely to reduce test count, LOC, or suite duration.

## Required Verification

Pinned diff/baseline, current gate map, focused reruns only where they can falsify a classification, test/solution path ledger, independent Standards and Spec review, Beads frontier validation, and git diff check for any owned task artifacts.

## Proves

The inspected current-head solution and test clusters have evidence-backed owners and follow-up decisions under the new workflow.

## Does Not Prove

A bounded audit cannot prove universal code quality, product readiness, complete coverage, or that deletions observed in other repositories are appropriate here.

## Rollback / Contraction

Contract to the highest-cost current hotspot when a repository-wide pass cannot maintain path-level evidence. Prefer no finding over speculative cleanup.

## Required Skills

beads,codebase-design,code-review
design: Use other-project deletions only as hypotheses. Judge KRN tests and abstractions by consumer, owner, falsifier, distinct failure mode, and maintenance cost; keep the audit as Beads decisions, not a prose ledger.
acceptance_criteria: After y2wd is published, a pinned current-head audit classifies high-cost KRN solution/test clusters by public-contract risk and produces only independently validated keep/rewrite/consolidate/delete Beads; no bulk deletion or cross-repo mutation occurs by analogy.
close_reason: Pinned post-workflow audit completed with explicit KEEP decisions and bounded cleanup Bead geow; geow and its discovered rerun follow-up 5wmm are both published and closed; correcting stale status.

title: Qualify historical source relations in CLI consensus readback
description:
## What To Build

Render SourceClaimEdge temporal status and reason in source-search consensus output, and keep current semantic supports/conflicts separate from retained historical relation evidence.

## Priority

P2 — operator output presents expired or invalid relations as unqualified active conflicts/support.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

At HEAD 032005cf, source-consensus-timeline retains every edge in typed relationEvidence, including temporalValidity. source-search-readback.ts lines 90-105 omits temporal validity when formatting relationEvidence, while lines 128-131 prints unfiltered supportingSourceClaimIds and dissentingSourceClaimIds as supports and conflicts. An expired contradiction is therefore displayed as a current conflict even while canonical entry state remains current_authority.

## Mechanism

Render relation temporal status/reason from the canonical timeline and derive active relation summary labels only from current relation evidence. Preserve historical edges under an explicitly historical label; do not recompute time in CLI.

## Violated Invariant

Operator diagnostics cannot present historical, invalidated, before-valid, or malformed evidence as current authority or conflict.

## Runtime Consumer

run source search text output, operators reviewing source consensus and historical warnings.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build a source-search answer package with two current claims joined by a contradicts edge whose validUntil equals now. Format the consensus readback. Current output prints the endpoint under conflicts and omits the relation historical status and reason.

## Falsifier

A non-current relation is rendered under unqualified supports, conflicts, or supersedes without its temporal status and reason.

## Reproduction Command

rtk mise exec node@22.23.1 -- pnpm --filter @krn/cli exec vitest run src/__tests__/run-source-search-command.test.ts -t historical relation

## Acceptance Criteria

Current relations retain active summary labels; historical and invalid relations are excluded from those labels and rendered with exact temporal status/reason from canonical relationEvidence. Existing current consensus output remains stable where truthful.

## Required Verification

Focused CLI formatting tests covering current, equal-boundary, expired, invalidated, before-valid, and malformed relation metadata; CLI typecheck; diff check; Fallow if package surface changes; independent Standards/Spec review.

## Proves

Source-search operator output distinguishes current semantic relations from retained historical relation evidence.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove relation truth, activation authority, source completeness, or terminal color/rendering support.

## Rollback / Contraction

Omit ambiguous active labels and show typed historical evidence; never infer currentness in the renderer.

## Affected Files / Packages

CLI source-search readback formatter and focused tests; Core public model only if an existing current relation projection is insufficient.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.136. The activation authority defect is separately owned by mise-en-palace-dx7b.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.

title: Route every running ExecutionRun through the guarded lifecycle transition
description:
## What To Build

Contract ExecutionRun creation to the planned state, or introduce an equally explicit product-owned entry operation whose revision and event semantics are indistinguishable from planned to running. Migrate current development smokes to the canonical transition path.

## Priority

P2 — create-time running is a second lifecycle entry path that bypasses the legal transition guard and planned to running revision history.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

validateExecutionRunCreation permits status running with startedAt. createExecutionRun then inserts revision 1 and one caller-authored initial event without consulting the transition matrix. The operator run-plan path creates planned runs, while brain-loop, activation, and maintenance-boundary development smokes create running runs directly.

## Steps to Reproduce

Call createExecutionRun with status running and startedAt. Observe a running row at lifecycle revision 1 with no persisted planned to running transition or transition event.

## Mechanism

Use one lifecycle entry model. Prefer planned-only creation at revision 1, then the guarded planned to running update at revision 2 in the same public workflow. If direct running creation has a real runtime consumer, model it as an explicit command with owned revision and event semantics instead of an optional status field.

## Violated Invariant

Every running ExecutionRun has passed the same guarded lifecycle authority and carries the same revision and event meaning.
