title: Detect cross-linked source import lineage during reconciliation
description:
## What To Build

Extend read-only import reconciliation to report structurally cross-linked lineage even when every component cardinality is one.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

Current diagnostics count SourceChunks by artifact and SourceClaims by artifact, but do not prove that the claim sourceChunkId belongs to that same artifact. SearchDocument checks project, claim and decision joins but does not prove its sourceArtifactId/sourceChunkId match the reconciled tuple. Cardinality can therefore look complete while lineage points across same-project tuples.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Persist two complete import tuples in one project.
2. Cross-link the first claim or SearchDocument to the second artifact or chunk while retaining one row of each component type.
3. Run bounded read-only source decision reconciliation and inspect whether the first tuple remains incorrectly complete.

## Mechanism

Add typed lineage violations at the reconciliation query boundary for claim-to-chunk and search-document-to-artifact/chunk coherence, retaining exact IDs and bounded output.

## Runtime Consumer

Integrity operators using source decision reconcile to identify partial or conflicting imported authority graphs.

## Falsifier

Cross-link a claim or SearchDocument to another same-project artifact/chunk while leaving all component counts at one; reconciliation still reports lifecycle complete.

## Required Verification

Disposable PostgreSQL fixture with one cross-linked tuple, exact violation and IDs, read-only transaction assertion, typecheck, Fallow and exact-SHA CI.

## Does Not Prove

Does not prove semantic source truth, evidence freshness, or safe automated repair.
design: Treat lineage coherence as a first-class typed structural invariant alongside component cardinality, without adding a repair path.
acceptance_criteria: A same-project cross-linked claim or SearchDocument is reported partial with exact typed lineage violations and component IDs while reconciliation remains bounded and read-only.
close_reason: Duplicate follow-up: SourceClaim legacy probe is owned by .36 and SearchDocument provenance integrity probe by .32; reconciliation-specific parallel ownership would fragment the same invariant.

title: Review counter reconciliation race and ranking neutrality

Reconciliation equals canonical applications at one snapshot and cannot reorder equal memories merely by repair time.

title: Report bounded source coverage without claiming universal completeness

## Consumer

Import readback, operator source review, DecisionPacket evidence gaps, and the final Phase-7 evidence decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Omitting one declared row or captured evidence reference yields incomplete.
- A fully captured declared manifest yields declared_scope_complete, never generic complete or true.

- Remote availability loss after capture preserves captured time, digest, and freshness state.
- Packet and readback retain doesNotProve for semantic truth and unknown external sources.

## Falsifier

A finite fixture or green import reports source or corpus completeness without declaring the checked universe.

Proof: complete, incomplete, and unknown fixtures plus exact readback and packet behavior.

Non-proof: declared-scope completeness does not prove universal completeness, semantic truth, unbiased selection, or remote freshness.

If no consumer uses a coverage manifest, retain unknown plus explicit evidence gaps. Do not add discovery machinery.

None.

## Mechanism To Evaluate
Treat a skill document as trainable external agent state; propose bounded add/delete/replace edits from rollout evidence; accept only if held-out validation improves; retain rejected edits as negative feedback; export compact validated skill artifacts.

## KRN Implication
Potentially informs repo-local skills, loop engineering, and future skills optimization without turning KRN into a markdown brain.

## Consumer
KRN skills workflow, future loop-engineering automation, and source-to-decision intake.

## Non-Goals
No immediate code changes, no automatic skill mutation, no new docs forest, no broad benchmark lane, no external reviewer gate.

design: Use source-to-decision: source -> mechanism -> KRN implication -> decision/rejection -> consumer -> falsifier. comments.author: korneliuszburian
comments.text:
Source intake: Matt Pocock skills repo @ d574778f94cf620fcc8ce741584093bc650a61d3.

Decision summary: do not install/copy upstream skills wholesale. KRN already has repo-local versions of the mechanisms that matter, adapted to Beads, KRN_ROADMAP, source-to-decision, anti-markdown-runtime-memory, and anti-test-theater.

Adopted mechanisms already present:
- code-review: two-axis Standards/Spec review + Fowler smell baseline. KRN local skill adds KRN-specific smells: Test Theater, Prompt/Context Bloat, Markdown Authority Drift. Consumer: review larger diffs/migrations. Falsifier: a review merges spec drift with style smells or praises green tests as product proof.
- codebase-design: deep modules, interface/seam/adapter/deletion-test/dependency categories. Consumer: architecture/naming/refactor slices. Falsifier: adding a seam with one real adapter, shallow pass-through module, or tests past the interface.
- tdd: red-green at public seams, anti-tautology, anti-horizontal tests. Consumer: parser/runtime/authority bug fixes. Falsifier: a test freezes prose/topology or passes without observing the behavior under change.
- to-tickets/wayfinder: tracer-bullet issues, native blockers, frontier. Consumer: Beads. Falsifier: creating tickets.md/markdown map or prose-only blockers instead of Beads dependencies.
- writing-great-skills: predictability, progressive disclosure, no-op/sediment/sprawl pruning. Consumer: future skill edits via global skill-creator/writing-great-skills. Falsifier: adding model-invoked repo skills whose trigger duplicates existing skills or whose body is mostly no-op prose.

Rejected upstream shapes:
- research: rejects Markdown-file output. Mechanism (primary-source research) is useful, but KRN consumer must be source-to-decision, Beads, store-backed candidates, or eval candidates; not a notes file.
- to-spec: rejects publishing conversation-derived specs as a separate spec artifact by default. KRN source of active work is Beads; architecture truth is KRN_ROADMAP.
- implement: rejects as too thin and duplicative of AGENTS + Beads + TDD + code-review workflow.
- prototype: defer. Useful only for explicit throwaway logic/UI questions; no current KRN consumer and no dashboard/UI work allowed by roadmap.
- domain-modeling upstream shape: rejects CONTEXT.md/ADR creation. KRN local domain-modeling resolves terminology at owning code/roadmap/Beads boundary instead.

Does not prove: upstream skills are globally best, local skill behavior is perfect, future skill edits need no review, or KRN should create a broad skill platform.

close_reason: Removed decorative Codex brief surfaces: skillBindingHints, hookExpectations, mcpResourceRefs, and subagentProbeHints are no longer part of ExecutionBrief or rendered product brief. description:

Scope: keep the fast CI gate, but add an explicit full-repo hygiene command/lane for periodic or local cleanup review. Remove stale ignores for packages that no longer exist and keep exceptions narrow and justified.

Non-goals: do not treat Fallow as automatic truth; do not delete fixtures/runtime files without owner evidence; do not make the full audit required on every tiny slice.
acceptance_criteria: Stale Fallow ignores are removed or justified; a documented pnpm command produces a full-repo hygiene report; changed-file CI behavior remains fast; true positives are either fixed or converted into narrow explicit exceptions with owner evidence.
close_reason: Completed: removed stale packages/schema/** Fallow ignore after confirming packages/schema is absent; added pnpm quality:fallow:report as a non-blocking whole-repo hygiene snapshot writing dead/dupe and health reports under .local-lab/fallow; kept pnpm quality:fallow:ci as the fast changed-file gate; documented the report command in README without adding new docs. Verified: pnpm quality:fallow:report exits 0 while reporting current backlog, pnpm quality:fallow alias exits 0, pnpm quality:fallow:ci passes for changed files, package/config JSON parse, git diff --check. Current full-repo findings were not auto-deleted; follow-up Bead mise-en-palace-yk2m captures the 23 dead-code findings and 3 duplication groups for owner-evidence triage.

title: Budget the Codex decision brief profile
description:
Why: codex-adapter brief rendering has accumulated optional/meta sections. The product surface should be a bounded decision packet, not a prompt junk drawer. After the product type and observation-prefix decision are resolved, shrink the required profile and gate optional sections by real consumers.

Scope: define the minimal decision-packet brief profile for packages/codex-adapter/src/render-execution-brief.ts and contracts.ts; add section/token budget behavior; omit reserved sections unless backed by a current consumer.

Non-goals: no provider-neutral adapter rewrite, no live-Codex eval requirement, no prose snapshot tests, no adding new sections.
acceptance_criteria: Required profile is explicit and small; optional/reserved sections render only when the input has a current consumer; budget behavior is deterministic; tests assert section presence/absence and budget behavior rather than exact prose; brief still carries objective, selected standards, rejected paths, evidence/proof boundaries, tool boundaries, and stop condition.
close_reason: Completed: Codex brief profile now reports deterministic budget readback, omits empty diagnostic/reserved sections, keeps required execution/proof/tool boundaries, and tests within/over budget behavior. title: Resolve DecisionPacket naming void: name the product type OR retire the roadmap term
description:
OPERATOR DECISION. Why: the roadmap names DecisionPacket as the operator-facing product (line 45) and a target type (line 522), but NO DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core or @krn/harness (grep for interface/type/class DecisionPacket in core/harness = ZERO; only CLI eval fixtures use the name). The real product is split across three names: ContextAssembly (core/contextAssembly.ts), ExecutionBrief (codex-adapter/renderExecutionBrief.ts), and RunReadbackResource (cli/runShowReadback.ts, 1098 LOC, the de-facto read model). A new agent reading the roadmap then the code cannot map DecisionPacket to any single type. Phase 2 (Decision-Packet Falsifier) has no named target.

Scope: operator picks ONE. (a) Introduce a thin DecisionPacket type in @krn/core composing the already-built ContextAssembly + ExecutionBrief pair, and rename runShowReadback RunReadbackResource to DecisionPacketReadModel (file decisionPacketReadModel.ts); the build/render pair becomes buildDecisionPacket / renderDecisionPacket; keep the CLI verb run show only on the command file. OR (b) edit KRN_ROADMAP.md (lines 45 and 521-531) to retire DecisionPacket in favor of the implemented names. Either branch removes the doc/code drift.

Non-goals: do not change ContextAssembly/ExecutionBrief structure or activation behavior (naming/type-composition only); no batch rename of the 33 run*Command files; do not move runShowReadback out of CLI in this slice (FromMetadata relocation is C3).
acceptance_criteria: If (a): a DecisionPacket type exists in @krn/core, RunReadbackResource renamed to DecisionPacketReadModel, the roadmap term maps to a real type. If (b): KRN_ROADMAP.md edited so no term names a non-existent type. Either way a reader can map the roadmap product name to exactly one code type (or zero, deliberately retired). typecheck + test + decision-packet eval green.
notes: Depends on C3 (FromMetadata relocation) so the read model rename lands on a clean decode layer. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Completed: DecisionPacket is now a real @krn/core type used by the decision-packet eval engine; run show JSON readback is named DecisionPacketReadModel; roadmap maps product/readback terms; local verification and second-opinion approve passed.

title: Rename/downscope workers to maintenance-preview contracts
description:
Why: g1gk resolved the deferred plnv boundary without routing to the operator. Current evidence shows @krn/workers is live contract/readback code, not dead runtime code: packages/workers has preview builders and job contract readbacks; maintenanceJobRuntimeContract.requiresBackgroundLoop is false; KRN_ROADMAP says no autonomous worker daemon or scheduler and says daemon requests should be rejected/deferred without a consumer; doctor readiness marks Redis/Kafka or a broad worker daemon as forbidden; DB smokes prove candidate-only worker boundary readback with no scheduler.

Decision: do not build a worker daemon/executor/loop now. Do not delete the package outright, because db and cli currently consume its contract/readback functions. Execute the conservative downscope branch: rename the package/surface away from runtime vocabulary toward maintenance-preview / maintenance-contract readbacks, remove Heartbeat/worker-execution naming where it implies a running scheduler, and keep candidate-only maintenance proposals reviewable.

Scope: rename @krn/workers to a non-runtime contract/readback package; rename HeartbeatPreview files and CLI heartbeat-preview surfaces to maintenance candidate/proposal/readback names; preserve current candidate preview behavior and DB smoke semantics; remove wording that suggests autonomous execution.

Non-goals: no worker daemon, no scheduler, no queue runtime, no Memory Core mutation automation, no deletion of live preview behavior unless a direct consumer is removed in the same slice.
acceptance_criteria: Package and CLI names no longer imply an autonomous worker runtime; current preview/readback behavior remains available under maintenance-contract terminology; @krn/db no longer depends on a package named workers for durable job contracts; doctor still blocks broad worker runtime; typecheck and focused tests pass; no file asserts runtime authority the code disclaims.
notes: g1gk decision: choose conservative rename/downscope. Evidence refs: KRN_ROADMAP no autonomous worker daemon/scheduler + Phase 6; packages/workers/src/job-types.ts requiresBackgroundLoop false and doesNotProve runtime execution; packages/cli/src/doctor-static-checks.ts forbids broad daemon/Redis/Kafka; packages/db/src/heartbeat-worker-boundary-smoke.ts proves no scheduler/no daemon candidate-only boundary. plnv is superseded by this executable slice.
close_reason: Completed conservative rename/downscope: @krn/workers moved to @krn/maintenance-preview, CLI heartbeat preview surface renamed to maintenance preview, DB smoke renamed to maintenance boundary, package deps/lock updated, stale worker package symbols removed. Verification: @krn/maintenance-preview test passed; focused @krn/cli maintenance/knowledge tests passed; focused @krn/db worker-job/maintenance tests passed; pnpm typecheck passed; pnpm quality:fallow:ci passed; git diff --check passed; stale-symbol grep clean. Full @krn/cli test exposed pre-existing memory candidate promote parser/runtime mismatch; filed mise-en-palace-qcqn.

title: Move FromMetadata deserializers out of @krn/core into the persistence/decode layer
description:
Why: FromMetadata functions parse Record<string,unknown> metadata blobs but live in @krn/core (the domain/contracts layer): sourceUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata + patternUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata (core/feedbackDelta.ts), targetEvidenceFromMetadata (core/evidenceBundle.ts), activationRetrievalDiagnosticsFromMetadata (harness/activation/activationDiagnostics.ts). The FromMetadata suffix advertises the storage shape inside the domain package. This is exactly the pattern AGENTS.md forbids: from X to Y conversion names that expose storage plumbing to product code. The CLI (runShowReadback.ts) then re-reads the same metadata a third time. Must land before the feedback fork fix (9xc1) so the unified read model has a clean home.

Scope: move the 4 functions to @krn/db mappers (or a CLI decode module) and rename to buildTargetEvidence, buildSourceUsefulnessOutcomes, buildPatternUsefulnessOutcomes, buildActivationRetrievalDiagnostics operating on validated input. Update callers (runShowReadback.ts, reviewDomain.test.ts, evidenceBundle.test.ts, krnBehaviorGate.ts). Keep the domain TYPES in core; only deserialization moves. Do NOT move the runShowReadback-local FromMetadata funcs (projectResolutionFromMetadata etc.) yet - those move with the DecisionPacket naming decision (D2).

Non-goals: do not change metadata schema or keys (that is a migration); do not unify the feedback fork here (that is 9xc1).
acceptance_criteria: grep for FromMetadata under packages/core/src returns ZERO; the builders live in the decode layer on validated input; all callers updated; pnpm typecheck + pnpm test green; Fallow reports no orphaned imports.
notes:
Unblocks 9xc1 and D2. Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
RE-SCOPE (session 2026-07-06): folded into mise-en-palace-9xc1. The 3 core FromMetadata functions (sourceUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata, patternUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata, targetEvidenceFromMetadata) are cohesive with their core-local helpers (sourceUsefulnessOutcomeField, normalizeTargetEvidence, targetChangedFilesField) and patternUsefulnessOutcomesFromMetadata is exactly what 9xc1 rewrites anyway. Moving them separately would double-touch + invert layering. The FromMetadata rename will happen as part of 9xc1 when it reshapes the decoder. Closed-as-folded; no standalone work.
close_reason: Folded into 9xc1 (see notes): standalone FromMetadata move would double-touch code 9xc1 rewrites and drag core-local helpers. Rename lands with 9xc1.

title: Decide outbox substrate: wire a consumer OR delete it
description:
Why: DrizzleOutboxRepository (enqueue + listPending only) and DrizzleEventLedgerRepository (appendRunEvent) appear to be write-only primitives with no runtime consumer. If nothing drains the outbox, it is speculative surface violating the roadmap rule: no subsystem without a runtime consumer.

Scope: audit every enqueue / listPending / appendRunEvent call site (grep for listPending, enqueue, outbox, appendRunEvent under packages, excluding schema and tests). If a real consumer exists, document it. If none exists, delete DrizzleOutboxRepository (and DrizzleEventLedgerRepository if likewise write-only), the table schema, and the migration that adds the table, after confirming nothing reads them. This is evidence-driven: the answer follows from the call-site audit, not a product preference.

Non-goals: do not build a worker daemon to drain the outbox (roadmap defers the maintenance runtime to P6).
acceptance_criteria: Either the outbox has a documented runtime consumer; or DrizzleOutboxRepository and its table are deleted with typecheck + test green and no dangling references. No write-only primitive remains.
notes: Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: No-op after evidence: the outbox is NOT dead. DrizzleHarnessRunRepository inserts outbox_events in-transaction with writes; doctorStaticChecks reads it; smokes count by feedbackDeltaId. It is a live transactional event log. Only listPending lacks a product drainer, which is intentional (deferred to P6 maintenance runtime). Deleting it would break feedback/harness-run event emission. No code change warranted.

title: Wire observationPrefix into the Codex brief OR remove it as dead surface
description:

This is half-built surface (compute + gate + persist + never render). Either observations govern Codex behavior or they are dead weight on the assembly type.

Scope: (a) Decide whether observations should reach Codex (read KRN_ROADMAP.md Layer 1 intent; ask operator if ambiguous). (b) If YES: wire contextAssembly.observationPrefix into renderExecutionBrief as a new brief section, add it to contracts.ts required sections if mandatory, add a decision-packet eval falsifier case. (c) If NO: remove ContextObservationPrefix types from contextAssembly.ts, remove the gate in assembleContext.ts, delete the observationPrefix assembly path. Either branch removes the half-built state.

acceptance_criteria: Either observationPrefix appears in createExecutionBrief output AND contracts.ts required sections AND at least one decision-packet eval fixture; OR ContextObservationPrefix types and the assembleContext gate are deleted. No computed-but-unused state remains. pnpm typecheck + decision-packet eval green.
notes: Source: kernel-direction-full-audit.
close_reason: Completed branch YES: observationPrefix now appears in ExecutionBrief output, contracts.ts required section profile, rendered Codex brief text, adapter unit coverage, and the decision-packet eval fixture/engine path via observationPrefixCount. title: Move brain usefulness feedback from JSON corpus to store-backed events
description: Why: usefulness feedback is runtime/event evidence, not a permanent JSON ledger. Current cleanup removed active usefulness-feedback files from corpus. Scope: design or reuse DB/event tables for pattern usefulness feedback, query it through read models, and keep corpus JSON as bootstrap fixtures only. Acceptance: brain knowledge readback can show usefulness outcome from store-backed events; no docs or static JSON ledger is required for current usefulness; tests prove no-feedback and helped-feedback paths.
notes:
RE-SCOPE (kernel-direction-full-audit, 2026-07-06): the revert was for execution defects (alias-only rename, missing tests, hardcoded slugs, undocumented outcome semantics), NOT wrong direction. The fork is real and this remains the highest-value fix. Re-attempt with these refinements: (1) BrainKnowledgeUsefulnessFeedback becomes a READ MODEL over FeedbackDelta store events, not a parallel JSON structure - same type, same store path; corpus/brain-knowledge JSON becomes seed-only. (2) PROVE THE READ SIDE: memory_feedback_events and observation_feedback_events are currently write-only in product code (inserted, never read by a read model) - this slice must implement the read model that reads usefulness from those events, not just add more writes. (3) feedback ingestion must join on ActivationTrace (retrievalRunId / contextAssemblyId) so "did the included standard help" is answerable. (4) Tests for helped / no-feedback / unused / stale paths. (5) Document outcome-value semantics (7 values today: selected|used|helped|neutral|noise|stale|unknown, all funnel through one field). (6) No hardcoded workspaceSlug / projectSlug. PRECONDITIONS: land C2 (slug consolidation = mise-en-palace-48f9) and C3 (FromMetadata relocation = mise-en-palace-is6c) first so the unification is real and does not re-introduce the reverted defects. Dependencies wired: 9xc1 now blocked-by 48f9 and is6c.
DESIGN LOCK (session 2026-07-06, post-investigation):
Two usefulness concepts today: (1) feedback-delta usefulness in feedback_delta.metadata JSON (run-show path, ALREADY store-backed); (2) brain-knowledge usefulness read from CORPUS JSON by brain-knowledge-read-model.ts:443.
GAP = #2: brain-knowledge pattern usefulness must be read from the STORE (feedback_delta records carrying patternUsefulnessOutcomes), not corpus JSON; corpus becomes seed-only.
KEY DECISION NEEDED: align the enums - SourceUsefulnessOutcome (7: selected|used|helped|neutral|noise|stale|unknown) vs memoryApplicationOutcome (4: helped|hurt|neutral|stale). This is the exact semantic gap that caused the prior revert. Recommend: document the 7->4 mapping explicitly OR extend memoryApplicationOutcome to match, with a per-outcome feedback-event handler.
Implementation shape: (a) give brain-knowledge-read-model a feedback-repository dependency to query feedback_deltas by patternId; (b) build usefulness readback from store records; (c) corpus JSON -> seed-only; (d) falsifier tests for no-feedback/helped/unused/stale; (e) run second-opinion-claude (CLAUDE.md mandates for migration slices).
Preconditions already met: C2 slug consolidation done (commit e9b68a3d); run-readback split (commit 1674dba3) isolates the decoders this touches.
close_reason: Completed: brain knowledge usefulness feedback now has a store-backed read path. Added krn brain knowledge --store-only, reading MemoryRecord cards from DB and pattern usefulness from feedback_deltas.metadata.patternUsefulnessOutcomes; explicit file/seed previews can intentionally merge current store feedback by stable pattern:<patternId>. Added DrizzleHarnessRunRepository.listFeedbackDeltasForProject(project-scoped through feedback -> review -> evidence -> execution -> plan -> task), exposed via DatabaseRuntime. Verified: pnpm typecheck; @krn/cli typecheck:tests:clean; focused parse-knowledge and brain tests; DB harness repository test; pnpm quality:fallow:ci; git diff --check; live DB store-only readback source=memory_store usefulnessSource=store_backed. second-opinion-claude first verdict approve_with_fixes MEDIUM; accepted evidence-gap by adding explicit file+DB merge test, rejected source-aware no-merge proposal because pattern:<patternId> is the intended identity, filed follow-up mise-en-palace-s2wm for live project-scoping regression; second review timed out and produced error_timeout only, no verdict.

title: Harden smoke createId uniqueness across both DB smokes
description:
Why this exists:
The session review flagged a latent przypał: createId in runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke is ${prefix}-${smokeId} and is shared across the 6 recall passes, so the task/intent ids handed to runSourceSearchCommand collide. Harmless today (retrieveActivationCandidates is read-only) but a landmine if source-search ever persists. The same pattern exists in runBrainSearchDbSmoke. The project bar is zero przypałów.

Scope:
- Make createId produce unique ids per call in both smokes (e.g., fold in a monotonic counter or the decision.id / phase), so task/intent ids never collide across passes.
- Keep determinism of marker cleanup (which keys on smokeId/source, not id values).
- Both smokes still pass reproducibly.

Acceptance criteria:
- createId returns distinct values across all calls within a smoke run.
- Both smokes pass reproducibly (3/3 real-recall; brain-search green).
- No test asserts a specific id string value that would now break.

Verification:
- pnpm db:smoke:real-recall-advantage (3/3, twice)
- pnpm db:smoke:brain-search
- pnpm --filter @krn/cli test -- db.test
- pnpm run typecheck
- pnpm -w run quality:fallow:ci
- git diff --check

Proof/non-proof:
Proves the smokes have no latent id-collision. Does not change proof semantics.

Rejected directions:
No UUID generation (needs randomness/determinism), no changing the seeded claim id format if avoidable.
close_reason: Completed: closed the latent id-collision przypal from the session review. Added createUniqueSmokeCreateId(smokeId) to smokeRuntimeCleanup.ts - a counter-based createId factory that returns ${prefix}-${smokeId}-${counter++}, so every generated id is unique per call. Replaced the non-unique ${prefix}-${smokeId} createId in runRealRecallAdvantageDbSmoke (inline) and runBrainSearchDbSmoke (local createSmokeId helper) with the shared factory. Counter is deterministic under sequential code; unique across concurrent recall passes that share one closure. Marker cleanup/count unaffected (key on smokeId/source, not id values). Both smokes still pass reproducibly: real-recall 3/3 (run twice), brain-search green. title: Live dogfood at scale: brain informs a real implementation task
description:

This slice records a fuller live dogfood: while implementing a real repo task (the adopt --link command from the sibling bead), query the brain (krn source search + krn source decision gaps) BEFORE and DURING implementation, and document which governing decisions surfaced and how they shaped the work.

Scope:

Proves the brain can inform real implementation work via its own CLI on a real task. Does not prove live Codex adherence, broad advantage, or that every task benefits.

description:

title: Reject non-ISO ExecutionRun lifecycle timestamps
description:
## What To Build

Parse lifecycle startedAt and completedAt with the canonical strict ISO timestamp boundary before converting them for persistence.

## Priority

P3 — current validation accepts implementation-dependent JavaScript date strings even though the contract and errors claim ISO timestamps.

## Exact Current-Code Evidence

requireValidTimestamp in drizzle-harness-run-repository.ts uses new Date and rejects only NaN. JavaScript accepts multiple non-ISO formats and normalizes them before storage. Existing core timestamp parsing already exposes a strict ISO predicate.

## Steps to Reproduce

Pass a JavaScript-parseable non-ISO date string as startedAt during creation or transition. Observe that lifecycle validation accepts and normalizes it instead of rejecting at the repository boundary.

## Mechanism

Use the shared unknown-first ISO timestamp predicate, then convert exactly once for storage. Keep error wording and accepted runtime type aligned.

## Violated Invariant

External lifecycle timestamps are strict ISO values before they enter the temporal domain model.

## Runtime Consumer

ExecutionRun ordering, timestamp coherence checks, event audit, DecisionPacket identity diagnostics, and API callers.

## Falsifier

A non-ISO but JavaScript-parseable timestamp is accepted by createExecutionRun or updateExecutionRunStatus.

## Reproduction Command

Run focused lifecycle parser and repository tests with accepted ISO, malformed, and implementation-dependent date formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

Only canonical ISO timestamps pass lifecycle creation and transition validation; valid existing ISO callers remain unchanged.

## Required Verification

Focused Node-22 tests, root typecheck, Fallow changed-files gate, and diff check.

## Proves

Lifecycle timestamp syntax is deterministic at the repository boundary.

## Does Not Prove

It does not prove provider clock accuracy, external work timing, or semantic ordering beyond existing transition checks.

## Rollback / Contraction

Reject ambiguous formats rather than adding parser aliases or compatibility shims.

## Affected Files / Packages

DB lifecycle validation and focused tests, with reuse of the existing core timestamp predicate.

## Native Dependency Edges

Discovered by independent review mise-en-palace-md7u.149. Direct terminal timestamp projection remains owned by mise-en-palace-md7u.198.

## Human / Provider Authority

No human or provider authority.

## Required Skills
diagnosing-bugs,krn-implementation,code-review
design: Reuse one strict ISO parser at the external data boundary; do not normalize ambiguous timestamp aliases.
acceptance_criteria: Non-ISO parseable dates reject while canonical ISO timestamps preserve current lifecycle behavior.
notes: Completed in commit 057d6be2a8fee8130f0291ed7da33bdade64aa49. Red falsifier showed JavaScript-parseable July 13, 2026 timestamps passed lifecycle validation and failed only later in fake persistence. Production now requires the existing core isIsoTimestamp predicate before exactly one Date conversion for both startedAt and completedAt. Verification: focused red/green test, repository file 18 passed with 8 configured-store tests skipped in the unconfigured run, configured PostgreSQL DB package 34 files / 186 tests, DB package and root typechecks, diff-check, fixed-point Standards/Spec review no findings, exact-range Fallow no findings, exact-SHA CI 29492413534 all four jobs successful. Required krn-implementation skill was unavailable; global implement workflow was used. Does not prove clock accuracy or lifecycle ordering beyond existing checks.
close_reason: ExecutionRun lifecycle rejects JavaScript-parseable non-ISO startedAt and completedAt values at the repository boundary.

title: Recall-quality: investigate why governing decisions rank below lexically-stronger peers
description: Seed for later. close_reason: Investigated, no safe clean win - closed by evidence. Empirical finding: for the dashboard query, ALL included candidates tie at totalScore=95 (lexicalScore=40, graphScore=25). The bounded-loop governing decision ranks last purely due to arbitrary tie-break (DB row order), NOT because it is less relevant. The candidates are genuinely tied. Forcing rank-1 via a subjective tiebreak (raw lexical hit count, confidence, etc.) would be fixture-fitting, not senior, and risks breaking slice 2's distractor-competition proof (which relies on the current score composition where high-confidence governing beats low-confidence distractor). The real recall gap was the missing-edge blindness (fixed in slices 4/5), not ranking quality. Recall works: the governing decision IS surfaced in top-k. Rank-position for genuinely-tied candidates is not a defect. No code change shipped. Honest outcome: investigated, ranking is defensible as-is.

title: Add reviewed merge and refresh consolidation candidates
description: Why: current consolidation handles stale/harmful memory via anti-memory invalidation; Bobbin-level maintenance also needs duplicate merge, refresh, supersession, and demotion proposals without silent truth mutation. Scope: define the smallest typed candidate model and reviewed application path for merge/refresh/supersession after the anti-memory path is proven. Acceptance: duplicate or superseded memory can be proposed for merge/refresh, reviewer accepts or rejects it, and later activation/readback explains the retained, superseded, or refreshed state. Dependencies: live DB consolidation proof should land first unless a smaller typed-only slice is explicitly justified. Falsifier: code mutates MemoryRecord truth directly from preview/maintenance without review gate evidence.
notes: Completed bounded typed slice for reviewed memory revision. Added MemoryRepository.supersedeMemoryRecord and Drizzle implementation using existing memory_records.status=superseded plus supersessionReview metadata and outbox event; no migration. Added harness flow: proposeMemoryRevision creates a MemoryCandidate + MemoryFeedbackEvent from a reviewed draft; applyReviewedMemoryRevision promotes the accepted candidate and supersedes the source MemoryRecord; rejectMemoryRevision routes rejection through rejectMemoryCandidate. Focused behavior test proves: no evidence means no writes; reviewed refresh promotes replacement, supersedes old memory, and later activation includes replacement while excluding old memory as superseded; reviewed merge proposal can be rejected. Verification: pnpm --filter @krn/harness test -- memory-consolidation; pnpm --filter @krn/db test -- drizzle-memory-repository; pnpm --filter @krn/harness typecheck; pnpm --filter @krn/db typecheck; pnpm typecheck; pnpm quality:fallow; pnpm --filter @krn/db db:check; git diff --check. Non-proof: no live DB smoke for merge/refresh yet; no autonomous maintenance runtime.
close_reason: Completed: reviewed memory revision path now supports accept/reject, replacement promotion, and source MemoryRecord supersession without preview-time truth mutation.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: consolidation and memory maintenance

Non-goals: no autonomous daemon until a named loop needs execution, no magical dreaming vocabulary without consumer proof.

title: Bobbin-level tracker: temporal consensus at scale
description: Why: Bobbin-level memory is not recall; it must explain how truth changed over time and why newer text is not automatically authoritative. Scope: after source governance and ingest proof, build consensus/conflict readbacks over temporal claims, relation edges, supersession, dissent, missing evidence, and author/source authority. Acceptance: KRN can answer a temporal why/when/what-changed question from stored claims and raw evidence spans; rejected/superseded claims remain citable history, not active authority; falsifier catches newer-but-weaker claims outranking stronger current consensus. Dependencies: Phase 5 temporal consensus, large corpus evidence ingest. Non-goals: no decorative GraphRAG layer, no consensus without citations.
close_reason: Completed: SourceConsensusTimeline now carries raw evidence citation refs/source ranges, keeps rejected and superseded claims as historical/rejected readback, and demotes newer weaker accepted claims behind stronger valid current consensus. Falsifier added for newer hypothesis with decision edge failing to outrank project-decision consensus. Gates: core source test, core typecheck, package typechecks, full pnpm test, pnpm quality:fallow, git diff --check.
